title: Constrainahedra
abstractText: We define a family of convex polytopes called constrainahedra , which index collisions of horizontal and vertical lines. Our construction proceeds by first defining a poset C ( m , n ) of good rectangular preorders , then proving that C ( m , n ) is a lattice, and finally constructing a polytopal realization by taking the convex hull of a certain explicitly-defined collection of points. The constrainahedra will form the combinatorial backbone of the second author’s construction of strong homotopy duoids . We indicate how constrainahedra could be realized as Gromov-compactified configuration spaces of horizontal and vertical lines; viewed from this perspective, the constrainahedra include naturally into the first author’s notion of 2-associahedra.

title: The burden of disease for children diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome — a European cohort study
abstractText: Background Klinefelter syndrome is a congenital chromosomal anomaly, where males have an extra X-chromosome. The syndrome may be associated with hypergonadotropic hypogonadism and many are late or undiagnosed. This European, population-based data-linkage cohort study was part of the EUROlinkCAT project and investigated the burden of disease for the first ten years of life for European children diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome. Results Thirteen national and regional population-based registries in ten countries from the European surveillance of congenital anomalies (EUROCAT) network participated. Data for live born children born in 1995-2014 and diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome prenatally or during infancy were linked to mortality and hospital records. Data for liveborn children born with any congenital anomaly and children without a congenital anomaly (reference children) were included for comparison on morbidity. Out of 5.8 million live born children 278 were diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome in the 13 registry areas, 96.8% survived the first 5 year of life, 64.7% (95% CI 51.8;75.0) were admitted to hospital during the first year with a median length of stay of 3.9 (95% CI 3.0;4.7) days, 10.8% (95% CI 6.9;16.4) had a hospital stay of ≥10 days and 12.3% (95% CI 7.1;18.9) underwent surgery. In the age group 1-4 years of age 53.5% (95% CI 41.2;64.4) were admitted to hospital, the median length of stay decreased to 0.7 (95% CI 0.3;1.1) days and 6.3% (95% CI 2.6;12.3) had a hospital stay of ≥ 10 days. Conclusions More children diagnosed prenatally or in infancy with Klinefelter syndrome were hospitalised and underwent more surgery compared to reference children, while less were hospitalised and fewer had surgery than all children with any other congenital anomaly. Thus, the burden of disease was increased for children diagnosed prenatally or in infancy with Klinefelter syndrome but decreased overall after the first year of life.

title: Sustaining democracy under the shadow of force
abstractText: Democracy faces two threats: incumbents may peacefully monopolize office, or political factions may seek power through violent conflict. Using a dynamic model, the authors examine some conditions under which democracy is sustainable against both threats. Two parties vie for office under the shadow of force. To resolve conflict, the incumbent can share revenue as well as hold competitive elections: each time, it chooses the probability of losing the next election and redistributes revenue. Elections enable the incumbent to concede control over revenue over time but come with regular risks of defeat. Democracy is sustainable if the economic stakes in elections are neither too low nor too high, while the military strength is sufficiently balanced between the two parties. When the stakes are high, democracy may be sustained only with civilian control of the military or programmatic transfers.

title: High-Quality Cu Metallization of Ceramics via Cold Spray Enabled by Ti or Cu-Ti Buffer Layer
A conserved region T cell vaccine for Sarbecoviruses
abstractText: SARS-CoV-2, the virus responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic, was first detected in Wuhan, China, in late 2019. It is a Sarbecovirus and a member of the Betacoronavirus genus. Effective vaccines based on the viral spike protein were available by late 2020. SARS-CoV-2 has continued to evolve in the human population, accruing neutralizing antibody resistance mutations that necessitate the vaccine be periodically updated to better match contemporary variants. Neutralizing antibody cross-reactivity is also limited among Betacoronavirus genus that are of clinical importance in people. We present an alternative vaccine strategy based on eliciting T cell responses targeting 4 highly conserved regions shared across Betacoronavirus , with the hypothesis that cross-reactive responses to these regions could temper disease severity should a novel Betacoronavirus enter the human population. Vaccination induced robust T cell responses in mice and rhesus macaques. Vaccinated hamsters were significantly protected against weight loss and lung inflammation after challenge with the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant. After a SARS-CoV-2 Delta challenge in rhesus macaques, 3 of 4 animals in the control group had infectious virus in their bronchoalveolar lavage samples, while the 4 animals in the vaccinated group did not.

title: The Wild Number of an Edge-Colored Graph
Nomogram for predicting early neurological deterioration in anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke patients treated with mechanical thrombectomy
abstractText: Background The importance of early detection of patients at risk of early neurological deterioration (END) after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) at the time of prognosis provision is paramount. Methods This retrospective study not only sought to determine the predictive variables of post-MT END but also created a prognostic model in the form of a nomogram. A predictive model based on END occurrence (≥ 4 points of NIHSS score increase or death) within 72 hours after the event was created through multivariate logistic regression analysis of the possible risk factors. Results Total that 161 AIS patients undergoing MT were gathered as training cohort and 69 as validation cohort. Multivariate analysis revealed three independent predictors: atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) (OR = 1.239, 95% CI: 1.015–1.513, P = 0.035), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII)(OR = 1.086, 95% CI: 1.007–1.172, P = 0.032), and smoking history(OR = 2.558, 95% CI: 1.030–6.348, P = 0.043). The predictive model based on the three variables achieved an AUC of 0.842 (95% CI: 0.763–0.922), with its calibration curve nearly aligning with the ideal diagonal. Conclusions These results showed that the nomogram has a strong discriminative ability and calibration level, which suggests that it can be used as a viable clinical tool to predict END among acute stroke patients with ischemia and who receive MT.

title: Three-dimensional modelling of serrated trailing-edge noise based on the Wiener–Hopf technique
abstractText: In this paper, a semi-analytical model based on the Wiener–Hopf technique is developed to predict the turbulent boundary layer trailing-edge noise from serrated edges, aiming to account for the correct three-dimensional noise source and propagation effects while retaining high computational efficiency. The scattered surface pressure over a semi-infinite flat plate is first obtained using the Green’s function developed for the acoustic scattering by a serrated edge. The radiation integral over a flat plate of a finite size is subsequently performed to obtain the far-field noise using Amiet’s approach. The model is then compared against the earlier two-dimensional Wiener–Hopf model, and experimental and numerical results. The predicted far-field spectra exhibit close agreement with the two-dimensional Wiener–Hopf-based model using a proper scaling coefficient dependent on the observer distance r r $r$ , but show overpredictions when compared with experimental and numerical noise reduction spectra. However, unlike the two-dimensional model, the present model successfully captures the three-dimensional characteristics. It reproduces the correct 1 divided by r squared 1 / r 2 $1/r^{2}$ decay of the sound-pressure power spectral density, exhibits the correct dipolar behaviour with vanishing emission at upstream angles, and captures the additional directivity lobes associated with the finite span and chord of the flat plate. In addition, it enables the prediction of a full three-dimensional directivity pattern. Compared with existing three-dimensional models, the present model based on the Wiener–Hopf technique reduces the computational cost by approximately two orders of magnitude. It is hoped that such a model may be used to enable an efficient numerical optimisation of the serration geometry in realistic applications.

title: A method for determining contact parameters in discrete element modeling: application to masonry pagodas
abstractText: The discrete element method (DEM) is an effective approach for simulating seismic cracking and damage processes in ancient masonry pagodas. Accurate representation of masonry behavior and dynamic fracture characteristics requires a reasonable determination of contact parameters between block elements. To address this, a contact parameter selection method for the model based on the physical properties of materials ( α p method) is proposed, incorporating mechanical property tests of masonry under different stress states and referring to the shaking table test results of the Xuanzang Pagoda model in China. It is applied to analyze block interface shear displacements, displacement time histories at monitoring points, and peak displacements of the pagoda model under different seismic conditions. The numerical results are compared with both the elastic theory-based method ( α e method) and experimental measurements. Findings indicate that the α p method provides a more reasonable simulation of the dynamic effects of the pagoda model and the dynamic transmission behavior of the internal infill. Under strong seismic excitation, the error between the predicted dynamic response of the pagoda and the shaking table test results is only 16.3%, which is reduced by 50% compared with the α e method. This approach more effectively captures material deformation and the typical characteristics of seismic damage evolution in pagodas. This research offers a useful reference for discrete element simulations of failure modes and seismic mechanisms in historic masonry structures.

title: Is psychomotor retardation associated with treatment response in adults with depression? A secondary analysis of nine randomized controlled trials
abstractText: Background Psychomotor retardation is characterized by slowed motor and cognitive processes. Although associated with greater illness severity in depression, its relationship with treatment response is unclear. We examined whether psychomotor retardation is associated with treatment outcomes in depression. Methods We conducted a secondary analysis of individual participant data from nine randomized controlled trials of pharmacological, psychological, and exercise-based treatments for unipolar depression in primary care (Dep-GP). Self-reported psychomotor retardation was assessed at baseline using the Revised Clinical Interview Schedule. The primary outcome was the standardized z -score of each trial’s validated self-report depression measure at 3–4 months post-randomization; the secondary outcome was remission. Within-study regression models were adjusted for established prognostic factors, with secondary analyses additionally adjusting for baseline core depressive symptoms and depression severity. Effect estimates were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. Results Among 4,290 participants, 2,754 (64.2%) reported psychomotor retardation. Psychomotor retardation was associated with greater depression severity at follow-up (pooled z -score = 0.184, 95% CI [0.059, 0.309], p = 0.004, I 2 = 68.7%) and lower odds of remission (pooled OR = 0.737, 95% CI [0.577, 0.941], p = 0.015, I 2 = 57.7%), adjusting for age, sex, ethnicity, marital status, employment status and allocated treatment. Findings were robust to adjustment for baseline core depressive symptoms but not after adjustment for full baseline severity. Conclusions Psychomotor retardation is associated with poorer treatment outcomes in depression, though this may reflect underlying severity. Recognition of psychomotor retardation may help identify patients at risk of poorer response and inform clinical management.

title: An Extended Two-Step Method for Inverse Singular Value Problems
abstractText: In this paper we investigate numerical solutions for inverse singular value problems (ISVPs) arising in various applications. We propose an extended two-step method for solving the ISVPs with zero singular values. Our algorithm eliminates the need for Cayley transformations and consequently avoids solving \(2(m+n)\) linear systems during the computation of approximate singular vectors at each outer iteration. Under the assumption that the Jacobian matrix at the initial point is nonsingular, we present a convergence analysis for the proposed algorithm and prove a cubic root-convergence rate. Numerical experiments are conducted to validate that the extended two-step method is an efficient algorithm for the ISVPs even when zero singular values appear. Our extended method and convergence result improve and/or extend the existing ones for solving the ISVP. As a byproduct, we also fill the gap in the convergence analysis of [W. Ma, Appl. Math. 71 (2026)].

title: Tissue-specific effects of in ovo prebiotic stimulation on cytokine gene expression in broiler chickens
abstractText: The modulation of the immune system during the early life of broiler chickens has been shown to have a beneficial effect on disease resistance and overall health. The present study investigated the effects of in ovo administration of xylo- and mannooligosaccharides (XOS and MOS) on cytokine gene expression in two immune-relevant tissues: the spleen and cecal tonsils. The injection of fertilized eggs was conducted on embryonic day 12, with the substances xylotriose (XOS3), xylotetraose (XOS4), mannotriose (MOS3), mannotetraose (MOS4), or saline (control) utilised for this purpose. The gene expression of cytokines representing general immune regulation (IL1β, IL2, IL10), Th1 (IL8, IL12, IFNβ, IFNγ), Th2 (IL4, IL6), and Th17 (IL17) pathways was quantified in 42-day-old birds using RT-qPCR. A significant immunomodulatory effect was observed in the spleen, where XOS3 consistently increased the expression of cytokines associated with Th1-, Th2-, and Th17-mediated responses, indicating enhanced systemic immune activation. Conversely, no statistically significant differences were detected in the cecal tonsils, although numerical variation was present. This muted mucosal response is likely to reflect the inherent heterogeneity and tolerance-oriented function of gut-associated lymphoid tissue, consistent with the concept of acquired immunotolerance to commensal microbiota. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that in ovo prebiotic stimulation exerts tissue-specific effects, promoting systemic immune readiness while maintaining mucosal homeostasis, and highlight XOS3 as a particularly effective modulator of splenic cytokine expression in broiler chickens.

title: Adaptation of Brief Resilient Coping Scale (BRCS) to Brazilian Portuguese
abstractText: This study aimed to adapt and validate the Brief Resilient Coping Scale (BRCS) for a sample of Brazilian adults. The adaptation process included translation and expert analysis using the three-stage Delphi technique. A total of 698 Brazilian adults, with a mean age of 48.4 years ( SD = 15.3), of whom 79% were women, completed the BRCS. To examine construct validity, confirmatory factor analyses and correlation analyses with indicators of depression, anxiety, and stress were conducted. The one-dimensional theoretical model demonstrated good fit (CFI = .998, TLI = .994, RMSEA = .058 [.017, .107], SRMR = .023), albeit not perfect, χ 2 (2) = 7.177, p = .028. The factor loadings were all above .30, varying from .62 to .82. The correlations between BRCS and the DASS-8 subscales were significant with p < .001 and r = -.31 for the correlation with depression, -.28 for anxiety and -.26 for stress. In comparison to previous studies of validity evidence of BRCS, our results presented the best values indicating suitability for Brazilian context. For that, we consider the BRCS to be a valid and reliable instrument for assessing resilient coping in the Brazilian population.

title: Shear-induced self-diffusivity in dilute suspensions with repulsive interactions
abstractText: In a dilute non-Brownian suspension undergoing simple shear, pairwise hydrodynamic interactions are fore–aft symmetric at zero Reynolds number and produce no net cross-streamline displacement. A weak central repulsive force between particles breaks this symmetry, deflecting trajectories and generating irreversible transverse displacements that cumulatively yield a shear-induced self-diffusivity. We derive, via matched asymptotic expansions in the limit of weak repulsion, closed-form scaling laws for the gradient and vorticity components of this diffusivity. The gradient component exhibits a logarithmic enhancement relative to the vorticity component, a structural anisotropy that persists for all monotonically decaying repulsive potentials. The specific interaction enters only through integral functionals of the force profile weighted by hydrodynamic mobility functions, establishing that the scaling is universal across physically distinct mechanisms, such as electrical double-layer repulsion, steric interactions or any other short-range central force. We validate the asymptotic predictions against full numerical trajectory integration for two representative cases: (i) electrostatic repulsion, modelled using the Gouy–Chapman description of the electrical double layer, and (ii) particle roughness, modelled using the Hertz contact force, and find excellent agreement in the expected regime.

title: Solar Orbiter observations of solar energetic electron events associated with hard microflares
abstractText: Generally, large solar flares accelerate electrons to high energies more efficiently than microflares. However, there are microflares, known as hard microflares (HMFs), which also produce high-energy electrons, as evidenced by their flat hard X-ray (HXR) spectra. These events are characterised by a footpoint rooted in or at the edge of a sunspot. The mechanisms underlying this efficient acceleration and their connection to solar energetic electrons (SEEs) are not yet understood. We aim to compare, for the first time, the HXR spectra of HMFs with in situ electron spectra of associated SEEs. For this purpose, we used observations from Solar Orbiter STIX and EPD instruments, respectively. This approach is set to provide new insights into the acceleration processes and how these high-energy electrons access interplanetary space. We found eight HMFs (of GOES C class or lower), jointly observed by Solar Orbiter and Earth-bound observatories, associated with SEEs. This association was verified through timing and magnetic-connectivity analysis. Each event was analysed through STIX HXR spectroscopy, SEE velocity-dispersion analysis, and in situ electron spectral analysis of EPD data. Seven out of eight SEE events show consistent timing between HXR emission from the flare and estimated electron injection into interplanetary space. They also exhibit good agreement between the flare location and the estimated magnetic connectivity to the Sun. When compared with correlation between HXR photon and in situ electron spectral indices established by previous studies, our HMFs tend to populate the hard end of the distribution, even though these previous studies include larger C- and M-class flares. This demonstrates, also through in situ observations, that HMFs efficiently accelerate electrons to high energies and efficient acceleration does not necessarily require large flare energy release. We conclude that HMFs produce prompt SEEs with hard spectral properties, consistent with their hard HXR spectra. This indicates efficient electron acceleration to high energies. The magnetic morphology in HMFs, which involves open field lines from the sunspot, suggests that these events may be an important contributor to filling the heliosphere with energetic particles.

title: A Zwitterionic Polymeric Quaternary Ammonium Microparticle (Z-pQAM) as a Candidate Wound Dressing with Simultaneous Procoagulant, Antimicrobial, and Wound-Healing Activities
abstractText: Wound infection, inadequate local hemostasis, and delayed healing remain major complications following surgery and in chronic wounds. Effective wound management requires materials that simultaneously prevent infection, support hemostasis, promote tissue repair, and maintain biocompatibility. Here, we synthesized a zwitterionic polymeric quaternary ammonium microparticle (Z-pQAM) and evaluated its biocompatibility, in vitro antimicrobial and procoagulant activity, and wound-healing effects. FTIR confirmed stepwise synthesis and quaternization, and zeta potential analysis showed that Z-pQAM retains a net-negative bulk surface charge across physiological pH. In vitro degradation studies in PBS showed that Z-pQAM retained >99% of its dry mass after three weeks, indicating slow, physiologically appropriate hydrolytic degradation. Functional assays are in line with the hypothesis that its procoagulant and antibacterial activity arise from locally accessible quaternary ammonium (QA+) microdomains rather than overall surface positivity. Z-pQAM achieved >7-log10 reduction against S. aureus and E. coli, and >5-log10 reduction against MRSA at 200 mg/mL, with Live/Dead staining confirming bactericidal membrane disruption, while maintaining <0.5% hemolysis and 100% cell viability across the tested concentration range. In recalcified whole blood, Z-pQAM achieved a blood clotting index of 36.5%, comparable to a benchmark FDA-cleared hemostatic powder. In an uninfected murine full-thickness excisional wound model, topical Z-pQAM accelerated closure at day 8 without altering epidermal thickness, reduced CD45+ inflammatory infiltration by >50% at day 3, and enhanced collagen deposition by day 12. Collectively, these findings position Z-pQAM as a promising candidate for a multifunctional topical wound dressing, combining antibacterial and procoagulant activity with biocompatibility and support for wound repair.

title: Statistical tests should inform behaviour in theory and practice
abstractText: Objectives Statistical hypothesis testing cannot establish a hypothesis as certainly—or even approximately—true, but it is valuable in guiding behaviour as if it were true. To make decisions in theory and practice, statistical testing in psychology should weigh the Type I (α) and Type II (β) error probabilities according to their respective costs . Methods We outline costs and how to approach the α-β balance for six common decision-making questions: (1) Should a hypothesis be considered tentatively accepted? (2) Should a model or theory cover a newly proposed effect? (3) Should a new hypothesis be proposed? (4) Should a new intervention be introduced? (5) Are the psychometric properties of an instrument sufficient to use it? (6) Are the assumptions of a statistical method met so that it may be used? We give a worked example with real cost figures for question (4). Results We argue that parsimony—prioritizing low α over low β—often serves as a useful default stance in questions (1) to (5). This resembles the general preference for focusing on fewer, larger and more robust effects to allocate resources efficiently and to make scientific communication more reliable. Conclusions The parsimony default invites transparent counterarguments to override it, justifying a preference for small β. Examples include adding promising intervention components with little risk of adverse effects to well-established interventions. As with (6), statistical tests can sometimes introduce unnecessary errors when a sound decision can be made on substantive grounds alone, for example when setting up a model to test a given hypothesis.

title: Apparent Power as a Unifying Metric for Frontal Polymerization
abstractText: In self-sustained transformations such as frontal polymerization, the balance between power generated and power transfer governs propagation dynamics. Herein, we demonstrate the use of an experimentally practical apparent power expression to characterize frontal polymerization. We validated our expression by frontally polymerizing 1,5-cyclooctadiene, dicyclopentadiene, and 5-ethylidene-2-norbornene at various initiator loadings, finding a strong correlation between apparent power and reaction propagation. Raising a system’s apparent power drove a progressive transition in the observed front regime, from quenched through unstable to uniform. We further demonstrated that modulating apparent power influences backbone isomerization and polymer morphology. To further validate our expression, we used heat sinks to vary the reaction power, linking distinct front regimes with apparent power values. Geometric normalization extended this framework to literature examples and frontal radical polymerization, allowing for meaningful comparisons across variable reaction systems and mechanisms. This analytical tool offers a more holistic comparison of monomers and reaction mechanisms that otherwise differ in their thermodynamics and kinetics.

title: DMT-induced aberrant salience and suggestibility correlate with mystical experiences and positive emotionality
abstractText: Paradoxically, psychedelics have long been used as models of both psychosis and therapy. After proposing mystical experiences as a link between these models for lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), we aimed to extend and refine this framework for N,N -Dimethyltryptamine (DMT). In a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, crossover study, 25 healthy participants received DMT (60mg) and an active placebo (0.6mg DMT), separated by two hours. Psychotic-like experiences were assessed via aberrant salience (Aberrant Salience Inventory [ASI]) and therapeutic-like experiences via suggestibility (Creative Imagination Scale [CIS]), including suggestion-induced mystical experiences. Psychedelic experiences were measured via the Six Dimensions and Eleven Factors of Altered States of Consciousness Questionnaire (6D-ASC and 11-ASC), Hallucinogen Rating Scale (HRS), and Mystical Experiences Questionnaire (MEQ). Compared to placebo, DMT increased all aberrant salience factors, most suggestibility modalities, including mystical experiences, and most 6D-ASC and HRS factors. Aberrant salience showed widespread correlations with psychedelic experiences, particularly mystical experiences (MEQ) and positive emotionality (e.g., Joyfulness [6D-ASC], Blissful State [11-ASC]). Suggestibility correlated with the same positive emotionality factors and inversely with negatively valenced aberrant salience (Heightened Emotionality [ASI]), emotionality (Dysphoria [HRS), and mystical experiences (Ineffability [MEQ]). In conclusion, DMT’s effects on aberrant salience and suggestibility support its role both as a psychosis and therapy model. The models’ link may be indirect with respect to mystical experiences, with emotionality playing a more crucial role. Importantly, suggestion-induced mystical experiences after DMT may suggest post-acute perceptual plasticity, informing the development of more tailored psychedelic treatments that induce, amplify, and guide therapeutic experiences.

title: Exploring social identity as a mediator of the relationship between personality and wellbeing using latent profile analysis
abstractText: Objective The well-established link between personality and wellbeing has been rarely explored using a social identity approach. This is despite social support typically mediating the association between personality and wellbeing, and the foundational importance of social identity to the provision and receipt of social support. Methods This study employed a cross-sectional online survey research design with 308 adult participants (mean age = 25.31 ± 9.69, 82.4% female, 87.7% white). Latent profile analysis was performed based on participants’ Interpersonal Sensitivity, Dispositional Optimism, Type D personality and Big-5 personality scores. Data were analysed using a combination of MANOVA, ANOVA and mediation analysis to explore between-profile differences in wellbeing and social identity, and the mediating role of social identity within these associations. Results Latent profile analysis identified four personality profiles that differed in wellbeing and social identification. Mediation analyses indicated a partial, modest indirect association for social identification linking profile membership and wellbeing when contrasting profiles characterised by higher versus lower optimism, emotional stability, and extraversion. Conclusions These exploratory findings support social identification as a theoretically relevant pathway linking personality profile typology and wellbeing. Future research could examine whether interventions designed to strengthen social identification can be adapted to reflect differences in personality profiles.

title: Combined Rhizophagus irregularis and Bacillus megaterium inoculation enhances root hydraulics and potassium acquisition and improves maize tolerance to drought stress and potassium deficiency
abstractText: In this study we investigated the effectiveness of combined inoculation with the arbuscular mycorrhizal fungus R. irregularis and the PGPR B. megaterium in improving maize tolerance to combined potassium (K) deficiency and drought stress. Thus, maize plants inoculated with these microorganisms or maintained as uninoculated controls were cultivated either under deficient K supply (0.3 mM K) or under ample K fertilization (6 mM K). Half of plants was maintained under well-watered conditions during the entire experiment and the other half was subjected to drought stress for 15 days before harvest. Results showed that under K deficiency, the combined inoculation of R. irregularis plus B. megaterium allowed maize plants to overcome the problem of K limitation and to reach a similar biomass production than uninoculated control plants cultivated under normal K levels. This effect was observed both, under well-watered and under drought stress conditions. The mechanisms underlying these effects on plant growth include enhanced root hydraulic conductivities, improved photosynthetic capacity and efficiency of photosystem II, reduced oxidative damage to lipids, and enhanced K uptake and accumulation. This indicates that, for important crops such as maize, the inoculated microorganisms can contribute to reducing the use of chemical fertilizers under the influence of additional abiotic stresses such as drought,

title: Polymer-modified manganese ferrite composites for non-photonic removal of Acid Orange 10 dye from aqueous solution
abstractText: A superior performance of manganese ferrite modified with synthetic polymer, polyaniline and biopolymer, chitosan has been effectively developed to achieve, the degradation of an azo dye known as Acid orange 10, in dark conditions. Since the persistent azo dyes are not easily broken down by regular treatment methods as they are chemically Hard-to-degrade, where these azo dye industrial effluents remain a significant issue of environmental concern. In this investigation, Manganese ferrite (MF), MnFe 2 O 4 /polyaniline (MF/PANI), and MnFe 2 O 4 /chitosan (MF/CS) nanocomposites were used to determine the photonic and non-photonic degradation of Acid Orange 10 (AO10) dye under ambient dark stirring conditions. The structural, morphological and surface chemical properties of the catalysts were analyzed with Fourier transform-infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), ultra violet visible spectroscopy (UV-Vis), the high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), energy dispersive X-ray analysis (EDX), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area analysis and Barrett-Joyner-Halenda (BJH) pore size distribution. The UV-analysis for the dye degradation resulted with 65% in 20 mins under UV-photoreactor for base MF, and 98.5% in 6 mins for MF/PANI and 95.8% in 14 mins for MF/CS nanocomposites from aqueous solution under dark stirring conditions.

title: Some Results for a Stationary Navier–Stokes Equation with a Rough Drift in a Weighted Functional Framework
The Effect of Numerical Integration in the FEM for Elliptic Problems with Mixed Boundary Conditions
abstractText: This paper investigates the impact of quadrature accuracy for volume and face integrals in the finite element method (FEM) using \(p\)-th order polynomial shape functions for elliptic problems with mixed Dirichlet and Robin boundary conditions. The optimal \(p\)-th order \(H^1\)-convergence is maintained when numerical integration with algebraic precision at least \(2p-2\) for volume terms and at least \(2p-1\) for face terms is adopted. For \(L^2\)-error, we achieve optimal \(\mathcal{O}(h^{p+1})\) convergence when using quadrature rules of precision no less than \(\max\{p,2p-2\}\) for volume terms and no less than \(2p-1\) for face terms. Of particular significance, we present two examples to show that the above result on \(L^2\)-error is sharp for the linear FEM (\(p=1\)). When reduced to the case of Dirichlet boundary conditions, our results yield improved dependence on the given data compared to the classical results established by Ciarlet et al. Numerical experiments are provided to illustrate the theoretical findings and confirm the necessity of specified quadrature accuracy and data regularity.

title: Detection and luminosity-dependent evolution of the high-energy hump in the Be/X-ray pulsar 1A 1118-61
abstractText: Accreting X-ray pulsars exhibit strong luminosity-dependent changes in their broad-band spectra. At high luminosities, their spectra are usually described by a power-law continuum with a high-energy cutoff, whereas low-luminosity observations have revealed a two-hump spectral morphology. We aim to trace the luminosity-dependent spectral evolution of the Be/X-ray pulsar and to constrain the luminosity range over which the high-energy hump becomes resolved as a separate spectral feature. We combine dense and monitoring with three νstar observations of the 2026 outburst to trace the spectral evolution from łum to a low-luminosity plateau at ≃(1--3) łum in the 4--35 keV band. For each νstar and ART-XC observation, we compare single- and two-component spectral models to determine where an additional high-energy component is required. We also use the two-component model to trace the flux evolution of both components. As the source faded, a smooth single-component continuum no longer adequately described the spectrum, and a two-component model became statistically preferred. At low luminosities, the spectrum developed two resolved broad humps, peaking near ∼10 keV and ∼30--40 keV. The ART-XC monitoring constrains the luminosity range over which this two-hump morphology first emerges to L_ 4-35 ≃(3--6) and 4 , with the lower break coinciding with the emergence of the resolved high-energy hump. title: Pore-Resolved High-Throughput Analysis of Amyloid Aggregation and Amplification
abstractText: Quantitative analysis of amyloid fibrils depends not only on total fibril content but also on how fibrillar species are organized, clustered, and amplified within heterogeneous populations. Conventional thioflavin T (ThT)-based assays provide sensitive sample-level readouts of β-sheet-rich material but offer limited access to the underlying population structure. Here, we introduce the Amyloid Pore Quantification (APQ) chip, a high-throughput analytical platform based on pore-resolved geometric partitioning that measures integrated ThT fluorescence intensity distributions across thousands of defined pore-level units. Using hen egg-white lysozyme as a model amyloid-forming protein, we combine length-controlled truncated amyloid nanofibrils with vacuum-assisted ThT infiltration to establish a reproducible pore-fluorescence reference. APQ provided a concentration-dependent response across a 50-fold range while preserving pore-level distribution information. Pore-resolved measurements revealed pH-dependent signal suppression near the isoelectric point, a population-wide increase in pore intensity following pepsin treatment, and distinct responses to monomer or oligomer incubation and subsequent pH adjustment. Comparison with bulk ThT measurements and AFM observations supported the use of APQ to compare condition-dependent fluorescence distributions influenced by fibrillar organization and pore accessibility. These results establish APQ as a high-throughput platform for distribution-resolved quantitative fluorescence analysis of fibril aggregation and amplification.

title: Testing cosmological structure formation in a unified dark matter-energy model with a fast transition
abstractText: Unified dark matter-energy (UDM) models, a class of models in which dark matter and dark energy exist as a single cosmological fluid, are an alternative approach to Λ cold dark matter (ΛCDM). In this work we focus on a model with a fast transition between dark matter-like and dark energy-like behaviour. The epoch and rapidity of the transition are the key features to enable the formation of structure in this model. We studied its viability using cosmic microwave background and weak lensing data with nested sampling inference methods. We found that the preferred region of the parameter space is the one with early and fast transition models, where the model's ΛCDM limit also lies. Our study confirms that this UDM model is able to form cosmological structure compatible with the data used.

title: Convergence analysis of a MAC scheme for the barotropic Euler system
abstractText: We study a Marker-and-Cell (MAC) scheme for the barotropic Euler system. First, we apply the recently developed Lax-type convergence theorem to show the convergence of the MAC scheme to i) a dissipative weak solution unconditionally and ii) a strong solution as long as it exists. Second, we derive relative energy error estimates up to the lifespan of a strong solution, without assuming uniform boundedness of the numerical sequence. Additionally, assuming the boundedness of the numerical solutions, we obtain a first-order relative-energy estimate, corresponding to a convergence rate of 1/2 for the numerical solutions. Finally, we corroborate our theoretical results by numerical experiments.

abstractText: This article analyzes the interconnection between traditional values and contemporary social demands in ensuring family stability under the conditions of modern society. Drawing on approaches in social philosophy, cultural studies, and sociology, the study examines the family’s moral-normative, spiritual, and social functions. In an analytical perspective, it elucidates the role of traditional values in strengthening the family, as well as the impact of globalization, technological progress, and lifestyle changes. The findings indicate that, to preserve the stability of the family as an institution, traditional values need to be reinterpreted in accordance with contemporary social conditions. The study proposes philosophical foundations for the reintegration of the value system to support family resilience.

title: Academic stress and its associations with perceived cognitive difficulties and sleep quality among individuals with recent MDCAT preparation or examination experience in Punjab, Pakistan: a cross-sectional study
abstractText: Background Academic stress begins long before entering into medical school, particularly among students preparing for highly competitive medical entrance examinations such as the Medical and Dental College Admission Test (MDCAT). Sustained long-term academic pressure may activate the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, increase cortisol secretion, and contribute to neurobiological changes affecting cognition, emotional regulation, and sleep. However, limited evidence exists regarding these effects among pre-medical students in Pakistan. Objective To assess academic stress among pre-medical students in Punjab, Pakistan, evaluate its relationship with perceived cognitive difficulties and poor sleep quality, and interpret these findings in the context of current evidence on the neurobiological mechanisms of stress. Methodology A cross-sectional questionnaire-based study was conducted among 302 pre-medical students from Punjab, Pakistan, who had recently completed the MDCAT examination. Participants completed an anonymous self-administered questionnaire comprising demographic information, an Academic Stress Scale, a Cognitive Difficulties Scale, a Sleep Quality Scale, and a Psychological Well-being and Examination Readiness section. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 32.0.0.0. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, and Pearson correlation analysis were performed to evaluate relationships among the study variables. Results The mean academic stress score was 43.56 ± 3.99 , indicating a high level of perceived academic stress. Mean scores for perceived cognitive difficulties and sleep quality were 34.06 ± 4.35 and 15.41 ± 3.18 , respectively. Academic stress demonstrated a moderate positive correlation with perceived cognitive difficulties ( r = 0.542, p < 0.001 ) and sleep-related problems ( r = 0.512, p < 0.001 ). Perceived cognitive difficulties were also positively correlated with poorer sleep quality ( r = 0.510, p < 0.001 ). These findings are consistent with current evidence suggesting that prolonged academic stress may adversely influence cognitive functioning through stress-related neurobiological pathways. Conclusion Pre-medical students preparing for MDCAT experience considerable academic stress, which is significantly associated with greater perceived cognitive difficulties and poorer sleep quality. The findings support existing evidence that chronic academic stress may have important neurobiological and cognitive consequences even before entry into medical school. Early stress-management interventions, psychological support services, and student well-being initiatives should be incorporated into pre-medical education to promote healthier academic outcomes.

JWST detects a dusty AGB-like source before the Type Ia-CSM supernova 2026sqf
abstractText: Supernova (SN) 2026sqf recently appeared in the nearby face-on spiral galaxy NGC 3310 and has shown signs of strong interaction with a circumstellar medium (CSM). Such an intense interaction, rare among nearby SNe, offers a valuable opportunity to reveal details of the origin and nature of its progenitor system. We present early-time photometric and spectroscopic observations of SN 2026sqf, along with our identification and characterization of a candidate pre-explosion counterpart in space telescope imaging. We analyzed the early-phase spectra and light curves (LCs) of SN 2026sqf. We identified a point source near the SN position in pre-explosion JWST and HST imaging, tested its association with the SN through astrometric alignment of pre- and post-explosion images and a chance-projection analysis, and constructed and modeled its spectral energy distribution (SED). The general characteristics of the spectra, the strengths of the emission lines, and the LC evolution all suggest that SN 2026sqf belongs to the rare SN Ia-CSM subclass, which would make it the closest known member (D ∼ 19 Mpc). The point source is a credible counterpart of the progenitor system, the first such identification for this SN subclass. Under our modeling assumptions, carbonaceous dust around a luminous evolved star provides a reasonable description of its combined SED; compared with local analogues, the candidate most closely resembles an extreme asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star. We report the first candidate pre-explosion counterpart of a thermonuclear SN identified in JWST imaging. Our results support the scenario in which SNe Ia-CSM emerge from a system consisting of a white dwarf and an evolved giant (probably AGB) star. Strong binary interaction, possibly involving common-envelope evolution or a merger, is a natural explanation for the observed properties of the SN and its candidate counterpart, although the channel and timescale remain uncertain. Late-time follow-up, especially with JWST, will allow us to test the identification and the conclusions of our early-phase analysis.

title: Acceptance counts: A social psychological perspective on young men’s responses to baldness
abstractText: Objectives Male pattern balding is a common and benign process. However, some men report intense distress because of it. Consistent with transactional coping theory and the idea of coping norms, this distress may not necessarily arise from baldness itself but rather from social judgments of men’s responses to baldness. Across four studies (total N = 686 young adults aged 18 to 35 years; 61% women), the present research investigated which ways of responding to baldness were perceived as appropriate (Studies 1a and 1b) and to what extent appropriate responses to baldness affected social attractiveness judgments (Studies 2a and 2b). Methods and Results Studies 1a and 1b revealed that participants mostly recommended a hypothetical male friend to accept his baldness or to pursue medical services (e.g., using pharmaceuticals), with the latter recommendation still relatively frequently given even when participants knew about the benign character of baldness. Recommendations for cosmetic services (e.g., using special shampoos) and compensation (e.g., gaining muscle) were less frequently made, and avoidance (e.g., of mirrors) was never recommended. Assessing impression formation, participants of Studies 2a and 2b rated balding men who accepted their baldness as most, and avoidant men as least, socially attractive. Compensating men and men pursuing medical or cosmetic services were ranked as moderately socially attractive. Participant gender was controlled for in all analyses. Conclusions Collectively, these results suggest acceptance of baldness is judged most appropriate and makes the most favorable social impression, offering an important counter to commercialized baldness treatment.

title: Predictive value of bone mineral density assessment methods for postoperative complications after unicompartmental knee arthroplasty
abstractText: Objective To investigate the predictive value of preoperative bone mineral density (BMD) measurements for postoperative complications and reoperation risk in patients undergoing unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA). Methods A total of 1,945 patients with knee osteoarthritis (KOA) who underwent primary UKA at the Affiliated Hospital of Jining Medical University between November 2018 and November 2025 were retrospectively included. Preoperative lumbar spine BMD was measured using quantitative computed tomography. Patients were divided into a reduced BMD group (< 80 mg/cm³) and a normal BMD group (≥ 80 mg/cm³). Data on demographics, surgical parameters, and outcomes were collected. Propensity score matching was performed to balance confounding variables. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were conducted to identify independent risk factors for postoperative complications, and receiver operating characteristic curves were plotted to evaluate the predictive efficacy of BMD. Results Among the enrolled patients, 234 (12.03%) were in the reduced BMD group and 1,711 (87.97%) in the normal BMD group, with the former having a higher proportion of women patients and a higher age (P < 0.001). After 1:1 propensity score matching, 233 patients remained in each group. The reoperation rate was significantly higher in the reduced BMD group (3.00% vs. 0.43%, P = 0.032). Patients with complications had a significantly lower median lumbar BMD value compared with those without complications (93.3 vs. 103.2 mg/cm³, P = 0.026). Multivariate logistic regression analysis confirmed that lumbar BMD was an independent negative predictor of complications after UKA ( OR = 0.700, P = 0.007); lower BMD values were associated with higher risks of postoperative complications. Conclusions Preoperative decreased BMD is an independent risk factor for postoperative complications and reoperation after UKA. Routine preoperative BMD screening and optimized perioperative bone health management should be implemented to reduce complications and improve surgical outcomes.

title: A Scoping Review of the Perceptions and Experiences of People From Underserved Groups of Being on Personalized Stratified Follow-Up Following Treatment for Breast Cancer
abstractText: BACKGROUND: Personalized Stratified Follow-Up (PSFU) is an approach to cancer follow-up involving patients re-accessing care when they need to, rather than attending predetermined appointments. The benefits of this approach are a more personalized experience for patients and increased capacity in clinics. OBJECTIVE: To understand the evidence relating to the experiences of people on PSFU following breast cancer treatment, specifically in terms of the perceptions of people from underserved groups. METHODS: A scoping review of the relevant evidence was conducted. Screening was conducted independently by 2 researchers. Data extracted were charted using a predetermined checklist for summary and analysis. RESULTS: A total of 2728 results were identified through databases; 11 papers were included. Nineteen gray literature resources were also identified. Findings were presented as: (1) key components of PSFU for breast cancer; (2) experiences and perceptions of patients and health professionals in relation to PSFU for breast cancer; (3) suggestions to enhance PSFU; and (4) evidence relating to underserved groups on PSFU for breast cancer. CONCLUSION: Patients on PSFU are generally satisfied with their care and are confident in managing their own condition. Unmet needs include psychological support and re-accessing clinical teams. This review has highlighted that little is known about the experiences of underserved groups. IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING PRACTICE: Nurses should be aware of the importance of providing patients on PSFU with information about self-examination, signs of recurrence, side effects, and re-accessing the clinical team. PSFU services should be designed to ensure that patients from underserved groups do not experience inequalities in their care.

title: Euclid: Quick Data Release (Q1) -- Exploring the detailed visual morphology of galaxies in clusters
abstractText: Galaxy clusters provide unique laboratories for studying environmental effects on galaxy evolution. The morphology--density (T--Σ) and morphology--cluster-centric radius (T--R) relations trace how galaxy morphology is influenced by the environment, but previous studies at intermediate redshifts have been limited in both sample size and radial coverage. We used the Euclid Quick Data Release 1 (Q1) visual morphology catalog to measure the T--Σ and T--R relations for smooth, featured-or-disk, and barred galaxies in known clusters at 0.2łeq złeq 0.5, extending this analysis to large cluster-centric distances (3,R_500c) and studying their dependence on stellar mass. Using photometric redshifts and stellar masses provided by Euclid, we identify 1754 cluster members within 1.5,R_500c, distributed across 71 clusters. We classify the identified galaxies as smooth, featured-or-disk, or barred using the predicted vote fractions provided by the deep learning foundation model in the Q1 visual morphology catalog. Our classification of smooth and featured-or-disk galaxies is similar to the separation between elliptical and disk galaxies. We confirm the T--Σ relation in all the stellar mass ranges studied, with a stronger influence of the cluster environment on galaxy morphology in the densest parts of the cluster and closer to the cluster center. Beyond 1.5,R_500c, the morphological segregation weakens, with featured-or-disk galaxies overtaking smooth galaxies at the lowest densities, consistent with the growing contribution of field interlopers in the cluster outskirts. For barred galaxies, we find a tentative decline of the bar fraction toward lower densities that is most pronounced for the most massive galaxies. In conclusion, our results show that the cluster environment drives a progressive transformation of galaxy morphology, with the loss of disk structure becoming more pronounced toward the cluster core, where environmental processes act most efficiently. These findings, enabled by the unique characteristics of the Q1 visual morphology catalog, advance our physical understanding of how galaxies evolve in dense environments at intermediate redshifts.

title: Prevalence of depression and dementia among institutionalized elderly in Kenya: Nairobi county
abstractText: Objective The purpose of this investigation was to determine the prevalence of and the link between depression and dementia, and other risk factors among institutionalized elderly in Kenya. Methods This research utilized a cross-sectional design. The sample of 194 was selected through simple random sampling. This study used 6-Item Cognitive Impairment test (6-CIT), Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS) and the Cornell Scale for Depression in Dementia (CSDD) to measure the point prevalence of depression and dementia, and a socio-demographic questionnaire to explore the other objectives. Results 11% and 37% screened positive for depression and dementia respectively. Identified risk factors for institutionalization were: being single, having an impairment, chronic illness, poor self-rated health, being dependent for basic daily functioning and having little social support. This study observed a positive relationship between depression and dementia ( r = .253, df = 186, p < .001). There was a statistically significant relationships between having supportive family and dementia ( r = -.181, N = 191, p = .012); and being dependent for basic daily functioning to both depression ( r = .191, N = 191, p = .008) and dementia ( r = .221, N = 191, p = .002). Conclusion Institutionalized elderly had a higher prevalence for depression and dementia. Being married and having higher levels of education were noted to be important protective factors against dementia. Overall study findings indicate that older adult’s mental health may be associated with multiple levels of factors including stressors and resources concurrently, which makes it imperative to further examine these relationships methodically.

title: A dangerous evolution of retroperitoneal infection to infrarenal abdominal aortic pseudoaneurysm
abstractText: Background Mycotic pseudoaneurysm of the infrarenal abdominal aorta is a rare and potentially fatal complication of infection. Early diagnosis can be challenging because clinical symptoms are often nonspecific, and initial imaging may demonstrate only inflammatory changes without aneurysmal formation. This case highlights the importance of recognizing evolving radiographic findings in patients with a history of recurrent infection. Case presentation A 46-year-old man with a history of recurrent pelvic abscesses secondary to diverticulitis presented with three days of back pain, nausea, and vomiting. Initial imaging demonstrated a retroperitoneal inflammatory mass encasing the infrarenal aorta without evidence of pseudoaneurysm. Repeat imaging two weeks later demonstrated interval development of a pseudoaneurysm, raising concern for an infected aortic process. The patient underwent midline exploratory laparotomy with definitive surgical management and subsequently completed six weeks of intravenous antimicrobial therapy. He had an uncomplicated recovery with resolution of the infection and no reported recurrence. Conclusions Mycotic pseudoaneurysm of the abdominal aorta should be considered in patients with systemic or localized infection and new, unexplained back or abdominal pain, particularly when inflammatory changes surround the aorta on imaging. Serial imaging may be critical for identifying rapid progression from periaortic inflammation to pseudoaneurysm formation. Early recognition and definitive surgical management combined with prolonged antimicrobial therapy can prevent rupture and improve outcomes.

title: Allegorical Anthropomorphism: The Hostile Environment, Brexit, and Discrimination in Jasper Fforde's The Constant Rabbit (2020)
abstractText: This article explores the satirical allegorisation of the UK's hostile environment policies, and Brexit, through anthropomorphism in Jasper Fforde's 2020 novel The Constant Rabbit. A self-consciously Brexit-era novel, the narrative engages closely with contemporaneous political and tabloid rhetoric to offer a biting commentary on society, casting anthropomorphised rabbits as the 'Other' against which policy and rhetoric rails, and society discriminates. What this article does, therefore, is make use of political speeches and tabloid articles, as well as scholarship around the hostile environment and crimmigration, to situate The Constant Rabbit within its various political and rhetorical contexts and demonstrate that, as a piece of ‘Brexlit’, the novel utilises allegory not only to highlight the mechanisms that perpetuate discrimination but to act as a warning against rising nationalism.

title: Short-time modified Robert Jones Bandage does not worsen postoperative swelling in enhanced-recovery after primary total knee arthroplasty without tourniquet: a single-centre, randomized controlled study
abstractText: Purpose Despite evidence showing the Modified Robert Jones Bandage (MRJB) is ineffective in reducing joint swelling after total knee arthroplasty (TKA), its use persists due to clinical tradition. This study examines the impact of a shortened MRJB duration on knee swelling and early postoperative rehabilitation in primary unilateral TKA without a tourniquet. Methods This single-centre, randomized controlled study included 114 patients, who were randomly assigned to two groups using an envelope method. All surgeries were performed by the same surgeon. The short-time group received MRJB for 4 hours postoperatively, while the long-time group wore the bandage for 24 hours post-surgery. Knee swelling was assessed by measuring the circumferences of the knee, thigh, and calf. Postoperative rehabilitation outcomes were evaluated using both subjective measures (self-reported knee comfort and pain, assessed by VAS scores at rest and during activity) and objective measures (passive and active extension, active flexion, extension lag, range of motion (ROM), Timed Up and Go (TUG) test, and adverse events). Results No significant differences in knee, thigh, or calf circumferences were observed at 1-, 3-, 14-, and 28-days post-surgery. On postoperative day 1, the long-time group exhibited slightly better passive extension (-1.39 ± 3.01 versus − 2.98 ± 3.07, P = 0.006). No significant differences were found in other rehabilitation parameters. Conclusion Reducing the duration of MRJB application to 4 hours did not exacerbate postoperative knee swelling. Furthermore, prolonged MRJB use did not improve rehabilitation outcomes. Based on these findings, we recommend adopting a 4-hour postoperative MRJB as a feasible and effective practice for TKA without tourniquet. title: Effects of AI-assisted case discussion and virtual patient consultation on medical students’ learning outcomes
abstractText: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) holds broad application prospects in medical education; however, systematic empirical evidence regarding its effectiveness in facilitating case discussions and virtual patient consultation remains scarce. This study recruited undergraduate medical students and conducted experiments to examine the pedagogical effects of AI-assisted case discussion and virtual consultation. Methods A total of 207 medical undergraduates participated in this study. Using the self-developed intelligent experimental platform, medical students engaged in AI-assisted case discussion and virtual consultation. Experiment 1 employed a single-factor, three-level between-subjects design to compare the effects of AI-assisted case discussion, peer case discussion, and a lecture-only control condition on medical students’ knowledge acquisition, intrinsic motivation, and interaction quality. Experiment 2 utilized a single-factor, four-level between-subjects design to examine the effects of virtual patient consultation and the sequencing of AI-assisted case discussion and virtual consultation on medical students’ knowledge acquisition, intrinsic motivation, and consultation process quality. The control group participants were the same individuals across both experiments. Results Results indicated that the AI-assisted case discussion group achieved significantly higher knowledge scores than the control group. The virtual consultation group, the consultation-then-discussion group, and the discussion-then-consultation group all outperformed the control group in knowledge acquisition. The discussion-then-consultation group demonstrated higher intrinsic motivation and consultation comprehensiveness, yet exhibited lower empathy than the virtual consultation group. Conclusions These findings suggest that both AI-assisted case discussion and virtual patient consultation can effectively enhance medical students’ knowledge acquisition compared with learning by watching instructional videos only, while different intervention sequences exert differential effects on intrinsic motivation, consultation comprehensiveness, and empathy. The results provide theoretical foundations and practical guidance for AI-empowered medical education.

title: Development and validation of a machine learning–based cell death–immune prognostic model for risk stratification in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
abstractText: Background Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) shows marked prognostic heterogeneity, partly driven by interactions between regulated cell death and the tumor immune microenvironment. A framework integrating multiple cell-death programs with immune states is still lacking. Methods This study integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data to characterize immune–cell-death interactions in DLBCL. Immune–cell-death-related genes were identified by intersecting differentially expressed genes with immune and cell-death gene sets. A cell-death–immune score (CDIS) was constructed using 101 machine-learning combinations and evaluated in three external cohorts. This study assessed immune infiltration, cell-death transcriptional programs, cell–cell communication, ligand–target interactions, pseudotime trajectories, drug connectivity, molecular docking and virtual perturbation. In vitro assays further tested BAFF stimulation and tamoxifen treatment in DLBCL cell lines. Results We identified 159 immune–cell-death-related genes and selected 16 genes from 25 candidates to construct the CDIS prognostic model; CoxBoost plus random survival forest ranked highest (mean C-index 0.703). High CDIS was associated with suppressed transcriptional programs of immunogenic cell death and an immune-cold microenvironment with M2-like macrophage enrichment. CDIS provides incremental value over International Prognostic Index (IPI), particularly within the IPI 2 stratum, where it significantly further distinguished high- from low-risk patients (5-year overall survival 63.6% vs. 42.7%; log-rank P = 0.012). Single-cell analysis localized model genes mainly to macrophages and identified an M2-like macrophage–BAFF/APRIL–malignant B-cell axis. Exogenous BAFF promoted DLBCL-cell proliferation and reduced apoptosis, whereas tamoxifen inhibited proliferation dose-dependently. Conclusions CDIS serves as a complementary prognostic model to IPI, refining risk within IPI strata, and reveals a candidate mechanism centered on the M2-like macrophage–BAFF/APRIL–malignant B-cell axis.

Quantum-enhanced Search for Galactic Dark Photons Using Cat-State Cavities
abstractText: We present a quantum-enhanced search for the Galactic dark-photon background (GDPB), a relativistic and anisotropic vector field that can be produced by dark-matter decay or annihilation in the Milky Way halo. We reinterpret an existing quantum-enhanced dark-photon dataset obtained with a superconducting circuit QED platform originally developed for wave-like dark-photon dark-matter searches, consisting of a high-$Q$ niobium cavity in the $\mathrm{TM}_{010}$ mode dispersively coupled to a transmon qubit. By preparing four-component cat states and performing repeated quantum non-demolition parity measurements, analyzed with a hidden Markov model, we extract photon-transition probabilities for multiple cat amplitudes and integration times. The coupling to the GDPB is governed by a polarization- and angle-dependent cavity overlap function, which predicts a distinctive diurnal modulation of the excitation rate for both longitudinal and transverse polarizations. From the absence of such modulation, we set 90\% Bayesian credible upper limits on the kinetic-mixing parameter $\epsilon$ for two benchmark production mechanisms (parametric and cascade decay) over the relativistic mass range $m_X \leq \omega_c/10$. title: Semantic Distance Differently Modulates FPVS-EEG Responses to Words and Pictures
abstractText: The organization of semantic knowledge within the brain has long been studied through various theoretical frameworks and is still a matter of debate. Many studies that have helped advancing our knowledge about this topic have approached it in the context of its deterioration, notably in patients with semantic dementia. In healthy subjects, the question whether and how semantic distance between concepts represented by picture or word stimuli influences brain responses remains understudied. In this study with 24 healthy subjects, we used EEG recordings coupled with a fast periodic visual stimulation (FPVS) approach, for the first time, to assess the semantic distance effect with different stimulus modalities. Picture or word stimuli from a reference category (birds) appeared every fourth item among a 4-Hz stream of either man-made objects (forming the high distance [HD] condition) or other animals (low distance [LD] condition). Within a few minutes of recording, EEG responses were observed at the predetermined frequency of the reference category presentation (at 1 Hz), suggesting its exemplars were activated at least sufficiently to be automatically discriminated from different superordinate (HD) and basic (LD) categories, for both pictures and words. Pictures and words elicited a different pattern of response to semantic distance, with larger amplitudes in the HD than in the LD condition for pictures but a reversed pattern of somewhat greater amplitudes in the LD than in the HD condition for words. Our findings support a similarity-based structure of semantic representations and provide evidence for a differential mapping between semantic and picture/word surface representations.

title: Antibacterial Activity Of Manganese-Doped Zinc Oxide Nanoparticles Against Multidrug Resistant Salmonella Typhi
abstractText: Background: Multiple drug resistant (MDR) Salmonella Typhi is a public health threat. Due to their unique physicochemical properties, the manganese doped with zinc oxide nanoparticles (Mn-ZnO NPs) have become of interest as possible antimicrobial agents. Background: Multi drug resistant (MDR) Salmonella Objective: This research aims at synthesis and characterization of Mn-ZnO NPs and its antibacterial activity and hemocompatibility. Methodology: Chemical co-precipitation method was used for the synthesis of Mn-ZnO NPs. UV–Vis, XRD, EDX, SEM and FTIR were employed to characterize the nanoparticles. Red blood cell (RBC) hemolysis assay was used to evaluate hemocompatibility of red blood cell (RBC). The antibacterial activity against the MDR S. Typhi was determined by agar well diffusion method and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) was determined by broth based assay. Results: The absorption peak of Mn-ZnO NPs is 372 nm and the pure ZnO NPs is 360 nm in the UV-Vis spectroscopy. XRD patterns display the hexagonal wurtzite structure and EDX analysis revealed the presence of zinc (56.3%), oxygen (38.2%) and manganese (5.5%). A few agglomeration and 40-80 nm particles were identified by the SEM. FTIR spectra showed typical peaks at 3412, 1635 and 435 cm-1. Hemolysis was 4.5% at 50 µg/mL and increased to 10.1% at 100 µg/mL. The diameter of the inhibition zone grew from 8.4 mm at 20 µg/mL to 16.8 mm at 60 µg/mL concentrations. The MIC of the MDR S. Typhi was 62.5 µg/mL. Conclusion: The concentration-dependent antibacterial activity of the Mn-ZnO NPs against MDR S. Typhi was observed and the relatively low hemolytic activity of the NPs was observed at low concentration. They need further investigation for their antimicrobial activity, action mechanism and for their safety concerning potential biomedical applications.

title: Disentangling geographic, climatic and edaphic signatures of genetic differentiation in Nigerien Acacia senegal populations
abstractText: Geographic distance and environmental heterogeneity can both generate genetic differentiation among natural populations, but their respective contributions are difficult to separate when climate varies along a geographic gradient. We examined the relative associations of geographic and climatic distance with genetic differentiation among eight natural populations of Acacia senegal (L.) Willd distributed along a west-to-east aridity and temperature gradient in Niger. Pairwise genetic differentiation was strongly associated with geographic distance and more weakly with climatic distance. When both predictors were fitted simultaneously, the geographic coefficient remained large whereas the climatic coefficient did not differ from zero. This result was consistent across the climatic distance definitions used and all eight leave-one-population-out iterations. Distance-based variance partitioning attributed 56.0% of adjusted genetic variation uniquely to geography and a smaller but statistically supported fraction of 12.1% uniquely to climate. Geographic separation is therefore the dominant factor structuring genetic differentiation. We hypothesize that the observed pattern reflects a strong isolation by distance pattern.

title: Moderate-Intensity Interval Training Is Sufficient to Increase Muscle Mitochondrial Respiratory Capacity and Exercise Tolerance in Young Untrained Men
abstractText: INTRODUCTION: There is considerable evidence that physical activity can stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis in muscles, enhance maximal mitochondrial oxygen consumption rate, improve physical fitness, and help maintain overall health in humans. On the other hand, there is growing evidence that excessive training load may have a detrimental effect on mitochondria and glucose homeostasis. HYPOTHESIS: We hypothesized that moderate-intensity interval training (MIIT) would be sufficient to increase muscle mitochondrial oxidative capacity and exercise tolerance in untrained healthy people. METHODS: Eleven young, healthy, untrained males took part in this study. They performed a 7-week endurance training program (MIIT) on a cycle ergometer, composed of 4 sessions per week, each lasting 40 min. Before and after the MIIT training program, a pulmonary maximal oxygen consumption (V̇O 2max ) as well as lactate threshold (LT) were determined and a muscle biopsy from the m. vastus lateralis was taken to evaluate the level of muscle proteins related to energy metabolism and mitochondrial biogenesis, and to measure the muscle's maximal mitochondrial respiration rate. RESULTS: The training resulted in an increase of skeletal muscle homogenate V̇O 2max (by ~50%, P =0.001), due to increased mitochondrial mass and the enrichment of mitochondria with the individual respiratory chain complexes. The MIIT increased the power output at the lactate threshold (PO at LT) by ~43 W ( P =0.001) and the pulmonary V̇O 2max by 7% ( P =0.01) and had no adverse effect on blood glucose homeostasis. CONCLUSIONS: MIIT, which is a less intense form of training than the commonly used types of interval training, effectively induces a range of beneficial muscular and systemic adaptations that contribute to improvement of physical fitness and maintenances good health in humans.
