title: Milliarcsecond-scale jet reorientations in GRS 1915+105 pointing towards a warped accretion disc
abstractText: The black hole X-ray binary GRS 1915+105 exhibited persistent X-ray activity for more than 26 years after its discovery, prior to entering a prolonged low X-ray flux state in 2018, while remaining bright at radio wavelengths. Multi-wavelength observations suggest that this low X-ray state results from the emergence of a complex layer of absorbing material, whose exact nature remains unknown. Since the X-ray emission is obscured, radio jet observations provide an unobstructed view of the physical changes associated with this phase. Recently published Very Large Array (VLA) and East Asian VLBI Network (EAVN) observations have revealed substantial changes in the jet position angle (PA). Here, we present higher-resolution VLBI observations to investigate the connection between the obscuration event and the jet behaviour close to the launch region. We observed GRS 1915+105 with the Very Long Baseline Array (VLBA) and European VLBI Network (EVN) during the early X-ray obscuration phase across four epochs spanning 2019--2021, sampling a diverse range of jet and accretion behaviours. In this paper, we focus on the milliarcsecond jet morphology and PA changes across the four epochs and contextualize these in relation to the reported X-ray behaviour. Many of the PAs measured post-2018 are significantly offset from GRS 1915+105's pre-obscuration jet axis, which has a weighted mean of 142^ ̧irc ± 7^ ̧irc on milliarcsecond scales. We find a maximum offset of 57^ ̧irc ± 8^ ̧irc from this axis, the largest such offset reported for GRS 1915+105 to date. Our four epochs reveal a broad variety of jet behaviours, ranging from a stable, compact source with a large PA offset, to a bright, flaring source with a similarly large offset, to an extended jet with a PA that is closer to the pre-obscuration axis, and finally to a non-detection. The lack of measurable PA changes within individual eight-hour epochs rules out rapid Lense-Thirring precession of the inner disc as the direct driver of the jet reorientation. Instead, given the timescales involved, coupled with the system's geometry and the apparent connection to the X-ray obscuration event, favour a radiation-driven warped accretion disc, in a configuration that could naturally explain the persistent obscuration.

title: The impact of M-dwarf stellar convection on exoplanetary atmospheric signatures. A 3D radiation-hydrodynamics simulation analysis for high-resolution spectroscopy
abstractText: M-dwarf stars, as the most abundant and long-lived stellar population in the Galaxy, represent prime targets for the detection and characterization of small, temperate exoplanets; however, their complex activity and convective surfaces pose significant challenges for high-resolution spectroscopic studies aimed at identifying atmospheric habitability signatures. This work investigates the impact of stellar convection on high-resolution spectroscopy of M dwarfs, quantifies its contamination of exoplanetary atmospheric signals, and develops an integrated framework combining 3D radiative hydrodynamical (RHD) simulations, spectroscopic modeling, and transit analysis to mitigate stellar noise. We employed 3D RHD simulations of M-dwarf convection to compute synthetic spectra using state-of-the-art molecular and atomic line data and compare them with observations of GJ 3470. We modeled high-resolution transits of the Neptune-size GJ,3470,b, including center-to-limb variations (CLVs) and the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect (RME), and used principal component analysis (PCA) to de-trend stellar effects. We show the contribution of different molecular absorption features in the dense and complex spectra of M dwarfs. We calibrated the empirical velocity parameters used in 1D hydrostatic stellar models. A comparison with observations shows that current H_2O line lists remain inaccurate, with modest agreement in line strength and position within the K-band interval. During the transit of GJ,3470,b, the CLVs+RME amplitude is comparable to exoplanet signals. Principal component analysis can, in principle, de-trend these effects, but its behavior depends on the co-presence of telluric and planetary signals and the observational noise budget. While we detect the exoplanet without bias from stellar residuals, this result is limited to a narrow spectral interval and a specific orbital configuration. This study demonstrates the importance of 3D RHD simulations for modeling convection-induced spectral variability in M dwarfs and provides a framework for quantifying stellar contamination in high-resolution transit spectroscopy, supporting robust atmospheric characterization with ELT observations.

title: The ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST survey. The Tully-Fisher relation at z = 4-6
abstractText: The Tully-Fisher relation (TFR) provides a fundamental link between galaxy mass and their kinematics. Although its evolution is relatively well constrained up to cosmic noon, observational probes at higher redshifts remain scarce. In this work, we investigate the stellar and baryonic TFRs at z=4-6 by analyzing JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations of 18 main-sequence star-forming galaxies belonging to the ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST survey. We applied a morpho-kinematic disk classification scheme, finding five disk-like galaxies and a survey disk fraction of 0.28 ,M_⊙, , and intrinsic velocity dispersions of These disk galaxies span stellar masses of 10^ 9.5-10.5 -1 -1 . For both versions of the TFR, we found that the ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST disks lie below the local relations and are likely offset from those reported at cosmic noon (z and By fixing the TFR slope to the z=0 value, we measured zero-point offsets for the stellar-mass TFR of -0.96 dex -0.50 dex relative to the local Universe and cosmic noon, respectively. For the baryonic TFR, we found zero-point offsets of -0.57 dex and -0.30 dex with respect to the local Universe and cosmic noon relations. Our measurements are consistent with the redshift evolution of the zero-points of both TFRs being driven by the evolution of dark matter halo properties with cosmic time, modulated by a reduced contribution of dark matter to the dynamical mass on the galaxy scale.

title: Cross-cultural validation of the AAQ-II in five countries: A SEM and psychometric network analysis approaches
abstractText: Background Experiential avoidance (EA) describes the tendency to evade negative internal experiences (e.g., distressing thoughts, emotions). EA is implicated across mental health conditions, positioning it as a central target for interventions like Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT). The Acceptance and Action Questionnaire-II (AAQ-II) is widely employed to measure EA; however, its cross-cultural reliability and factorial stability have not been comprehensively validated across diverse contexts. Aim This study aimed to assess the cross-cultural validity and psychometric stability of the AAQ-II across five countries (Peru, Mexico, USA, Belgium, and Hungary) using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) and network analysis. Method A sample of 3,719 adults, primarily female (63.65%), was collected from five countries. Data analysis included SEM to evaluate factorial structure and network analysis to examine item interrelationships, assessing Expected Influence (EI) as a centrality measure. Multiverse analysis using 5,000 bootstrap samples further evaluated network stability across samples. Results SEM confirmed a unidimensional AAQ-II structure across all regions, indicating consistent factorial validity. Network analysis identified "Painful Memories" (AAQ4) and "Painful Experiences" (AAQ1) as central nodes across cultures, with regional variations in item relationships reflecting unique sociocultural influences. For instance, individualistic societies (e.g., USA) emphasized EA linked to achievement and competitive concerns, while collectivist countries (e.g., Peru, Mexico) associated EA with familial and social obligations. Multiverse analysis revealed stable EA constructs across samples. Discussion Results validate the cross-cultural applicability of the AAQ-II, with findings underscoring cultural impacts on EA manifestations. Network analysis provided nuanced insights into item interactions, showing that cultural factors, such as individualism, historical trauma, and social norms, shape EA expression differently across regions. This supports the use of culturally informed approaches in EA interventions. Conclusion The AAQ-II exhibits reliable cross-cultural validity, affirming its utility for assessing EA across diverse settings. These findings enhance the application of the tool in psychological therapies worldwide, suggesting that culturally tailored EA interventions may benefit from considering specific sociocultural factors influencing EA processes. Future research should investigate additional variables that may affect EA in different cultural contexts.

title: A large radiatively loud anti-glitch in 1E 2259+586 with a protracted recovery
abstractText: Anti-glitches are relatively rare and enigmatic timing anomalies. While recent high-cadence monitoring has revealed some radiatively quiet anti-glitches across various pulsar populations, the nature of radiatively loud anti-glitches---and their intricate connections to magnetospheric activities---remain poorly understood. We aim to present a comprehensive observational characterization of a new, large anti-glitch in the magnetar and explore its phenomenological uniqueness relative to other magnetars. We analyzed the timing, flux, pulse profile evolution, and spectral properties of the source during this new event using multi-instrument X-ray observations from , , and . EP NICER IXPE We report a new anti-glitch in ,Hz and Δν/ν ≈ -8.19(4) . In stark contrast to the source's anti-glitch event in 2019, this anomaly is accompanied by extreme radiative activity. The persistent X-ray flux roughly doubles (∼ 106% increase), followed by a protracted recovery exceeding 320 days. Moreover, the pulse profile exhibits a modest but significant change: the depth of the valley between the main and secondary peaks decreases, and then recovers slowly along with the flux. In addition, the spectral properties change across the event, and a short, soft γ-ray burst was detected by the -GBM around the time of the event. These characteristics are similar to those observed during the radiatively loud anti-glitch in 2012. occurring in 2025, which is the largest detected in this source, with Δν ≈ -1.174(7) 10^ -7 10^ -7 Fermi is a unique source even among magnetars, exhibiting an anti-glitch rate comparable to that of normal spin-up glitches. Strikingly, its anti-glitch events can occur either accompanied by dramatic radiative changes or in relatively quiescent states. In addition, we find that the fractional amplitudes of its anti-glitches appear to increase monotonically. Whether this trend persists merits further verification. These unique observational characteristics indicate that continuous, regular monitoring of is essential for understanding the underlying mechanisms of anti-glitches.

title: Medication Safety Risks Associated With Inappropriate Use of Non-Crushable Tablets in Enterally Fed Patients: A Nationwide Cohort Study
abstractText: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Hospitalized patients receiving enteral feeding are at high risk of medication administration errors. In clinical practice, non-crushable oral tablets may be inappropriately prescribed, potentially resulting in adverse outcomes. This study examined the association between inappropriate use of non-crushable oral tablets during hospitalization and early post-discharge emergency department (ED) visits among patients receiving enteral feeding. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide population-based cohort study using a national health insurance claims database in 2020, including 173,476 hospitalized patients receiving enteral feeding. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate the association between inappropriate use of non-crushable tablets and the hazard of the first ED visit during the 3-day post-discharge follow-up period. RESULTS: Among 173,476 patients, 40.2% were exposed to inappropriate medication use. Exposure was associated with a significantly higher hazard of a first ED visit during the 3-day post-discharge follow-up period (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.954; 95% confidence interval, 1.721-2.217). The association varied significantly across age groups and inpatient departments, with the largest adjusted hazard ratios observed among patients aged <65 years and those treated in hematology and oncology, infectious diseases, and neurosurgery. Selected comorbidities, including hypertension, cerebrovascular accident, and dementia, were also associated with a higher hazard of an early ED visit. CONCLUSION: Orders for non-crushable tablets among hospitalized patients receiving enteral feeding were common and were associated with a substantially higher hazard of an early post-discharge ED visit. The association varied across age groups and inpatient departments, although these subgroup findings should be interpreted cautiously. These findings highlight an important medication safety concern during transitions of care and support further evaluation of system-level strategies, including prescribing safeguards, clinical decision support, and multidisciplinary medication review, to improve the quality and safety of medication management.

title: The indirect effects of social anxiety and social support on alcohol use among UK university students: The role of negative reinforcement
abstractText: Background Socially anxious students may be vulnerable to risky alcohol use, whereas perceived social support may be protective; however, the mechanisms through which social anxiety heightens risk and perceived social support reduces risk remain unclear. This study examined how social anxiety and perceived social support influence risky alcohol use through negative-reinforcement pathways of coping and conformity drinking motives. Method A convenience sample of undergraduate students from a large university in the United Kingdom ( N = 152; 74% female) completed an online self-report survey assessing perceived social support (MSPSS), social anxiety (SIAS), drinking motives (DMQ-R), and past-year alcohol use (AUDIT-C score). Using a cross-sectional observational design, structural equation modelling was conducted to test direct and indirect associations among study variables. Results Social anxiety significantly predicted coping (β = .260, p = .001) and conformity (β = .222, p = .006) motives. Past-year alcohol use was predicted by coping motives (β = .429, p < .001), but not by conformity motives. An indirect effect of social anxiety on alcohol use via coping motives was identified (β = .113, p = .005). Perceived social support was associated with lower coping motives (β = –.172, p = .038), but not with conformity motives. A protective indirect effect of perceived social support on alcohol use via lowered endorsement of coping motives was also observed (β = –.074, p = .037). Conclusion The findings suggest that social anxiety may increase risky alcohol use through coping motives, whereas perceived social support may protect against risky alcohol use by reducing coping-motivated drinking, thereby partially counteracting this risk pathway.

title: Penerapan Ne Bis In Idem oleh Penyidik Pada Tindak Pidana Penipuan Bermodus Arisan Online
abstractText: Asas Nebis In Idem diatur pada Pasal 76 KUHP yang menyatakan bahwa seseorang tidak boleh dituntut dua kali karena perbuatan yang telah mendapat putusan hakim yang telah mempunyai kekuatan hukum tetap. Pada kasus penipuan arisan online dimana korban melapor secara terpisah kepada pihak kepolisian, padahal pelaku yang dilaporkan adalah orang yang sama dan dengan modus operandi yang identik. Di sinilah permasalahan mulai muncul: setelah pelaku diproses hukum dan dijatuhi putusan pidana berdasarkan satu laporan, apakah laporan-laporan lainnya masih bisa ditindaklanjuti. Penelitian ini mengkaji tentang penyidikan tindak pidana penipuan bermodus arisan online serta penerapan ne bis in idem oleh Penyidik, dengan menggunakan pendekatan yuridis empiris di dukung pendekatan yurididis normatif. Hasil penelitian di peroleh penyidikan tindak pidana penipuan bermodus arisan online oleh penyidik Kepolisian Daerah Sumbar dilaksanakan dengan melakukan penelusuran jejak digital serta pengumpulan alat bukti elektronik yang sah menurut hukum. Penerapan Ne Bis In Idem oleh penyidik pada tahap pertama dilakukan melalui identifikasi dasar laporan dan objek peristiwa pidana. Tahap ini merupakan kerja awal ketika laporan diterima dan ditelaah untuk mengetahui siapa pelapor, siapa terlapor, kapan peristiwa terjadi, bagaimana modusnya, apa bentuk kerugiannya, serta apakah sebelumnya sudah pernah ada proses hukum atas kejadian yang sama. Selanjutnya dilakukan pemeriksaan status hukum perkara terdahulu yang mungkin berkaitan dengan pelaku yang sama dan sudah adanya putusan pengadilan terhadap perkara tersebut.

title: Temporal dependence and variable persistence in daily fluctuations of the peso/dollar exchange rate: Mexico, 2004–2026
abstractText: This study analyzes the temporal dependence of daily Mexican peso/U.S. dollar exchange-rate fluctuations over 2004–2026 using the Hurst exponent, detrended fluctuation analysis (dfa), and the semiparametric gph estimator. The sample is divided into subperiods associated with different economic and financial episodes and is complemented by a rolling-window analysis. The results reveal substantial temporal heterogeneity: Hurst, dfa, and gph estimates vary across subperiods and, in some cases, provide divergent signals. In the recursive analysis, the signal compatible with persistence remains in a majority of windows when window lengths of 181, 252, and 365 observations are considered, although mean H declines as the window length increases. The Ht – Ht (t + 1) representation also shows a concentration of estimates around central H levels of approximately H = 0.53–0.55, depending on the window length. These findings are consistent with time-varying dependence and changes in the intensity of the estimated temporal structure. The evidence does not by itself establish long memory for the entire sample, causal relationships between economic episodes and persistence, or a formal rejection of the efficient market hypothesis. The phase-space analysis is therefore interpreted as an exploratory representation of the recursive dynamics of the estimator.

title: Localized Acanthosis Nigricans Induced by Exogenous Insulin Delivery at Insulin Pump Site in Adolescent with Type 1 Diabetes
abstractText: Acanthosis nigricans is a hyperkeratotic dermatosis that is commonly associated with severe insulin resistance and rarely in patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus. Here, we report a novel case of an adolescent with type 1 diabetes mellitus who developed localized acanthosis nigricans at his continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion site. This case demonstrates both the unusual cutaneous complication as well as and highlights the importance of pump-site rotation with continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion.

title: How AI-powered chatbot empathy drives online repurchase intention: the mediating role of service trust
abstractText: AI chatbots are performing an increasing amount of emotional labor for online retailers. However, it is still unclear if the engineered empathetic nature of these AI chatbots can lead to increased repeat purchasing behavior and how they do so. This paper uses the stimulus-organism-response model to conceptualize AI chatbot emotional support as a stimulus, service trust as an organismic state (or internal experience), and repurchase intentions online as a response to those stimuli. Additionally, we examine the role that digital anxiety may play as a boundary condition. Using survey data from 447 Iraqi consumers who have purchased items online, we used Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLSSEM) to analyze our results. The results show that AI chatbot emotional support was significantly related to service trust, which in turn was significantly related to repurchase intentions. Furthermore, trust completely mediated the positive relationship between the two variables, such that all of the effects of chatbot emotional support on repurchase intentions were carried by trust. Contrary to expectations, digital anxiety did not moderate the relationship between chatbot emotional support and trust or conditionally affect the mediation of trust; thus, the process of generating trust occurs at similar rates regardless of level of digital anxiety. Overall, the findings suggest that trust is the primary pathway by which machine-generated empathy leads to customer loyalty and also demonstrate that there are no contingency conditions associated with stimulus-organism-response theory within a developing e-commerce environment.

title: “Becoming known”: the role of everyday, authentic encounters
abstractText: Purpose This article aims to further our understanding of the ways in which informal communication between managers and employees is experienced as positive/negative and its related benefits/drawbacks. Design/methodology/approach To better understand the antecedents and benefits of positive informal communication, we conducted 10 semi-structured, in-depth interviews with remote and hybrid workers within 4 different industries across the western United States. Findings This study advances our understanding of when everyday encounters are experienced positively in manager–employee relationships. These encounters were most beneficial when they created moments of shared identification oriented toward connection rather than task accomplishment and when those encounters were perceived as authentic. Over time, repeated authentic interactions strengthened workplace relationships. In contrast, absent, inconsistent or unevenly distributed opportunities for connection were experienced negatively. Originality/value The findings demonstrate that the concept of encounter is a useful lens through which to understand how everyday informal interactions contribute to healthy manager–employee relationships. In particular, the study highlights the importance of authenticity and consistency in shaping whether or not informal communication is experienced positively.

title: Better off without it: the influence of negative review labels on consumers' purchase intentions
abstractText: Purpose This research examines whether and why the presence versus absence of a negative review label influences consumers' purchase intentions, tests the mediating role of perceived fit and examines the moderating roles of negative review content salience and purchase type. Design/methodology/approach Four online experiments were conducted via the Credamo and CloudResearch platforms. A total of 1,300 Chinese and U.S. consumers were recruited. Findings This research identifies a “negative review label effect”: holding review content constant, the absence (vs presence) of a negative review label increases consumers' purchase intentions (Study 1). This effect is mediated by perceived fit between review information and consumers' positive initial expectations (Study 2). Further, the effect is attenuated when negative review content is made salient (Study 3) and disappears for experiential purchases (Study 4). Originality/value Theoretically, this research extends the literature on negative consumer reviews and the fit effect by identifying negative review labels as an understudied feature of review presentation and perceived fit as its underlying mechanism. Practically, it offers guidance for optimizing review-page design through strategic presentation of negative review information.

title: Explaining citizen complaints against the police: organizational, environmental and system factors
abstractText: Purpose The study aims to examine variation in citizen complaints against police departments, with particular attention to how organizational characteristics, environmental context and features of complaint systems shape complaint volume. Design/methodology/approach Using data from 129 large U.S. municipal police departments, this study employs stepwise negative binomial regression to assess the impact of organizational characteristics, environmental context and features of complaint systems on complaint volume. Findings Organizational characteristics – particularly department size and educational requirements – emerge as significant predictors of complaint volume, with larger agencies generating more complaints and those requiring education beyond high school generating fewer. In contrast, community-level variables such as crime rates, unemployment and racial composition show limited explanatory power. Importantly, features of citizen complaint systems play a meaningful role. Departments that allow third-party complaints and avoid penalties for false reporting exhibit different complaint patterns, suggesting that system accessibility influences complaint levels. Moreover, the relationship between in-service training and complaints varies depending on complaint system openness, indicating that training effectiveness may depend on broader accountability structures. Practical implications The findings suggest that citizen complaint volume reflects not only organizational characteristics but also complaint system accessibility. Future research should account for variation in complaint system accessibility when using complaints as indicators of misconduct. Originality/value While prior research has relied heavily on citizen complaints as a proxy for police misconduct, few studies account for differences in the accessibility and structure of complaint processes themselves.

title: Ethical leadership, coworker cyberloafing cues and employee cyberloafing: an applied behavior analysis perspective
abstractText: Purpose This study examines whether ethical leadership is associated with employee cyberloafing directly and indirectly through the cyberloafing behavior of immediate coworkers. Drawing on applied behavior analysis (ABA) and social learning theory, it conceptualizes coworkers’ cyberloafing as social antecedent cues in each employee’s local work environment rather than as a shared team norm. Design/methodology/approach Data came from 100 team leaders and 300 employees in 100 three-member teams in City of London investment banks. Leaders rated their own ethical leadership; employees reported their own cyberloafing. Team dependence and within-team agreement were assessed with intraclass correlations and the within-group agreement index (rwg). The direct association was tested with a random-intercept multilevel model; the mediation hypotheses were tested with a focal–coworker design that separates each focal employee’s cyberloafing from that of the two coworkers, with sensitivity analyses. Findings Ethical leadership was negatively associated with employee cyberloafing after accounting for nesting. Cyberloafing clustered within teams (intraclass correlation = 0.22), but agreement indices did not support a consensual team norm. Ethical leadership was negatively associated with coworker cyberloafing cues, which were positively associated with focal employees’ cyberloafing; the indirect association was negative across focal assignments, although the most conservative interval approached zero. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and cyberloafing was self-reported. Originality/value The study distinguishes coworkers’ reported behavior from shared norms and gives ABA a substantive explanatory role for employees’ digital behavior.

title: The broad reach of financial socialisation in the home
abstractText: Purpose This study examines whether cognitive ability, gender, socioeconomic status (SES), interest in finance and country context condition the association between parental financial socialisation and young adults' objective financial knowledge and subjective financial knowledge (financial confidence). By examining both outcomes together, the study addresses a gap concerning the boundary conditions of family financial socialisation. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on data from 353 university students across Australia, New Zealand and New Caledonia, objective financial knowledge was measured using a ten-item test and financial confidence using subjective financial knowledge. Parental financial socialisation was measured with the Parent Financial Socialisation Scale (PFSS). Ordinary least squares regressions and PROCESS Model 1 moderation tests incorporated fluid intelligence, approximate numeracy, cognitive reflection, gender, SES, financial-information engagement and country controls. Common-method-bias diagnostics were also conducted. Findings Parental financial socialisation was positively associated with both objective financial knowledge and financial confidence. Fluid intelligence, approximate numeracy and cognitive reflection were associated with objective financial knowledge, whereas only cognitive reflection among the cognitive measures was associated with financial confidence. Gender and engagement with financial information were associated with both outcomes. None of the cognitive, demographic, interest-based or country variables significantly moderated the PFSS relationships. Common-method-bias diagnostics did not indicate a material problem. Originality/value The study extends the family financial socialisation framework by testing multiple proposed boundary conditions in a multinational sample and by distinguishing objective knowledge from confidence. The absence of moderation suggests that the positive PFSS association is comparatively broad, while the differing predictor profiles for knowledge and confidence refine understanding of the pathways through which financial capability develops.

title: A new piece of the Butia archeri complex (Arecaceae)
abstractText: Background and aims – Butia archeri is a species complex from the Brazilian Central Plateau that comprises unresolved species. One of these populations, with collection records from the 1950s, has recently been documented on YouTube, prompting field surveys. Material and methods – Following standard methodology, the pinnae and flowers were analysed by using LM (free-hand transverse sections) and SEM. At this point we compared the morphoanatomy of the new species, Butia cerussa sp. nov., with that of B. archeri and the other recognized species of the complex. We made an identification key and an updated distribution map of the complex. Key results – Butia cerussa sp. nov. can be differentiated from B. archeri by a series of striking characters. Among these, congested light purple flowers stand out, as do pistillate and staminate flowers of distinct sizes. The white pulverulent aspect of the rachis and rachillae of the inflorescence is also a noticeable and unprecedented characteristic for the genus. Anatomically, there are also distinctive differences between B. cerussa sp. nov. and B. archeri , notably the absence of raphides and the fact that the accessory bundles do not surround the fibrous ring completely in the new species. Conclusion – Endemic to the Cerrado sensu stricto, its type population is located near charcoal-burning and mining activities, highlighting the urgency of recognizing the region as an area of occurrence for a previously unknown species.

title: Present but absent: workplace phubbing, relational resources and burnout-related states
abstractText: Purpose Phubbing (snubbing a conversational partner by attending to one’s smartphone) is prevalent in workplace interactions, yet its organisational correlates remain underexplored. Drawing on social exchange theory and the job demands-resources model, this study aims to examine whether being phubbed in workplace meetings is indirectly associated with burnout-related states through participative safety and perceived organisational support (POS). Design/methodology/approach In a naturalistic, time-proximal field survey, 373 employees completed validated measures immediately after a real 30-minute workplace meeting. Serial mediation was tested with PROCESS Model 6 (10,000 bootstrap samples). Findings Phubbing was reported in 84.2% of meetings, regardless of hierarchical relationship. Phubbing was associated with lower participative safety (β = −0.16), which was positively associated with POS (β = 0.55); POS was negatively associated with burnout-related states (β = −0.39). The serial indirect association was significant but small (b = 0.03, 95% CI [0.01, 0.05]); a direct association remained. The model explained 36.1% of the variance. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional, single-source design precludes causal inference, and scores reflect burnout-related states following a single meeting rather than chronic burnout. Practical implications Organisations can establish meeting-specific attention norms, leader modelling of device use, technology-check intervals and explicit exceptions for legitimate device use. Social implications The findings show how constant connectivity may erode the relational quality of everyday work interactions. Originality/value To the best of the author’s knowledge, this is the first study to test participative safety and POS as serial mediators between workplace phubbing and burnout-related states in a naturalistic meeting context.

title: Mechanical property degradation and thermal recovery of FDM-printed discontinuous carbon fiber-reinforced Onyx after moisture exposure
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to investigate the mechanical degradation caused by moisture absorption in FDM-printed discontinuous carbon fiber-reinforced nylon (Onyx) and evaluate the effectiveness of thermal recovery treatments, including conventional drying temperatures (80–150°C) and industrial Zortrax annealing cycles, in restoring mechanical performance. Design/methodology/approach The study subjected FDM-printed Onyx specimens to 24 h water immersion to induce moisture degradation. Recovery was then evaluated through controlled thermal treatments at temperatures ranging from 80°C to 150°C and through industrial Zortrax annealing profiles. Tensile testing, mass tracking during drying and scanning electron microscopy were used to assess mechanical recovery, moisture-removal kinetics and microstructural changes. Findings Moisture absorption significantly reduced yield strength and stiffness due to matrix plasticization. Thermal treatments successfully reversed much of this degradation. Higher temperatures (120–150°C) accelerated moisture removal and improved interlayer consolidation, especially near the glass transition temperature (∼114°C). Industrial annealing profiles produced the best mechanical recovery, achieving ultimate tensile strengths of approximately 90 MPa and outperforming standard 80°C drying. Scanning electron microscopy analysis confirmed improved interlaminar bonding after thermal treatment. Originality/value The study provides a practical framework for optimizing post-processing workflows for moisture-sensitive discontinuous carbon fiber-reinforced nylon composites. It demonstrates the effectiveness of industrial annealing profiles for restoring and enhancing mechanical performance in humid environments, addressing a gap in the understanding of standardized industrial thermal recovery strategies for FDM-printed Onyx.

title: Cross-Sectional Study of Multiple Sclerosis Nurse Care in Australia: Care Provision, Value, Estimated Avoided Costs, and Recommendations—Part 2
abstractText: Background: In Australia, multiple sclerosis specialist nurses (MSSNs) are an integral part of the multidisciplinary health care team; however, their numbers have decreased in recent years. Few data exist on the care MSSNs provide and the cost-saving measures associated with their services. Our aim was to describe the provision and value of MSSN care and to estimate potential avoided costs. Methods: Cross-sectional survey data on MSSN care (provider, length of care, contact frequency, consultation types and satisfaction, and support types) and perceived value and effects were collected in 2020 from 1417 Australians with MS. Descriptive analysis was used, and potential avoided costs were estimated. Results: (78%, 522 of 667). The most frequent support types related to information about and management of MS symptoms and treatments and their side effects. Not having MSSN care access would have resulted in more general practitioner (21.2%, 147 of 693) or neurologist (21.1%, 146 of 693) appointments and hospital visits (5.3%, 37 of 693). If those without access gained access, their associated health care costs would have been reduced by 10% or 20%, generating potential avoided costs of AU $74.7 million and AU $149.4 million in 2024, respectively. Conclusions: This cross-sectional study suggests that tailored MSSN services reduce the need for more costly care and that MSSN care is a highly cost-effective model of care.

title: Linking teaching excellence to organisational development in academia: opportunity or missed potential?
abstractText: Purpose Promotion in terms of teaching reward systems has increasingly been introduced in higher education organisations (universities), to recognise and reward teaching excellence. However, little attention has been given to if and how the competence of appointed teachers is organisationally used. Drawing on workplace learning (WPL) theory, this paper aims to critically analyse how a teaching reward system at a Swedish university is articulated and enacted in relation to organisational development. Design/methodology/approach The paper is based on a survey with open-ended questions, directed to all recognised and distinguished university teachers at one Swedish university (response rate 70%, n = 21), complemented with an analysis of institutional decision documents. With departure in WPL theory, the analysis focused on perceived alignment between individual competence and organisational development. Findings Although the formal objectives of the teaching reward system include contributing to educational quality development, findings indicate limited organisational integration following appointment. Respondents report unclear role expectations, little leadership communication and lack of structured follow-up. In particular, appointed teachers express absence of formal time allocation and explicit mandates constrains systematic sharing and collective use of these teachers’ pedagogical competence. Research limitations/implications The study contributes to WPL research by highlighting the relevance of WPL as a perspective for understanding academia as a work organisation, characterised by highly skilled and highly specialised employees operating in a highly competitive and hierarchical context. It also points to the need for further research on how teaching reward systems can be integrated into broader workplace learning and organisational development strategies in higher education. Practical implications If aspiring to gain optimal organisational output, higher education leadership needs to articulate role expectations and create structural conditions that enable organisational use of the pedagogical competence there is. Mirroring aspects of research-based promotion pathways may strengthen the legitimacy of teaching reward systems and further enhance their value as an academic career path. Originality/value There is a shortage of analyses of teaching reward systems through a perspective. Rather than focusing on individual competence development or reward, this paper examines how appointed teachers experience their pedagogical expertise being organisationally used after appointment. In doing so, it identifies a gap between formal recognition and organisational utilisation, highlighting an overlooked dimension of teaching reward systems in higher education.

title: Workplace health interventions in SMEs – experiences of employees performing as in-house facilitators
abstractText: Purpose Facilitation is a key factor in workplace health and organizational interventions. However, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) often lack the resources needed to access professional facilitation. The purpose of this study is to examine how in-house facilitators are experienced in workplace health interventions in SMEs and to identify the qualities that enable in-house facilitators to perform this facilitation role effectively as an alternative to engaging external facilitators or internal professional process consultants. Design/methodology/approach A multiple-case study approach was used across three Danish SMEs in the manufacturing and Information Technology sectors, each of which conducted two interventions. Each company appointed two in-house facilitators among employees who had no formal facilitator training. Data were collected over six months through FishBone, Chronological Workshops and interviews with employees, in-house facilitators and managers, followed by a completion survey. Findings The in-house facilitators supported the identification of workplace health issues and contributed with contextually relevant solutions. Besides demonstrating established facilitator competencies, participants highlighted two key characteristics: (1) contextual sensitivity; the ability to align actions with the organizational environment and participant needs and (2) creative problem-solving based on personal experience and interest, akin to the role of a bricoleur, reflecting agency and adaptability. These qualities positioned in-house facilitators as a viable, context-sensitive alternative to external consultants. Originality/value By leveraging employees' insider knowledge, relational trust and informal competencies, SMEs can strengthen organizational interventions and enhance employee well-being. The findings suggest that SMEs may hold untapped resources within their workplace to drive successful interventions.
venueName: International Journal of Workplace Health Management

title: Residential self-selection, housing allocation and neighbourhood social cohesion in Jordan: implications for socially sustainable residential development
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to examine whether informed residential self-selection is associated with neighbourhood social cohesion in Hanina, Madaba, Jordan. Design/methodology/approach An embedded mixed-methods design combines questionnaires with 358 household heads in public and private housing and interviews with six planners and decision-makers involved in public housing. Cohesion was assessed through participation, belonging, legitimacy, recognition and inclusion. Findings Residents reporting limited or no informed self-selection, whether through public-housing lottery allocation or private choice without prior neighbourhood information, reported significantly lower cohesion across all five dimensions. Self-selection and housing typology explained 16.3% of the variance in overall cohesion. Interviews showed that practitioners often viewed random allocation as procedurally fair and assumed socioeconomic homogeneity would generate cohesion, despite weak coordination and limited attention to social outcomes. Practical implications The findings support ranked preferences, transparent choice within eligibility constraints, access to non-identifying neighbourhood information, resident associations and stronger coordination between planning and housing institutions. Originality/value The article reframes residential self-selection as a substantive housing and planning variable, tests its association with five cohesion dimensions among 358 households and links the survey results to interviews with planners and decision-makers who design allocation procedures, in a developing-country public/private housing comparison.
venueName: International Journal of Housing Markets and Analysis

title: ‘They told us that she is a witch, that’s why we beat her’: 2 Timothy 1:7 and witchcraft accusation-related violence against women in Isuokoma, Nigeria
abstractText: This study examines 2 Timothy 1:7 in relation to the growing spate of witchcraft accusation-related violence (WARV) against women in Isuokoma, Nigeria. In Isuokoma, accusations of witchcraft are commonly directed at vulnerable women, particularly the elderly and widows, resulting in social exclusion, physical assault, psychological trauma and sometimes death. Such accusations are, in some cases, sustained by fear-driven narratives embedded within local cosmologies and reinforced in some Pentecostal and/or prophetic movements. Against this backdrop, the study explores how 2 Timothy 1:7, which emphasises that a believer’s life should not be governed by fear but by divine empowerment, can be reread to deconstruct these fear-based cultural and religious narratives that underpin WARV against women in Isuokoma. The study employed a lexical exegetical approach to reread the pericope, alongside in-depth interviews with women who have been accused of witchcraft, their family members and church leaders in Isuokoma. A purposive sampling technique guided the selection of nine participants, and the data were analysed qualitatively and presented thematically in the study. The study argued that a contextual rereading of 2 Timothy 1:7 can help to challenge narratives that sacralise fear and suspicion, and also foster a community characterised by spiritual courage, love and sound judgement. As part of the recommendations, the study highlights implications for safeguarding and pastoral practice, including trauma-informed care, community education, and other strategies aimed at enhancing the protection, psychosocial well-being, dignity and safety of women accused of witchcraft in Isuokoma. Contribution: This ethnographic study offers a theological framework and practical recommendations for challenging fear-driven narratives and supporting women who are often the victims of witchcraft accusations.

title: Exploring the relationship between consumer religiosity and perceptions of corporate social responsibility in tobacco companies: Does smoking status matter?
abstractText: Purpose Corporate social responsibility (CSR) has become an essential component of corporate strategy, aiming at improving social and environmental outcomes. It is increasingly recognized as a powerful tool for shaping public perceptions of businesses' fair treatment of employees and consumers, addressing social issues, profit orientation, and overall commitment to ethical practices. However, controversial industries are frequently accused of exploiting CSR initiatives. These range from the core “sin” sectors of tobacco, alcohol, and gambling to more contested categories such as fast food and fossil fuels. Such firms often establish their own permissive guidelines under the guise of social responsibility, potentially undermining genuine efforts for positive change. Tobacco, the most consistently classified sin industry, provides the focal context for this study. This study examines how different types of religiosity affect consumers' views on tobacco companies' CSR and their support for these companies, with consumer corporate identity (CCI) serving as a mediator. It also explores how smoking status moderates the relationship between religiosity and CCI. Design/methodology/approach Using a survey of consumers in Indonesia (n = 331), our findings reveal a complex relationship between consumers' religiosity, smoking status, and their perceptions of tobacco companies. Findings Intrinsic religiosity positively shaped CSR perceptions across four of five domains: employee, social, profit, and ethics, with no significant effect on consumer-focused initiatives. Smokers who are more likely to identify with tobacco companies were more inclined to support the CSR initiatives, even disregarding their detrimental effects on society. Extrinsically religious people also show a positive perception of CSR initiatives. In contrast, people with quest religiosity are more likely to question CSR initiatives. Originality/value This is one of the few papers that explores the impact of smoking status on perceptions of tobacco companies' CSR. The overall results have significant ethical implications for governments, religious leaders, and non-profit organizations working in this sector.
venueName: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics

title: Beyond the digital divide: algorithmic marginalisation in the age of AI
abstractText: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to examine how the advent of artificial intelligence (AI) may exacerbate the existing digital divide and create new forms of inequality, particularly among marginalised communities. Drawing on the Matthew effect, the paper explores how existing advantages in digital access, AI literacy and knowledge resources may accumulate over time, enabling privileged groups to benefit disproportionately from AI while further disadvantaging those already excluded. Design/methodology/approach This paper adopts a qualitative, conceptual methodology based on a critical review of the literature on the digital divide, digital equity, AI literacy and the Matthew effect. It also uses a conceptual figure to illustrate how AI-driven decisions, shaped by information available in online data sets, may be imposed on marginalised communities whose experiences and perspectives remain underrepresented in these data sets. Findings AI may deepen existing inequalities when digital data sets underrepresent the knowledge and experiences of marginalised communities. The Gujjar and Bakerwal communities of Jammu and Kashmir illustrate how such omissions can exclude them from AI-driven decision-making. Digital equity must therefore ensure not only access to technology but also meaningful representation in the knowledge systems shaping otherwise AI risks reinforcing the very inequalities it promises to overcome. Originality/value This paper is original and represents the authors’ own work. It offers a distinct perspective on the relationship between AI, the digital divide and the marginalisation of underrepresented communities.

title: Psychological safety, work-related flow and employee innovation: a person-centered test of voice profiles in India
abstractText: Purpose This study examines when perceived team psychological safety is associated with employees' innovative work behavior in India. Design/methodology/approach Using survey data from 318 full-time employees, the study applies latent profile analysis to identify employee voice profiles based on item-level indicators of promotive and prohibitive voice. Multigroup structural equation modeling is then used to test whether work-related flow links psychological safety to innovative work behavior, and whether this indirect association differs across voice profiles, using formal pairwise contrasts. Findings Psychological safety was positively associated with work-related flow, and flow was positively associated with innovative work behavior; psychological safety was indirectly associated with innovative work behavior through work-related flow, with a residual direct association also present. Three voice profiles, heuristically labelled Cautious Contributors, Moderate Engagers and Vocal Champions, emerged that differed in voice levels, demographic seniority and outcome levels. The indirect pathway was reliably positive within the Moderate Engager profile, though formal pairwise contrasts did not reliably detect profile differences in the pathway. Originality/value The study examines work-related flow as a theoretically proposed pathway consistent with the observed indirect association between psychological safety and employee innovation. Its person-centered contribution is a formal test that found limited evidence of voice-profile differences, illustrating why subgroup significance patterns alone should not be interpreted as boundary conditions. The Indian employee sample provides an empirical setting for future comparative research.

title: Evaluating the barriers to lean ımplementation for a manufacturing company using grey influence analysis (GINA)
abstractText: Purpose Lean manufacturing is a widely adopted philosophy for enhancing productivity, yet many organizations face significant barriers to implementation. This study aims to assess lean implementation barriers and analyses their causal interdependencies through a case study within a company operating in the production of industrial and construction machinery in Türkiye. Design/methodology/approach Ten barriers were identified and evaluated using the grey ınfluence analysis (GINA) methodology, leveraging data from an expert-response survey to map their causal structure. Furthermore, a MICMAC analysis was conducted to establish the hierarchical relationships among these barriers. Findings The findings indicate that lack of management strategy (B1), financial constraints (B5) and lack of incentives and motivation (B6) are the most significant driving factors, exerting the strongest causal influence on other barriers. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first study in the literature to apply the GINA method for the evaluation of lean implementation barriers, offering a new analytical approach for this domain globally and specifically within Türkiye.

title: Effect of physical, psychological and demographic factors of construction craft workers on hazard recognition performance and safety risk perception
abstractText: Purpose Despite advances in safety protocols, the construction industry still experiences high occupational injury rates, partly due to limitations in craft workers’ hazard recognition performance (HRP) and safety risk perception (SRP). However, prior research has largely examined antecedents of safety cognition in isolation, with limited attention to the combined effects of physical, psychological and demographic factors, including sleep quality, job stress, fatigue, education, experience and age. This study aims to examine the combined associations of physical (fatigue, sleep quality), psychological (job stress) and demographic (age, education, experience) factors to provide a more systemic understanding of safety cognition. Specifically, safety risk perception is operationalized through the Discrepancy in Safety Risk Perception Index, which measures the alignment or discrepancy between workers’ subjective risk assessments and an established expert-referenced benchmark. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional quantitative design was used, integrating structured surveys with image-based hazard identification tasks. Data were collected from 96 construction craft workers across 11 construction projects in Iran using validated instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to test the hypothesized direct and mediated pathways, with fatigue positioned as a central mediator. Findings The results indicate that higher fatigue is significantly associated with lower HRP and mediates the associations of poor sleep quality and high job stress on HRP. Furthermore, findings indicate that education and experience are positively associated with better HRP, while age was not significantly associated with HRP. Importantly, higher HRP is statistically associated with lower discrepancies between workers’ and experts’ risk perceptions. Practical implications These findings provide practical recommendations for safety management, based on the observed associations between human factors and safety cognition. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature by empirically examining a systemic model that integrates antecedent factors into the cognitive process of safety, with fatigue acting as a critical linkage. Unlike studies that examine factors in isolation, this research provides a holistic framework for understanding the associations between physical and psychological conditions and safety performance.

title: Coordinated dual layer volt-var control for power distribution systems with electric vehicles and distributed generations
abstractText: Renewable distributed generators (DGs) such as solar PVs, and vehicle-to-grid technology (V2G) are gaining traction in the power distribution sector to ensure energy security. However, renewable DGs exhibit intermittency that can cause rapid voltage fluctuations leading to frequent switching when performing voltage regulation using conventional feeder control devices such as on-load tap changers (OLTC) and capacitor banks (CB). The frequent switching can bring about increased equipment operation and maintenance costs. This issue of voltage regulation can be addressed through the 4-quadrant smart inverters functions of DGs and electric vehicles (EVs). Hence, this paper proposes a dual layer control method aimed at mitigating rapid voltage fluctuations to reduce switching operations for the feeder voltage regulating devices. Moreover, it also optimizes the reactive power operation of the inverters with the aim of reducing the aging rate of the inverters. The efficacy of the proposed method is demonstrated through a modified IEEE 123-bus system by obtaining minimized voltage deviation, optimized reactive power consumption/generation of DGs to reduce inverter aging, and optimized charging/discharging of EVs for voltage regulation.
venueName: International Journal of Emerging Electric Power Systems

title: Family feeding environment, food insecurity, and their associations with undernutrition and overnutrition among Indonesian school-aged children
abstractText: INTRODUCTION: The double burden of malnutrition (DBM), the coexistence of stunting and overweight/obesity, has emerged as a growing concern among school-aged children in low-and middle-income countries, yet remains poorly understood. The present study aimed to examine how family feeding environments, food insecurity, and dietary behaviours are associated with undernutrition and overnutrition in an Indonesian population undergoing rapid nutrition transition. METHODS: This cross-sectional study involved 161 children and 116 parents across three districts in South Sulawesi. Data on dietary intake, nutritional status, feeding practices, and household food insecurity were collected using structured questionnaires, FFQ, and HFIAS. Nutritional status was assessed using BMI-for-age and height-for-age z-scores. Associations were examined using descriptive statistics, correlations, and exploratory multivariate logistic regression. RESULTS: Children had low fruit and vegetable (median 127 g/day) intake and high consumption of SSB and UPF (149.5 mL/day and 116 g/day, respectively). Overweight/obesity (OWOB) affected 52.2 % and stunting 29.2 %; 4.3 % had both. Parent-reported feeding practices showed a limited association with children's dietary intake. Food insecurity was prevalent (54 %). In exploratory adjusted models, moderate food insecurity (aOR=7.51; 95 % CI: 1.14-66.76) and residence in Takalar or Makassar compared with Maros were associated with higher odds of OWOB, whereas female sex was associated with lower odds. Stunting was associated with female sex (aOR=3.79; 95 % CI: 1.28-13.08) and residence in Maros, but not with food insecurity. CONCLUSIONS: Children's diets remained poor despite generally positive parent-reported feeding practices, which may reflect broader environmental influences. The differing correlates of OWOB and stunting highlight the need for tailored, context-specific interventions aiming at improving diet quality and food environments. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in larger longitudinal studies integrating dietary, environmental, and biological data. Despite generally positive feeding practices reported by parents, children's diets remained poor, which may reflect broader environmental influences.

title: Shock-driven evolution of a hydrogenated amorphous carbon analog: Pathways to small hydrocarbons, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and fullerenes
abstractText: Hydrogenated amorphous carbon (HAC) is ubiquitous in the interstellar medium (ISM). However, the contribution of shock-processed HAC to the formation of large carbonaceous molecules, including polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and fullerenes, remains largely unexplored. In this work, we examined the chemical products and transformations associated with shock processing of HAC particles by investigating the gaseous volatiles and solid residues . We used polystyrene (PS) as a proxy for HAC. produced We a pressure-driven shock tube to heat PS particles to employed ∼ 4000,K. We monitored the time-dependent shock processing of PS in situ using optical emission spectroscopy. We further analyzed the gaseous products with the help of gas chromatography. We collected the solid residues and analyzed them ex situ using a variety of methods including infrared microspectroscopy, Raman microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and laser desorption ionization mass spectrometry. molecular dynamics and chemical kinetic modeling, the experimental findings. We performed simulations which support Shock processing induces rapid heating, during which extensive dehydrogenation and fragmentation of PS occur, accompanied by the release of H_2 and small hydrocarbons. From this hot chemistry, a diversity of large molecular species, including PAHs, emerges. An H-poor solid material that contains graphitic structures is produced during cooling. The shock-induced thermal processing of HAC involves both top-down and bottom-up mechanisms that generate small hydrocarbons, PAHs, and fullerenes. The rapid destruction of HAC-like material, followed by molecular reassembly, offers a plausible explanation for the coexistence of abundant small hydrocarbons and a variety of carbonaceous dust species, including PAHs , in the ISM.

title: An information intervention combined with a behavioral cue to reduce food waste in a university canteen: a field experiment
abstractText: Purpose There is a growing need for systematic food waste intervention studies that combine survey-based measures of psychological constructs with objective plate waste data collected over extended periods. This study aims to address this gap through a three-month field experiment in a university canteen, complemented by pre- and post-intervention surveys. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of an informational intervention, including a behavioral cue, on internal psychological constructs and actual behavior, measured in terms of plate waste. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a real-world quasi-experimental field design conducted in a university canteen. The intervention consisted of an information-based nudging campaign incorporating a behavioral cue that encouraged canteen users to request smaller portion sizes. The intervention aimed to increase awareness of food waste and reduce actual plate waste. To assess these effects, surveys were administered before and after the intervention across three measurement periods. The survey instrument was grounded in the theory of planned behavior and captured key psychological drivers related to food waste behavior. Findings Overall, average plate waste per person decreased by 58% from 33.32 g during the initial premeasurement phase in March to 14.12 g during the intervention phase in June. However, only a 9% reduction (1.30 g) can be directly attributed to the nudging intervention itself, as a substantial 53% reduction had already occurred before its implementation, likely as a result of survey-induced awareness. Survey data further indicate that the intervention increased both awareness of food waste and perceived behavioral control among canteen users. However, intentions to reduce food waste and self-reported plate waste behaviors remained unchanged. These findings point to both an intention–behavior gap and the susceptibility of self-reports to social desirability and reporting biases, highlighting the need to measure actual plate waste in field experiments to identify intervention effects. Research limitations/implications This study has several limitations. First, the mechanisms underlying the observed reduction in plate waste could not be identified, as data on portion-size choices and menu selection were not available for all canteen users throughout the intervention. Second, a reduction in food waste would not necessarily represent a sustainable outcome if it were simply achieved through increased caloric intake. Third, the baseline and intervention survey samples differed in size and composition, partly because the intervention coincided with the examination period. Finally, the study was conducted in a single university canteen, limiting the generalisability of the findings. Practical implications The results suggest that simple, low-cost behavioral interventions, combining awareness messages with behavioral cues, can be easily integrated into existing institutional food services and contribute to reducing food waste without requiring substantial financial investment or major changes to current practices. Therefore, universities and food service providers could consider incorporating similar interventions into their sustainability initiatives, alongside measures such as promoting appropriate portion sizes and regularly monitoring food waste. These results also have broader policy relevance, as they support the integration of food waste prevention strategies into institutional sustainability policies and contribute to achieving sustainable development goals12 on responsible consumption and production. Social implications Final consumers play a significant role in the generation of food waste along the supply chain. Actively involving them is therefore essential for achieving food waste reduction and broader sustainability goals. The survey results indicate that university canteen users are already highly aware of food waste issues, suggesting strong potential for participatory approaches. Involving users in codeveloping strategies may thus represent an effective and inclusive initiative for food service providers. Originality/value The originality of this study lies in the integration of survey-based psychological measures with objective plate waste data collected during a three-month field experiment in a university canteen. By linking awareness and intentions to observed behavior in a real-life setting, the findings advance understanding of the awareness–behavior relationship and provide practical value for universities and food service providers seeking low-cost food waste reduction strategies.

title: Effect of Structured Preceptor Education on Preceptor Self-Assessed Capability and Competency
abstractText: BACKGROUND: Preceptor Education Programs (PEPs) play a vital role in preparing nurses to mentor newly hired nurses by serving as role models, teachers, and evaluators. This study evaluated the impact of a structured PEP on registered nurse (RN) preceptors' self-assessed role capabilities and competencies. METHOD: Of 142 eligible RNs, 99 completed the study. The structured PEP included online Mosby's Preceptor 3.0 modules, an in-person class, and pre- and post-assessments using the modified Preceptors' Orientation Competence Instrument). RESULTS: Participants were predominantly female (87.9%), with a mean age of 36.2 years. Most had been employed at the Medical Center for less than 3 years (65.6%), and 83.8% had never participated in formal preceptor education. Reported barriers included inadequate knowledge (27.3%) and lack of time (24.2%). Significant differences were found in six Preceptors' Orientation Competence Instrument domains. CONCLUSION: A structured PEP was effective in enhancing RN preceptors' self-assessed role capabilities and competencies.

title: A t - SNE approach to visualising scenario-dependent coherent generator clusters
abstractText: A novel data-driven method for identifying coherent generators in power systems following a significant disturbance is proposed in this paper. For the analysis of post-disturbance generator dynamics, the t-distributed Stochastic Neighbour Embedding (t-SNE) algorithm is utilised, with explicit account taken of the pre-disturbance operating point and the specific location of the disturbance, factors often overlooked by traditional linearised methods. Validation of the technique is performed on a dynamic equivalent of the Mexican Interconnected System (MIS) under varying load conditions. From the results, it is demonstrated that the identified coherent groups are susceptible to disturbance location, a critical insight for accurate transient stability assessment and dynamic model reduction. The framework is intended as an off-line analysis and planning tool. An initial assessment of noise resilience on the IEEE 118-bus system indicates that the integrity of the angle-based embedding is maintained at signal-to-noise ratios as low as 20 dB, while susceptibility to noise is exhibited by the speed-based embedding. A two-level framework is delineated, in which a reference library of embeddings is constructed during the off-line analysis, and new disturbances are assigned to the most similar reference scenario during the online phase, without t-SNE being re-executed.

title: Co-caring consumer socialisation: adolescents’ perspectives on sustainable eating
abstractText: Purpose This paper aims to examine adolescents’ perspectives on their experiences of agency in shifting family food consumption towards greater sustainability. Design/methodology/approach This study draws on 20 interviews with 26 Danish adolescents on family dietary practices using innovative, engaging tools embedded in in-depth, semi-structured interviews. Findings The adolescents interviewed revealed a paradoxical “climate pragmatism”; although aware of sustainability issues related to food consumption, they preferred to adhere to (unsustainable) family eating habits. Family negotiations were characterised by “family diplomacy”, with consumer decisions based on dialogue, consensus, mutual care and the inclusion of all family members in what we term “co-caring consumer socialisation”. Adolescents were unwilling to push green consumer practices unless other family members supported them. Co-caring consumer socialisation, thus, plays an ambivalent role in the green transition. It gives adolescents a voice in family consumption, however, climate pragmatism and family diplomacy keep them from using that voice to drive change. Transforming family food consumption towards more climate-friendly food practices, therefore, remains a challenge. Research limitations/implications The findings of this study demonstrate that studies of family consumption should approach the family as a co-caring unit, in which care is jointly produced through family members’ consumption practices. This study draws on a sample of adolescents from primarily middle-class, White, Danish families and future research should investigate co-caring consumer socialisation in sustainable eating and beyond in families of different compositions and origin. Practical implications Emphasising taste, health and well-being seems to be a more relevant argument for adolescents than climate protection. Social implications Adolescents do not seem to lack information about climate issues, and therefore, expectations that pro-environmental education in schools will result in a greening of households will not be fulfilled. On the contrary, the results of this study indicate that adolescents, who have practical experience with green eating in contexts where it is seen as the norm, are powerful in changing behaviour towards more sustainable family food consumption. Originality/value This article contributes to the marketing literature by unfolding the concept of “co-caring consumer socialisation” in family decision-making practices which goes beyond “reverse consumer socialisation”.

title: Biomass-enabled metal−organic framework-based macroarchitectural materials with advanced applications
abstractText: Purpose The rising global demand for energy, together with the environmental pressures linked to industrial growth, has made sustainable green development a global priority. This review focuses on biomass-enabled MOF macroarchitectures as an important class of sustainable porous materials. Design/methodology/approach This review focuses on three main aspects: fabrication strategies, structure–property relationships (dimensions) and advanced applications. It covers key synthesis routes such as templating, interfacial assembly and reaction confinement, while showing how biomass components such as cellulose, lignin and chitosan influence material formation and performance. The review also explains how pore hierarchy, interface design, surface chemistry, transport pathways and mechanical stability determine the final properties of these systems. Findings By combining the tuneable structure and functionality of MOFs with the renewability, hierarchical architecture and easy processability of biomass, these materials address major drawbacks of conventional MOF powders, especially poor shape control, weak mechanical strength, limited mass transfer and difficult device integration. Their growing applications in adsorption, catalysis, environmental cleanup, energy storage and drug delivery are highlighted. Current challenges include large-scale production, interface control, durability and limited mechanistic understanding. Originality/value The article points to future directions for designing application-oriented biomass-enabled MOF macroarchitectures. These materials are expected to become a key platform for scalable and high-performance next-generation technologies.

title: Reframing physical activity in migration: a qualitative study of Iranian female students through the COM-B model
abstractText: Purpose Migrant women frequently encounter social, cultural and structural barriers that shape their engagement in health-promoting behaviours such as physical activity. The purpose of this qualitative study was to explore perceived barriers and facilitators to physical activity among Iranian female international students living in Italy, using the capability, opportunity, motivation-behaviour (COM-B) model as a guiding framework. Design/methodology/approach Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 25 Iranian female international students enrolled at a university in Northern Italy. Data were analysed using deductive thematic analysis, with the COM-B model providing the analytical framework for coding and theme development. Findings Physical opportunity emerged as the most prominent source of barriers, particularly time constraints related to academic demands, financial costs and limited access to culturally appropriate facilities. In contrast, social opportunity and reflective motivation were identified as key facilitators, highlighting the importance of social support, exposure to active lifestyles and conscious evaluations of health and functional benefits. Automatic motivation showed an ambivalent pattern, with positive emotions encouraging participation and negative affective responses discouraging it. Psychological and physical capability were less frequently perceived as limiting factors. Originality/value This study provides qualitative evidence on how migration-related social, cultural and contextual conditions shape physical activity among Iranian female international students living in Italy. By applying the COM-B model, the findings contribute to the migrant health literature, demonstrating how the interaction between opportunity, motivation and capability influences health-promoting behaviours. Ultimately, these insights suggest that health interventions should prioritise reducing structural barriers rather than focusing exclusively on individual motivation.

title: Inclusive Excellence Training for Nurses: Awareness Does Not Equate to Action
abstractText: BACKGROUND: Nurses have an ethical obligation to address bias and prejudice, yet a considerable number experience workplace racism and microaggressions, negatively impacting well-being and patient care. Inclusive excellence training is frequently conducted to increase awareness in recognizing microaggressions. Research on inclusive excellence training for nurses is limited, emphasizing the need to improve its effectiveness in addressing microaggressions. METHOD: An exploratory, qualitative research design with individual interviews was used to explore the impact of inclusive excellence training on nurses' ability to recognize and respond to microaggressions and training recommendations. RESULTS: Four themes emerged: (1) training delivery and design; (2) relational and contextual factors in learning; (3) sustained change and implementation; and (4) barriers to action. CONCLUSION: Effectiveness of inclusive excellence training depends on bridging four critical gaps: delivery; context; sustainability; and action. Moreover, engagement with content and personal/work climate change requires meaningful dialogue among those interacting in the clinical setting.

title: Exploring the transformation towards a learning organization in practice: applying the Theory of Change framework in a Dutch nursing home
abstractText: Purpose This study explores how actors in a nursing home organization perceive the transformation into a learning organization and the outcomes they aim to achieve. The study offers practical insight into learning-oriented transformation in long-term care. Design/methodology/approach We conducted a qualitative single-case study in a Dutch nursing home that aimed to become a learning organization. Using the Theory of Change framework, semi-structured interviews were held with care professionals (n = 21) and managerial staff (n = 12). An inductive thematic analysis identified the intended impact, outcomes, activities, and contextual factors shaping the transformation. Findings Both interview groups viewed improvements in quality of care and quality of life as the intended impact of becoming a learning organization. Respondents associated learning organization transformation with a shared vision, supportive leadership, psychological safety, an adaptive and responsive culture, behavior and capabilities, and collaboration within and beyond the nursing home. These elements were perceived as important for enabling learning and alignment with shared organizational goals. Practical implications The findings highlight the need for integrated approaches where nursing home leaders actively engage care professionals in the transformation towards a learning organization. In addition, the identified capabilities may facilitate integrated care through collaboration within and across organizational boundaries. Originality/value Using a Theory of Change approach, this study provides empirically grounded insight into how actors perceive and shape a learning organization in practice. In doing so, it helps bridge the gap between conceptual understandings and workplace realities.
