title: Effects of temperature and pH on early degradation of anion exchange membranes
abstractText: The degradation of anion exchange membranes (AEMs) remains a major limitation to the broader deployment of membrane-based electrochemical devices. Although the operating conditions known to promote membrane deterioration are broadly recognized, the specific operating regimes and timescales that initiate degradation have not been resolved. This uncertainty hinders the definition of operational windows that are required to achieve stable and efficient membrane utilization. This work examines two degradation protocols representative of electrodialysis operating environments: thermal exposure and alkaline exposure, investigated both independently and in combination. In contrast to prior studies centered on extended operation (>2 years), the present analysis targets short exposure intervals (≤1, 24, and 48 h). The impact of these conditions was quantified through measurements of ionic conductivity, ion exchange capacity, electron microscopy, and spectroscopic analyses. Both temperature and alkaline exposure result in a continuous decrease in membrane conductivity through distinct electrochemical responses. Alkaline conditions decrease conductivity and shift the phase angle in Bode analysis toward values approaching zero, consistent with predominantly resistive behavior. In contrast, thermal exposure decreases conductivity while maintaining a nearly constant phase angle, indicating retention of capacitive contributions. These observations indicate that alkaline conditions induce a decrease in the magnitude of double-layer and diffusion boundary layer capacitances, reflected in the shift of the phase angle toward resistive behavior. When combined, elevated pH exerts a greater influence on degradation than temperature alone. Time-resolved measurements revealed a continuous, approximately linear increase in resistivity within the first hour, demonstrating that degradation initiates immediately upon exposure. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) reveals surface morphological deterioration, while infrared spectroscopy indicates chemical transformation of functional groups. These findings demonstrate that degradation processes are activated at early operational stages, requiring precise control of initial operating conditions in electrodialysis systems to limit performance decay.

title: Information management and decision-making in child and adolescent mental health services in a low-resource healthcare setting
abstractText: Purpose Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) in low-resource healthcare settings face workforce shortages, structural barriers and fragmented information systems. Little is known about how CAMHS professionals use information to support operational and tactical decision-making. This study describes how CAMHS professionals manage and use information to support decision-making in a low-resource CAMHS setting. Design/methodology/approach A descriptive qualitative study was conducted using two in-person focus group discussions with 17 CAMHS professionals. Participants were selected through purposive sampling, and data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. The interview guide was informed by the Descriptive Model of Decision-Making Levels and Information Management in Hospitals. Findings were discussed in relation to the World Health Organization's Global Strategy on Digital Health (2020–2025). Findings The analysis developed three themes: (1) foundational conditions shaping information-driven decision-making in CAMHS; (2) workforce capacity and role-specific health information system (HIS) use; and (3) alignment between HIS and real-world care delivery and decision-making. Strengthening information-driven decision-making in CAMHS requires reliable infrastructure, system-level governance, role-specific workforce capacity building and people-centred system design. Informal practices, such as verbal follow-up, printed records, spreadsheets and messaging platforms, played an important role in maintaining information flow when formal systems were incomplete, inaccessible or poorly aligned with daily work. Originality/value This study is among the first to explore how CAMHS professionals manage and use information in a low-resource CAMHS setting. It offers insight into how infrastructure, governance, workforce capacity, informal practice and system design shape operational and tactical decision-making. These insights can inform context-appropriate information systems and information governance strategies.

title: Irradiated reactor graphite: experimental characterization – insights from German research reactors
abstractText: A detailed radiochemical characterization was conducted on irradiated graphite samples from two German research reactors: the FRJ-2 (Jülich) and the TRIGA Mainz. The investigation combined non-destructive autoradiography and gamma-ray spectrometry with destructive sample oxidation and subsequent liquid scintillation counting to determine the specific activities of key activation products, including 60 Co, 152 Eu, 154 Eu, 3 H, and 14 C. As there is no sufficient information on trace element concentrations from the time of manufacturing available, good radioanalytical characterization is required to scale simulation result of radionuclide inventories. For both sample types, the apparent activation shown by gamma dose rates was rather low. Marked differences in radionuclide inventories were observed between the two graphite types, attributable to variations in material composition, operational history, and neutron flux profiles. Localized hotspots within the graphite were systematically analyzed, revealing spatial inhomogeneities in activity distribution. For the beta emitters, statistical evaluation demonstrated that targeted subsampling of fragments can significantly improve measurement precision without biasing the mean activity values. With increasing distance from the reactor core activities decreased e.g. for tritium in samples of TRIGA Mainz from 1,400 ± 84 to 7.0 ± 5.1 Bq/g and for 14 C from 127 ± 8 to 2.5 ± 1.4 Bq/g, and for tritium in FRJ-2 samples from 1.1E6 ± 4.0E4 to 4.1E4 ± 1.6E3 Bq/g and for 14 C from 3.2E4 ± 1.1E3 to 1.5E3 ± 7.9E1 Bq/g. Similar trends are observed for the gamma emitting radionuclides. These results highlight the importance of robust sampling strategies in radiological inventory assessments and provide benchmark data for future waste characterization, safety evaluations, modeling of irradiated graphite, and decontamination planning.

title: Plasma D- and L-2-hydroxyglutarate during vorasidenib treatment of isocitrate dehydrogenase-mutant glioma: development and validation of an enantioselective LC–MS/MS assay
abstractText: Objectives Mutant forms of isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 and 2 (IDH1/2) produce D-2-hydroxyglutarate (D-2-HG), which may serve as a circulating marker of biochemical target engagement during treatment with vorasidenib, an oral, brain-penetrant inhibitor of mutant IDH1/2. We aimed to develop an enantioselective LC-MS/MS assay for plasma D-2-HG and L-2-HG and evaluate its ability to detect longitudinal pharmacodynamic changes during treatment. Methods We developed an LC-MS/MS assay for plasma D-2-HG and L-2-HG using protein precipitation, diacetyl-L-tartaric anhydride derivatization, reversed-phase separation, isotope-labeled internal standards, and stripped-serum surrogate calibration. Analytical performance was evaluated over the 6.75–2,030 nmol/L measuring interval. The assay was applied to baseline, 3-month, and 6-month samples from 36 patients with IDH -mutant grade 2 glioma receiving vorasidenib. Results Both enantiomers were baseline-resolved within a 10-min run. The lower limit of quantification was 6.75 nmol/L. Relative error remained within ±15 % at all calibration levels, and short-term between-run CVs in plasma-based QC materials were 2.3–5.7 %. Median D-2-HG decreased from 265 nmol/L (IQR, 223–305) at baseline to 121 nmol/L (IQR, 95–160) at 3 months and 128 nmol/L (IQR, 82–174) at 6 months. Model-estimated concentrations were 53.3 % lower at 3 months and 53.8 % lower at 6 months than at baseline, with no difference between follow-up visits (p=0.88). L-2-HG showed no significant time effect (p=0.53). Conclusions The assay provided sensitive, reproducible, enantiomer-specific quantification of plasma 2-HG and detected early, sustained D-2-HG suppression during vorasidenib treatment. It supports pharmacodynamic assessment of mutant IDH inhibition. External validation and studies relating metabolite changes to clinical outcomes are needed before broader clinical implementation.

title: Origami-based deployable, programmable and reconfigurable structures in civil engineering
abstractText: Origami originates from an ancient art. It has inspired structures that are deployable, programmable and reconfigurable, offering tunable properties and multiple functionalities. In civil engineering, conventional construction involving large quantities of on-site work often leads to long construction periods, environmental pollution and high energy consumption. Although precast structures have been widely adopted, transporting large-scale precast components incurs significant costs. Deployable structures with high-ratio packaging capabilities and ease of fabrication can help address this issue. Moreover, enhancing seismic and impact resistance remains a key research focus for ensuring structural safety under extreme loads. Compared with traditional structures, origami-based structures are reconfigurable and programmable, exhibiting tunable properties and multiple functionalities and demonstrating excellent load-carrying and energy-absorption capacity. However, applying paper-folding principles to metre-scaled structural components still faces several challenges. This paper reviews existing research on the mechanical properties of origami structures and examines their feasibility in civil engineering. Potential applications include seismic and impact resistance, foldable shelters, modular structures, building energy efficiency, damage detection and health monitoring. The challenges and future prospects of origami in civil engineering are also discussed. Origami structures have promising application prospects in areas such as post-disaster rapid reconstruction, deployable bridges and protective structures.
venueName: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Civil Engineering

title: Effects of Interactive Ebook Training on Urinary Catheterization on Knowledge, Skills, and Learning Motivation of Novice Nurses
abstractText: BACKGROUND: Supporting novice nurses during the transition to practice is an important goal of continuing nursing education. Interactive ebooks may enhance learning by providing flexible, engaging, and multimedia-based training. METHOD: This quasi-experimental study compared interactive ebook training focused specifically on urinary catheterization and related perineal care with traditional instruction for 100 novice nurses at a medical center in Taiwan. Knowledge, skills, and learning motivation were measured before and after the intervention. RESULTS: Postintervention knowledge, skills, and learning motivation improved in both groups. The interactive ebook group showed significantly better posttest outcomes than the control group. CONCLUSION: Interactive ebook training on urinary catheterization shows promise as a continuing education approach to strengthen clinical learning outcomes for novice nurses.
venueName: The Journal of Continuing Education in Nursing

title: Waste-Derived Zwitterionic Bacterial Cellulose Membranes with Enhanced Silica and Scaling Control for Sustainable Nanofiltration Pretreatment
abstractText: Bacterial cellulose (BC) membranes were engineered via kombucha fermentation with the incorporation of polyethylene glycol (PEG-600 and PEG-1000, 1–2%, w/v) to tailor pore formation and enhance structural stability. Subsequently, the BC membrane was functionalized with chitosan polyampholyte (CPA) to introduce zwitterionic properties for fouling mitigation. The incorporation of 2% PEG-1000 enhances BC production and mechanical properties, with elongation increasing from 20.3% to 49.7%. The zwitterionic modification leads to reduced pore size and altered surface morphology of BC membrane. The zwitterionic CPA-BC membrane exhibits effective pretreatment performance, achieving accumulated removals of 45% for soluble silica, 35% for calcium (Ca2+), and 19% for sulfate (SO42–), while maintaining a stable flux of 20 L m–2 h–1 over 17 h. CPA-BC pretreatment mitigates surface fouling of the commercial nanofiltration (NF) membrane, as evidenced by optical coherence tomography (OCT) and digital image processing, which reveal reduced surface coverage from 99.4% to 64.8%. This contributes to reducing the rapid flux decline observed with pretreatment, from 42 L m–2 h–1 at 2 h to 29 L m–2 h–1 at 17 h, compared to a rapid decline to 7 L m–2 h–1 within 2 h without pretreatment. The findings demonstrate the technical potential of waste-derived zwitterionic BC membranes to offer an effective and sustainable pretreatment strategy for controlling silica fouling and scaling, enabling improved stability and performance of desalination systems.

title: Wounds that speak: addressing linguistic racism through arts-based autoethnography and emotional praxis
abstractText: While recent TESOL scholarship has explored racially minoritized educators’ emotions, less attention has been paid to how racial trauma might be navigated through arts-based auto-ethnography. Addressing the need for theoretical frameworks to better understand Asian immigrant educators’ emotions, this conceptual paper proposes a healing-centered model of emotional praxis that integrates a combination of Asian critical race theory, affect theory, and decolonial aesthesis. Drawing from a vignette, I examine how emotional praxis can address the embodied and affective dimensions of linguistic racism. Through collaborative art making, I explore three recursive moments of healing, namely re-membering, re-worlding, and re-connecting. Re-membering involves transforming racial trauma into visible counterstories against institutional whiteness. Re-worlding reconfigures racialized emotions through artistic practice. Re-connecting focuses on collective healing that embraces embodied and relational forms of knowledge making. This paper re-envisions arts-based practices as a site for emotional praxis, where teacher educators can transform experiences of racial trauma into emotional resistance.

title: Evolution of drying shrinkage cracks in concrete: a quantitative study based on digital image analysis
abstractText: Early-age drying shrinkage cracking can substantially weaken concrete durability. Conventional restrained shrinkage test devices and traditional crack-detection techniques have limitations in characterising the spatiotemporal evolution of full-surface cracks in large slab specimens. In this study, a dynamic crack-quantification method integrating OpenCV-based pre-processing and the YoloV5-seg segmentation model was developed. Restrained slab specimens of size 600 mm × 600 mm × 60 mm were used for single-sided drying tests, and three-zone and five-zone partitioning schemes were adopted to quantify zonal cracking characteristics. The effects of the water/binder (w/b) ratio, silica fume (SF) and slag (SG) replacement levels, ambient temperature and internal restraint configuration on cracking behaviour were quantitatively investigated. The results showed that reducing the w/b ratio increased final cracking severity and led to centrally concentrated cracking, but delayed initial crack formation within the tested range. SF increased early-age cracking risk, whereas SG delayed crack onset and promoted a more homogeneous spatial crack distribution. Elevated-temperature exposure shortened the initial cracking time and induced multi-stage abrupt crack growth, while X-type internal reinforcement exhibited better crack-mitigation performance than grid-shaped J-type internal restraint.

title: Effectiveness of a Clinical Nursing Preceptor Teaching Program Based on the WHO Nurse Educator Core Competencies Framework
abstractText: BACKGROUND: Preceptors play a vital role in nursing instruction, and their competencies need improvement to enhance teaching effectiveness. METHOD: A convergent mixed-methods design was used. Researchers developed a teaching program based on the World Health Organization Nurse Educator Core Competencies (NECC) framework. Self-repeating measurements were used to assess the effectiveness of the teaching program. One-to-one semi-structured interviews were conducted to obtain more details about the teaching program. RESULTS: The teaching program had 37 participants, and the interviews had 14. The results showed that the teaching program led to a statistically significant improvement in the overall core competencies of the participants. Seven of the eight subdimensions also showed statistically significant improvement. Three themes were identified from the interviews: benefits, challenges, and suggestions. CONCLUSION: The results showed the effectiveness of program, which aligned with the World Health Organization NECC framework in enhancing the competencies of clinical nursing preceptors and can inform further research on support strategies for clinical education.

title: Polyimide-Encapsulated Ag/Aramid-Reinforced Graphene Aerogel for Ultrasensitive and Fatigue-Resistant Wearable Motion Sensing
abstractText: Graphene aerogel (GA) combines ultralow density, high porosity, excellent conductivity, and mechanical tunability, making it ideal for piezoresistive sensing. However, achieving both high sensitivity and robust mechanical performance remains challenging. Herein, we report a flexible pressure sensor based on a hierarchical PI/Ag@AFs/GA composite: polyimide (PI) fibers reinforce the GA scaffold, preserving porosity while enhancing structural integrity; silver-coated aramid fibers (Ag@AFs) are interwoven into the GA network, forming a percolating conductive pathway that lowers electron transport resistance. The resulting sensor delivers high sensitivity (7.63 kPa-1), rapid response/recovery (385/386 ms), and exceptional compressive strength (153 kPa at 90% strain). It enables reliable human motion monitoring and tactile signal transmission, underscoring its potential for applications in electronic skin, wearable health electronics, and soft robotics.

title: Foundations for MetNet : A Proposed Framework for Modeling Metaphorical Productivity
abstractText: An adequate computational treatment of metaphor requires a representational model that captures its cross-domain, productive nature. Existing approaches and resources fall short: (i) ontological models of general meaning representation, such as WordNet, ConceptNet, BabelNet, and OntoLex, treat concepts atomically, omitting the event structure needed to capture contextual variation; (ii) distributional models (e.g., Word2Vec, BERT) encode metaphorical patterns only implicitly, offering little interpretive insight; (iii) metaphor-specific resources such as MetaNet typically pre-encode mappings rather than deriving them from independent structure, or emphasize ontological (Framester, Amnestic Forgery) or pragmatic (MetCL) representation instead. Although FrameNet – encoding events (frames) and participant roles (frame elements) to support systematic cross-domain alignment – offers a promising foundation, existing approaches built on it leave the underlying linguistic mechanism unaccounted for. In this paper, we review these models and resources to motivate the need for a new theoretical approach to capture this linguistic – and thus systemic – metaphorical mechanism, MetNet , a theoretical framework that refines FrameNet for metaphor modeling through a dedicated reasoning engine, specified through four core tenets: lexical frames, providing the structured, role-based representations over which mappings are established; abstract frames, narrowing the space of plausible candidate pairs; constraints, determining whether a given candidate mapping is admissible; and a mappability scale, grading admitted mappings by the density of their preserved relational structure. Our approach rests on two premises: (i) metaphor should be modeled analogically, as mappings between non-metaphorical frames; and (ii) evaluating such mappings requires a framework capable of encoding graded alignment constraints.

title: Values, risk perceptions and pro-environmental behaviour among university students: evidence from Indonesian higher education
abstractText: Purpose This study examined value-based, risk-cognitive and normative antecedents of pro-environmental behaviour (PEB) among Indonesian university students by integrating value–belief–norm theory, protection motivation theory and the theory of planned behaviour. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey of 614 undergraduates from 16 Indonesian universities was analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM), with predictive validity assessed through the cross-validated predictive ability test (CVPAT). Findings Of the 16 direct paths tested, 11 were significant. Pro-environmental intention predicted PEB with a large effect, which was strongest in the model. Injunctive norms and perceived behavioural control were the leading predictors of intention. Altruistic values predicted attitude and biospheric values predicted intention directly. Both anthropocentric and ecocentric risk perceptions significantly predicted attitudes and intentions. Descriptive norms and egoistic values were not significant. Practical implications Indonesian higher education institutions should prioritise intention formation over awareness-only approaches, strengthen injunctive normative climates through institutional leadership and invest in enabling campus infrastructure, consistent with the Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) for 2030 roadmap and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 4 and 13. Originality/value This study is among the first to integrate tripartite value orientations, dual-dimension risk perceptions and differentiated social norms in a single PLS-SEM model of student PEB in Indonesian higher education, an underrepresented context in sustainability in higher education research.

title: Institutional theory and its application to library studies. Part 2
abstractText: Purpose Part 2 of this article explores how institutional theory could be applied to library studies by identifying a range of elements in the library environment that could be examined with an institutional theory lens. Design/methodology/approach Potential applications are considered by identifying institutional carriers found in the library environment and in the existing library studies literature, using Scott's table of generic institutional carriers to frame this study. Findings A wide range of institutional carriers were identified; many pertaining specifically to libraries and many that were already of interest to scholars. Those particularly associated with libraries and most represented in the existing research literature, tend to form part of the normative or regulative “pillars” in Scott's table, especially those that constitute, or are elements of, symbolic systems or institutional activities. Nevertheless, virtually all the generic carriers listed by Scott could be translated to the library context. Originality/value The article constitutes the first discussion in the scholarly literature of the application, and applicability, of institutional theory to the study of libraries and their environments.

title: Digital promotions and impulse buying among Muslim Generation Z: the roles of illusion of liquidity and religiosity
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to examine how responses to digital promotions such as free shipping and cashback offers are associated with impulse buying among Muslim Generation Z e-wallet users. It investigates the illusion of liquidity as a mediating mechanism, self-control as a protective individual characteristic and religiosity as a direct predictor and moderator. Design/methodology/approach Cross-sectional survey data from 305 Muslim Generation Z users of e-wallets recruited through purposive sampling were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings Cashback was positively associated with illusion of liquidity and impulse buying, whereas the corresponding relationships involving free shipping were not significant. Illusion of liquidity mediated the cashback–impulse buying relationship, while self-control was negatively associated with both illusion of liquidity and impulse buying. Contrary to expectations, religiosity was positively associated with impulse buying. Religiosity weakened the association between free shipping and impulse buying but strengthened the cashback–impulse buying association. Research limitations/implications The findings extend stimulus–organism–response theory by identifying illusion of liquidity as a promotion-specific mechanism and showing that religiosity operates as a contingent, rather than uniformly protective, influence on impulse buying. Practical implications Platforms should recognise that different promotional formats may be associated with different consumer responses, improve transparency regarding actual expenditure and avoid designs that inflate perceived liquidity. Because religiosity did not weaken the illusion-of-liquidity effect, religious messaging alone may be insufficient; ethical safeguards should instead support financial awareness and behavioural self-regulation. Originality/value This study identifies promotion-specific relationships involving perceived liquidity and shows that self-reported religiosity does not uniformly constrain promotion-related impulse buying.

title: When participation is not inclusion: the service-participation paradox in mental health
abstractText: Purpose This conceptual paper aims to examine why increased participation in mental health services does not necessarily produce social inclusion and develops a framework for distinguishing participation that expands a person’s social world from participation that remains contained within services. Design/methodology/approach As a conceptual paper, it develops a theoretical distinction and framework by drawing on selected literature on mental health recovery, social inclusion, community integration and occupational engagement. Findings The paper introduces the service-participation paradox, whereby services can successfully increase participation while leaving a person’s wider social world largely unchanged. It distinguishes service-contained from inclusion-oriented participation, proposes a two-dimensional matrix crossing participation intensity with social-world expansion and offers a sustainability heuristic for examining what remains beyond the service’s direct organisation and mediation, alongside meaning, choice and agency as person-centred criteria for interpreting both dimensions. Practical implications Services are encouraged to evaluate participation not only by attendance but by whether it is meaningful, chosen and expands access to relationships, roles and settings beyond the service system. Originality/value The paper offers a novel conceptual framing of the relationship between service-organised participation and social inclusion, bringing together the service-participation paradox, a distinction between service-contained and inclusion-oriented participation and heuristic tools for examining social-world expansion.

title: Hard X-ray flux rope anchor points in the October 2024 X9 flare
abstractText: In recent studies, signatures of non-thermal hard X-ray (HXR) emission at the anchor point of erupting flux ropes were reported, suggesting that accelerated electrons trapped in the erupting flux ropes can reach the chromosphere and produce Bremsstrahlung emission there. We investigated the HXR sources observed during the impulsive phase of the X9-class flare SOL2024-10-03T12:18 from AR 13842 and assessed whether any of the HXR sources are associated with the anchor points of the erupting flux rope. We analysed the evolution and location of the flare ribbon sources and coronal dimmings to diagnose the eruption process by using multi-vantage point data from the Solar Orbiter and Earth-orbiting instruments. We combined this with a pre-eruption non-linear force-free magnetic field extrapolation to reconstruct the initial magnetic connectivity and compare it to the observed flare ribbons and dimming locations. The magnetic field extrapolation shows two flux ropes before the flare onset. Tether-cutting reconnection during the impulsive phase of the flare results in a larger erupting flux rope formed by the reconnection of the two pre-existing flux ropes. The Spectrometer/Telescope for Imaging X-rays on Solar Orbiter observes at least four distinct HXR sources: two flare footpoints and two additional outer sources at the anchor points of the erupting flux rope. These observations corroborate earlier speculations that non-thermal electrons trapped in the erupting flux rope precipitate along the field lines into the denser chromosphere.

title: Mesenchymal Stem Cell-Mediated Uptake and Delivery of Indocyanine Green/Doxorubicin-Loaded Stimuli-Responsive Dendrimers to Tumors
abstractText: Systemic administration of nanocarriers can be limited by rapid clearance and off-target distribution, motivating the investigation of cell-based carrier strategies. Here, we evaluated skin-derived mesenchymal stem cells (S-MSCs) as carriers for PEGylated poly(amidoamine) dendrimer nanoclusters (DNCs) co-loaded with the chemotherapeutic doxorubicin (DOX) and the photothermal dye indocyanine green (ICG). The dendrimer nanoclusters (DNCs-ICG-DOX-PEG) enabled effective co-encapsulation of both cargoes and retained the optical properties required for NIR activation. Confocal imaging confirmed intracellular retention of DOX-associated fluorescence, predominantly within vesicular compartments, for up to 48 h after DNC loading, whereas free DOX was largely lost from S-MSCs within 24 h. At lower tested concentrations, DNC-loading preserved S-MSC metabolic activity, surface marker expression, and migratory function. Irradiation at 808 nm increased DOX release from the DNC formulations and produced an irradiation-dependent reduction in S-MSC metabolic activity. In a pilot murine LLC1 tumor model, S-MSCs preloaded with DNCs and administered adjacent to the tumor were detected within tumor tissue after 24 h, indicating that DNC loading did not abolish local tumor-directed migration. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the feasibility of using S-MSCs as carriers for NIR-responsive, DOX- and ICG-loaded dendrimer nanoclusters and provide a foundation for further studies of cargo biodistribution and therapeutic efficacy.

title: Ventricular Septal Rupture: A Contemporary Review of Pathophysiology, Diagnosis, Management, and Future Directions
abstractText: Ventricular septal rupture remains a deadly complication of acute MI, despite advances in medical care. In the reperfusion era, its incidence has declined to approximately 0.3%. Early and late ventricular septal rupture occur due to distinct mechanisms, including hemorrhagic infarct conversion and inflammatory extracellular matrix degradation, respectively. Clinical presentation can range from asymptomatic to fulminant cardiogenic shock, depending on shunt fraction, coexisting right ventricular failure, and mitral regurgitation. Diagnosis is commonly achieved by transthoracic or transesophageal echocardiography. Mainstay management is afterload reduction and early use of temporary mechanical circulatory support in cases of shock, alongside hemodynamic monitoring via pulmonary artery catheterization. Definitive repair beyond 7 days is associated with improved outcomes; options include surgical versus transcatheter approaches. A multidisciplinary approach with early referral to high-volume shock centers is crucial upon diagnosis. Future research defining patient or hemodynamic phenotypes associated with survival using distinct approaches and randomized comparisons of different closure strategies is needed.

title: Analytical validation of an in-house CSF neurogranin assay for clinical use
abstractText: OBJECTIVES: Synaptic dysfunction is an early and central feature of Alzheimer's disease (AD), and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) neurogranin (Ng) has emerged as a promising biomarker reflecting synaptic pathology. However, despite its increasing use in research, comprehensive analytical and clinical validation supporting its routine clinical use remains limited. METHODS: We developed an updated version of an in-house CSF Ng enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (UGOT-Ng) and performed a full analytical validation, including precision, selectivity, measurement range, dilution linearity, interference, and sample stability. Method comparison with a previous assay version and instrument comparability were also assessed. A distribution-derived upper threshold was established using a large set of prospectively measured routine clinical samples. Finally, the associations between CSF Ng concentrations and core AD biomarkers were examined in a large retrospective dataset. RESULTS: The assay demonstrated acceptable analytical performance, with good repeatability and intermediate precision across the evaluated concentration levels. The measurement range was established at 38-1,200 ng/L, with satisfactory dilution linearity and minimal interference from blood contamination. CSF Ng showed high stability under various preanalytical conditions. Distribution-derived analysis in amyloid-negative clinical samples yielded an upper limit of 390 ng/L. In clinical samples, CSF Ng correlated strongly with total tau and phosphorylated tau, while associations with Aβ42/40 were weaker and largely driven by differences between amyloid-positive and -negative individuals. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides a comprehensive analytical validation of an in-house CSF Ng assay, supporting its implementation in a routine clinical laboratory. CSF Ng was strongly associated with CSF total tau and phosphorylated tau, supporting its relationship with tau-associated neuronal and synaptic pathology in AD. However, the strength of these correlations also raises the possibility that CSF Ng provides information that overlaps with established tau biomarkers. Further studies should therefore determine whether Ng offers incremental diagnostic or prognostic value, identifies biologically distinct patient subgroups, or improves the monitoring of synaptic dysfunction beyond currently available biomarkers.

title: Intelligent prediction of time-varying transmission ratio in harmonic drive for end-effector positioning accuracy enhancement of industrial robot
abstractText: Purpose This paper aims to enhance the absolute positioning accuracy of industrial robot end-effectors under dynamic operating conditions through joint-level transmission error correction. Design/methodology/approach An intelligent regression model is designed that fuses differentiable innovation search, multi-branch convolutional network, bidirectional long short-term memory network, squeeze-and-excitation attention mechanism and kernel density estimation. The model predicts instantaneous reduction ratios of the fourth, fifth and sixth joints. To fully excite nonlinear characteristics of transmission, a random path generation strategy based on nonuniform B-splines and a cryptographically strong hybrid entropy source is proposed, achieving dense coverage of the workspace. The predicted ratios are subsequently fed into a flexible-joint dynamics model, with driving torques corrected via proportional-derivative control and injected as feedforward compensation to enhance end-effector positioning accuracy under dynamic operating conditions. Findings End-effector position accuracy compensation experiments demonstrate that, compared with the fixed reduction ratio model, the mean errors in X, Y and Z directions are reduced by 40.0%, 69.4% and 71.3%, respectively, while the standard deviations are reduced by 1.6%, 13.4% and 11.8%. The proposed method not only reduces the mean end-effector positioning error but also effectively enhances the stability of the positioning accuracy. Originality/value A hybrid intelligent regression model is constructed to predict instantaneous joint transmission ratios, which are then used to correct a flexible-joint dynamics model and applied as feedforward compensation to enhance end-effector positioning accuracy under dynamic operating conditions.

title: Influence of human activities on the trophic behavior of the African golden wolf Canis lupaster in an olive grove and a cork oak forest in the Tizi Ouzou region, Algeria
abstractText: The African golden wolf ( Canis lupaster ) is one of the main wild canids occurring in northern Africa, and significant gaps remain regarding its biology, diet, and foraging strategies. This study investigates its diet and how it is shaped by environmental conditions, particularly human activity. The trophic ecology of this carnivore was analyzed using 327 fecal samples collected over a period of six months, in two ecosystems: Aberrane cork oak forest and Ath Bouadou olive grove, located in the Tizi Ouzou region, northern Algeria. The presence of an illegal poultry waste dump in the cork oak forest led to a noticeable increase in domestic birds (FO = 60.12 %) in the wolf’s diet, illustrating its opportunistic nature. In the olive grove, a high level of household waste suggests direct interaction between human settlements and wildlife, further influencing dietary patterns. The FTIR analysis of plastic samples eaten by this predator shows the presence of phthalate plasticizers. These chemicals are known to be very dangerous to animals’ health. This study confirms the African wolf’s ability to modify its diet in response to available resources and human presence. However, its reliance on anthropogenic waste raises concerns. Regular scavenging at landfills may pose health risks and disrupt ecological balance, altering predator–prey dynamics and favoring certain species over others, with potential long-term consequences for the ecosystem.

title: Effect of WC-NiCrBSi/NiCuBSi based coatings on wear performance of austenitic stainless steel
abstractText: This study aims to comparatively evaluate the metallurgical, mechanical, and tribological characteristics of WC-based composite coatings with different metallic matrix compositions deposited on a steel substrate by oxy-acetylene flame spraying. Three coating formulations containing 60WC–40NiCrBSi wt.%, 50WC–50NiCrBSi wt.%, and 30WC–35NiCrBSi–35NiCuBSi wt.% are investigated. The coating cross-sections are characterized to determine the WC distributions embedded within solidified metals, coating/substrate transition zones, and heat-affected zones (HAZs). Dry sliding tests are performed to determine the coefficient of friction (CoF) and specific wear rate, while worn surfaces are examined to identify the prevailing wear mechanisms. The coatings develop heterogeneous solidification structures comprising WC-reinforced metallic matrices, with local variations in grain size and WC distribution. The coating/substrate transition zone and HAZ exhibit lower hardness than the deposited coating, whereas the refined solidification structure of the solidified metal contributes to local hardening even in WC-deficient regions. The highest-WC coating attains the highest hardness (∼850 HV 0.3 ), while the ternary composite maintains ∼725 HV 0.3 despite its lower WC content. The CoF decreases from ∼0.12–0.15 to ∼0.05–0.09 with increasing NiCuBSi contribution, while the specific wear rate varies with the combined effects of WC content, matrix chemistry, and microstructural characteristics.

title: Targeted Gene Delivery with Enhanced Efficacy through Heterochiral Coassembly of Peptides
abstractText: The development of gene-based therapeutics faces substantial delivery challenges. To address this, we report a strategy involving heterochiral peptide coassembly to create an efficient peptidyl delivery platform. Our experimental results reveal that equimolar mixture of l-KH-CCR and d-KH-CCR peptides exhibit significantly enhanced gene condensation efficiency, improved structural stability, and more effective endosomal membrane disruption compared to their pure enantiomeric counterparts. These superior properties facilitate increased cellular internalization and efficient endosomal escape, ultimately leading to optimized delivery of various gene therapeutics, particularly mRNA and siRNA. Building upon these findings, we engineered a four-component system that integrates a targeting peptide and PEG-conjugated anti-adhesion peptides within the heterochiral peptide system, which was evaluated for pulmonary mRNA delivery and expression in an orthotopic A549 lung tumor model. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that these peptides can effectively bind to mRNA through a combination of electrostatic, hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions, leading to the self-assembly of nanoparticles with accessible targeting and anti-adhesion motifs. In this model, the targeting-peptide-containing heterochiral formulation produced higher lung reporter expression than the corresponding homochiral formulations. These findings underscore the pivotal influence of chirality in optimizing the performance of peptidyl nanocarriers for targeted gene delivery applications.

title: Negotiating AI at work: motivational tensions and the redefinition of marketing expertise
abstractText: Purpose Artificial Intelligence Marketing (AIM) tools are increasingly transforming how marketing work is performed. However, its impact on individual practitioners remains underexplored. This study aims to examine how marketing professionals experience and negotiate the contradictory motivational consequences of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled work. Rather than treating AI as either empowering or threatening, the study explores how these effects coexist and how practitioners respond to them. Design/methodology/approach Twenty in-depth interviews were conducted with marketing practitioners using an exploratory, theory-informed qualitative design. Maslow’s Hierarchy of Needs, Self-Determination Theory and the Job Characteristics Model were used as complementary sensitising lenses to orient interpretation, while coding procedures informed by grounded theory techniques were used to develop themes inductively from the data. Findings The findings reveal that AIM simultaneously empowers and destabilises practitioners. AI enhances efficiency, capability, strategic focus, confidence and creative possibilities, while also generating uncertainty regarding task ownership, professional identity, technological dependence and future relevance. These effects are not experienced as separate outcomes. Instead, practitioners continually negotiate competing tensions by reframing expertise, selectively integrating AI, preserving human control over consequential tasks and reaffirming distinctively human sources of professional value. Motivation therefore emerges as dynamic and continually reconstructed rather than as a stable outcome of AI adoption. Research limitations/implications The design prioritises interpretive depth rather than statistical generalisability. Future research could develop measures of AI-enabled empowerment, destabilisation and negotiation using larger and more diverse samples. The research sample did not analyse differences across career stages, and warrants future investigation. This paper examines broad AIM tools rather than isolated technologies. Future studies should explore how particular AI capabilities change dimensions of professional value and motivation. The findings highlight negotiation as a continuing process, but the cross-sectional design provides only a snapshot of the process. Longitudinal research could establish whether empowerment-destabilisation tensions persist, intensify, diminish or change form over time. The findings suggest potentially important roles for trust, employee participation, work design, organisational support and AI governance. Future research could investigate the organisational conditions that facilitate productive negotiation of AI-related tensions for marketing practitioners. Practical implications Organisations should consider: Evaluating AI in terms of how it changes employees’ experiences of expertise, ownership, autonomy and professional value; Approaching AI capability development as workforce transformation, rather than technical training alone; Preserving meaningful human ownership of work; Addressing the efficiency-intensification paradox. Providing employees with meaningful agency over AI adoption; Treating AI governance as a crucial part of the employee experience. Social implications AI simultaneously empowers and destabilises marketing practitioners, generating tensions around expertise, autonomy, identity and employability. Rather than passively accepting change, individuals actively negotiate these tensions through adaptation, reframing and human–AI collaboration. AI’s long-term impact will depend not only on technological capabilities, but also on how organisations sustain meaningful work, professional development and human agency. Originality/value This study contributes a new tension-based framework that explains how motivation is continuously constructed under AI-driven work environments. In addition, it advances the understanding of AI-enabled work in three ways. Firstly, it conceptualises employee motivation as shaped by simultaneous empowerment and destabilisation rather than by uniformly positive or negative effects. Secondly, it shows how AI redefines marketing expertise from task execution towards judgment, interpretation, contextual understanding and human–AI orchestration. Thirdly, it identifies ongoing negotiation as a central process through which practitioners sustain professional value and motivation under technological change.

title: From compliance to resilience: a functional framework for AI-enabled environmental governance
abstractText: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in corporate environmental governance, yet much of what is labelled AI in this context is difficult to distinguish from conventional rule-based digital automation. Its contribution so far has concentrated on automating compliance reporting rather than building the adaptive capacity that resilience thinking requires. The paper defines what qualifies as AI-enabled environmental governance and develops a framework for distinguishing AI-enabled compliance from AI-enabled resilience, with particular attention to enterprises in middle-income, small and medium enterprise (SME)-dominated economies undergoing simultaneous digital and green transformation. Design/methodology/approach This conceptual paper takes a theory-synthesis approach, combining a technical definition of AI systems with resilience theory, the technology-organization-environment framework and research on greenwashing and AI-washing to propose a four-layer framework: sensing, decision, institutional and equity. Each layer's level of analysis and candidate operational indicators are specified, its relationship to existing digital-maturity models is clarified and its boundary conditions are set out. The central sensing-to-decision mechanism is illustrated with secondary case evidence and examined alongside independent survey-based studies from South and Southeast Asia, whose findings are consistent with, though not a direct test of, the proposed mechanism. Findings The paper argues that AI investment concentrated in the sensing layer, without corresponding investment in the decision and institutional layers, produces compliance-grade rather than resilience-grade outcomes. This pattern is expected to be most pronounced in resource-constrained, SME-dominated settings, where sensing tools can be purchased as point solutions while decision-layer integration requires internal capability that is harder to build. Independent survey evidence from medium enterprises in Indonesia and from the banking sector in India is consistent with this asymmetry, although neither study was designed to test the framework directly. Practical implications The framework offers regulators, firms, financial institutions and educators a vocabulary and a set of candidate indicators for distinguishing genuine resilience investment from compliance automation, useful for designing tiered, capability-aware policy instruments during the current transition towards harmonized international sustainability disclosure standards. Social implications Because environmental shocks fall hardest on those least able to absorb them, the distribution of AI-enabled resilience capability across firms of different sizes is a question of social equity and not only of technical efficiency. The framework's equity layer treats this distribution as a design variable that regulators, financiers and educators can act on, rather than as an unintended side effect of technology diffusion. Originality/value The paper supplies a technical definition of AI-enabled environmental governance and identifies a specific governance failure mode: a layer-specific asymmetry in the cost and purchasability of AI capability that predicts where disclosed adoption and substantive practice are likely to decouple. It proposes candidate indicators for operationalizing the framework's layers at their respective levels of analysis, differentiates this functional approach from adjacent stage-based digital- and environmental, social, and governance (ESG)-maturity models, and narrows its boundary conditions to the institutional settings in which it is expected to apply.

title: TiO2/ZIF-8/CF-Based Triboelectric Nanogenerator for Intelligent Ammonia Sensing and Wireless Alarm in Livestock Farms
abstractText: Ammonia, a common hazardous gas, severely endangers ecosystems and public health through unregulated industrial emissions and accidental leaks. Given the wide distribution and potential hazards of ammonia, a high-speed pulse airflow-powered triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) was constructed to realize ammonia sensing and environmental surveillance in animal breeding facilities. This device adopted a TiO2/ZIF-8/copper foam (CF) composite structure as the friction electrode (TZP-TENG). The composite nanogenerator efficiently harvested energy from high-pressure waste gas and exhibited outstanding electrical output performance. It delivered a short-circuit current output of 3.36 μA together with a peak power density reaching 41.19 μW at an NH3 concentration of 30 ppm. This device could illuminate 60 LEDs and supply different capacitors. For its excellent ammonia-sensing capability, the TZP-TENG could be integrated into a wireless early warning system to realize real-time monitoring and automatic alarming for high-concentration ammonia. Furthermore, the device is applicable to ammonia concentration detection in livestock farms, which helps stabilize the breeding environment and optimize the growth conditions of livestock and poultry. This design not only expands the technical approaches for ammonia detection but also enables intelligent regulation of breeding environments. It provides significant technical references and practical application demonstrations for harmful gas monitoring and environmental management in livestock breeding sites.

title: Osteopathic manipulative treatment in resolving post-stroke depression: a case report
abstractText: Depression affects approximately one in three people following a stroke, most commonly within the first year. The current standard of care for post-stroke depression (PSD) does not differ from that of a non-stroke patient. Few studies have investigated the application of osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT) within psychiatric conditions; however, studies have demonstrated its potential in downregulating the body's stress response. In this case report, we explore the use of OMT as an adjunct intervention for new-onset mild depressive symptoms following a stroke. This case follows a 64-year-old woman who presented to an outpatient behavioral health clinic in October 2024 for depressed mood following a left middle cerebral artery stroke four months prior. She initiated psychotherapy and declined medication management. After four months of psychotherapy exclusively, her mood symptoms continued to worsen and her PHQ-9 was 7. In April 2025, after six months of psychotherapy, she began OMT every two weeks, for a total of three treatments, addressing somatic dysfunctions of the head, cervical spine, thoracic inlet, and associated musculature. At each session, she completed the PHQ-9 and a pre- and post-session questionnaire assessing specific mood symptoms (sleep, irritability, stress/tension, hopelessness, anxious mood, and depressed mood). At initiation of OMT, the patient's PHQ-9 score was 5, with clinician-observed emotional lability and tearfulness. Her pre-session questionnaire indicated disturbances in sleep, irritability, hopelessness, and depressed mood. Immediately following her first treatment, the patient noted absence of symptoms on post-OMT questionnaire. Following three OMT sessions, her PHQ-9 decreased to 0 and there was no self-reported anxious or depressed mood, irritability, or hopelessness. After two months without OMT, the patient's depressive symptoms and emotional lability returned. These symptoms resolved immediately following an additional OMT session. Two weeks later, her PHQ-9 was 0 and no other mood symptoms were reported. With ongoing OMT every 4-6 weeks, subsequent PHQ-9's continued to be 0. This case suggests the potential of integrating OMT in the treatment of mild PSD, with this patient experiencing initial resolution of depressive symptoms following three OMT sessions. We hope these findings encourage providers to consider OMT in management of depressive symptoms following stroke and spur further investigation of the utilization of OMT as an adjunctive treatment in PSD.

title: When digital-only and physical-only service experiences become infeasible: a phygital feasibility restoration framework for hybrid ecosystems
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to explain when digital-only and physical-only service experiences become infeasible for customers and how phygital service design restores journey feasibility in hybrid ecosystems. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a conceptual approach and draws on affordance theory and service-dominant logic to develop a 4A taxonomy of single-modality infeasibility and a phygital feasibility restoration framework, which is supported by ten propositions and four vignettes. Findings Single-modality infeasibility arises when access, ability, acceptability or appropriateness conditions fail. Phygital design restores feasibility through substitution, augmentation, scaffolding and safeguarding, which, in turn, improves experience feasibility, continuity and ecosystem resilience. Originality/value This study reframes phygital service experience as a feasibility restoration problem rather than an integration problem, shifting the design and policy test from nominal availability to feasible participation. The framework treats the human side of service as a design resource that technology, including artificial intelligence, should augment rather than displace, thereby advancing theory, service design, inclusion, wellbeing and policy in hybrid ecosystems.

title: Queer(y)ing gender in entrepreneurial action through the experiences of transgender women entrepreneurs in Tasmania
abstractText: Purpose This study examines and queers entrepreneurial action theory using queer phenomenology, showing how gender affirmation reshapes entrepreneurial action. While entrepreneurial action theory traditionally focuses on decision-making within uncertain environments, it rarely accounts for experiences of transgender women. Design/methodology/approach This research combined narrative inquiry and visual methods to collect data from two transgender women entrepreneurs in Tasmania, Australia. Research on transgender women entrepreneurs is limited, so combined methods capture emotional nuances: (1) drawings of self-perception before and after starting the business and (2) an in-depth interview. Findings Findings suggest considering temporal dynamics across different industries when entrepreneurs seek to reveal their identity. Louise is a mechanical engineer, and being a mechanic in a masculine-dominated industry significantly influences the perceptions of family, friends and customers. Meanwhile, Sally, a comedian, was provided with space for creativity and fluid perceptions. The women's experiences are not uniform, with industries entrepreneurs are aligned with shaping their negotiation of entrepreneurship. Research limitations/implications This study advances entrepreneurial action theory by integrating queer phenomenology to account for transgender women entrepreneurs' lived experiences. It challenges the assumption of time as a neutral construct in entrepreneurial action theory. This study shows how cisnormative expectations within transgender women's space shape entrepreneurial decision-making timing, pacing, and sequencing. Originality/value This article challenges existing discourses around entrepreneurial action theory and gender in entrepreneurship. Transgender women entrepreneurs may have limited ability to conceal their gender identity, which complicates their steps towards entrepreneurial action. The current study advances understanding of time and space for transgender women in their entrepreneurial trajectories.

title: Association between internet non-use and mortality risk among older adults: the explanatory contribution of social integration
abstractText: Purpose Digital exclusion has emerged as an important dimension of social exclusion among older adults and has been associated with adverse health outcomes. However, its association with all-cause mortality and the potential role of social integration remain unclear. This study examined whether recent internet non-use was associated with all-cause mortality and explored the potential contribution of social integration. Design/methodology/approach Data were obtained from the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE), including 47,989 community-dwelling adults aged 50 years and older from 18 countries. Internet non-use was defined as no internet use during the previous seven days. Country-stratified Cox proportional hazards models examined the association between internet non-use and mortality, adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics, depressive symptoms, and physical health. Mediation analyses evaluated the potential contribution of social integration. Findings Internet non-use was independently associated with a higher risk of all-cause mortality after adjustment for sociodemographic characteristics, depressive symptoms, and physical health. This association remained after accounting for social integration, although it was partially attenuated. Social integration explained part of the observed association, suggesting that it may represent a potential explanatory pathway linking internet non-use and mortality. Research limitations/implications Recent internet non-use was independently associated with higher all-cause mortality among older adults. Social integration accounted for part of this association, although additional pathways are likely to contribute. These findings support the interpretation of internet non-use as a marker of broader digital exclusion and highlight the importance of promoting digital inclusion and social participation in healthy ageing. Practical implications Policymakers should prioritize digital inclusion as a public health strategy. Programs promoting digital literacy and improving internet accessibility for older adults are essential not only for social integration but also as potential interventions to mitigate mortality risks associated with the digital divide. Social implications Non-use of the internet represents a critical barrier to contemporary social well-being. Addressing digital inequalities is a matter of social justice; fostering inclusive technological environments can enhance the social fabric and support the overall health and survival of aging populations. Originality/value This study extends previous research by examining, in a large multicountry European cohort, not only the association between recent internet non-use and all-cause mortality but also the potential explanatory contribution of social integration. These findings support the interpretation of internet non-use as a marker of broader digital exclusion and highlight the importance of promoting digital inclusion and social participation in healthy ageing.

title: Tandem Dual Catalytic Pyrolysis of Lignin and Spent Bleaching Clay over Mo/C and Ammonia-Assisted Cu-Loaded Y-Type Zeolite to Produce Monoaromatic Hydrocarbons
abstractText: Catalytic copyrolysis of lignin and hydrogen-rich feedstocks is a sustainable process for producing monocyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (MAHs). A tandem dual catalytic system comprising a Mo/C catalyst and ammonia-assisted Cu-loaded Y zeolite was constructed for the conversion of the pyrolysis gas of lignin and spent bleaching clay (SBC). Results showed that the incorporation of Cu species into the framework of Y zeolite increases the specific surface area, total acid content, weak acid sites, and Lewis acid sites. At a pyrolysis temperature of 500°, with a raw material to catalyst ratio of 1:3, and a Mo/C to Cu/Y-0.3 ratio of 1:3, the Cu/Y-0.3 catalyst increased the bio-oil yield to 26.39% and achieved an MAH content of 70.59%. The precatalysis of Mo/C and the additional weak Lewis acid sites reduced coke deposition on the catalyst and shifted the oxidation peak of coke to lower temperatures. The coke deposited on the surface of the Cu/Y-0.3 catalyst contains more C–O/C═O bonds and fewer C–C bonds, making it easier to remove. These functional groups increased its oxidation reactivity and facilitated coke removal. The optimal conditions (pyrolysis temperature: 636.88 °C, catalyst-to-feedstock ratio: 4.62, and mass ratio of Cu/Y-0.3 to Mo/C: 3.04) for MAHs yield were obtained through the response surface model. Under the optimal conditions, the catalyst maintained 59.39% MAH relative content after four cycles. Life cycle assessment shows that, when the system boundary was defined from raw material and catalyst purchase to the completion of pyrolysis and harmless treatment of the catalyst, copyrolysis reduces greenhouse gas emissions by 90.62% and toxicity impacts (freshwater, marine, terrestrial, and human) by 64%–89% compared with traditional treatment. The possible reaction mechanism of tandem catalysis was analyzed. This study provides insight into the production of high-value chemicals through catalytic pyrolysis of lignin and hydrogen-rich wastes.

A Multimodal Hyaluronic Acid Approach to Compensate Menopause-Related Skin Changes: Hyaluronic Acid Serum Subanalysis With HA Filler Injection
abstractText: BACKGROUND: Estrogen depletion during menopause reduces collagen, elastin, and glycosaminoglycans (GAG) synthesis, particularly hyaluronic acid (HA), and is associated with skin thinness, wrinkles, reduced elasticity, and decreased hydration. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy of an integrated facial antiaging approach using a multiglycan HA serum with HA filler injection in menopausal women. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A serum formulation (containing HA, dipotassium glycyrrhizate, purple rice extract, Lactobacillus/soybean ferment extract, pro-Xylane) was applied twice daily on the face from Day -14 to Day 56 and integrated with nasolabial fold HA dermal filler injection on Day 0. In a post hoc subanalysis of 12 menopausal women, facial aging signs were assessed using instrumental measurements of skin elasticity and firmness, and standardized photography. RESULTS: At baseline, net skin elasticity in the temple area and in the nasolabial fold area were lower in the menopausal subgroup compared with the overall cohort. In menopausal women, nasolabial and temple skin elasticity showed improvement between baseline and Day 56. CONCLUSION: A multimodal HA serum integrated with HA dermal injection may offer a promising facial rejuvenation strategy in menopausal women with skin aging signs.

title: Beyond the EAP Bottleneck: An Integrated Framework for Academic English Learning in Higher Education
abstractText: English for Academic Purposes (EAP) enables university students to engage with disciplinary reading, writing, lectures, discussion, and research. Yet learners can encounter a persistent bottleneck when academic vocabulary, dense texts, genre expectations, oral participation, and access to support are treated as separate problems. This narrative review synthesizes foundational and recent scholarship on EAP and develops an integrated framework for responding to these interconnected demands. It asks: (1) Which linguistic, academic-literacy, cognitive, and affective barriers most often constrain students’ participation in EAP? and (2) How can instruction connect these needs to authentic university tasks while remaining inclusive of learner differences? The synthesis identifies five linked domains: vocabulary depth and disciplinary language; reading and source use; genre-based writing; listening and spoken participation; and learner variability, confidence, and access. It proposes a task-centered cycle that diagnoses needs, teaches language explicitly, engages learners in communicative disciplinary tasks, provides staged feedback, and evaluates transfer to new academic contexts. Research on mobile vocabulary learning and inclusive EAP informs the design; work on translation, L2 processing, linguistic relativity, and communicative language teaching provides complementary perspectives rather than direct evidence of EAP outcomes. Because the review is narrative and introduces no new participant data, the framework is a reasoned proposal that requires empirical testing across disciplines and institutions.

title: Deep cervical lymphovenous anastomosis for neurodegenerative disease: from biological rationale to first clinical evidence
abstractText: Recent advances in neurolymphatic research have challenged the traditional concept of the central nervous system as an organ without lymphatic drainage. The glymphatic system and meningeal lymphatic vessels contribute to cerebral fluid homeostasis and the clearance of metabolic waste, with downstream drainage toward the deep cervical lymphatic system. Dysfunction of these pathways has been implicated in neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s disease. These discoveries have recently led to an unconventional application of lymphatic microsurgery: deep cervical lymphovenous anastomosis (dcLVA), intended to enhance cerebral waste clearance by facilitating cervical lymphatic outflow into the venous circulation. Since 2025, first prospective clinical studies have reported technical feasibility as well as short-term cognitive, functional, and biomarker changes after dcLVA in patients with Alzheimer’s disease. The concept has also been extended to Parkinson’s disease. However, current evidence remains limited to uncontrolled or nonrandomized studies and isolated case reports, while the underlying physiology, long-term anastomotic function, and clinical efficacy remain uncertain. This review summarizes the rapid development of dcLVA for neurodegenerative disease, critically evaluates the first clinical evidence, and discusses the requirements for translating this intriguing concept into an evidence-based application of lymphatic microsurgery.

title: Smartphone visibility and digital advertising in retail checkout
abstractText: Purpose This study examines how smartphone visibility and in-store digital advertising jointly influence consumer attention and impulse purchasing in retail checkout environments. Drawing on the limited-capacity model of attention and the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework, the research investigates how digital advertising, particularly its auditory features, shapes attention and impulse purchasing under own-smartphone visibility conditions. Design/methodology/approach A pretest was conducted to validate high- and low-attention zones within convenience stores, followed by two field studies in Taiwan(Study 1: N = 112; Study 2: N = 141). Construct reliability and validity were assessed using SmartPLS 4.0, and hypotheses were tested using ANOVA and SPSS PROCESS Models 4 and 8. Findings Study 1 shows that consumers whose own smartphones remained within their visual field during checkout reported lower attention to nearby products than those whose smartphones were out of sight. Study 2 shows that own-smartphone visibility was associated with greater ad-related product attention and impulsive purchase intention under silent but not sound-enabled digital advertising. Ad-related product attention statistically mediated the relationship between own-smartphone visibility and impulsive purchase intention, with the indirect effect emerging only under silent advertising. Originality/value This study identifies own-smartphone visibility as an overlooked checkout condition and shows that its relationships with consumer attention and impulsive purchase intention vary with the sensory context of digital advertising, particularly advertising sound.

title: Multimodal Imaging in Pericardial Disease: Integrating Echocardiography, Cardiac MRI, Cardiac CT, and Nuclear Imaging with Novel Tracers
abstractText: Accurate diagnosis of pericardial diseases can be challenging. Appropriately selected imaging studies to evaluate pericardial disease can refine diagnosis and therapeutic decision-making, provide value-based care by preventing unnecessary testing, and potentially avoid invasive procedures. For clinical scenarios with hemodynamic consequences, evaluation with high-temporal-resolution echocardiography or cardiac MRI (CMR), which enables simultaneous respirophasic evaluation, will have the highest diagnostic yield. When suspecting inflammatory pericardial disease, CMR or nuclear imaging are particularly sensitive. For pericardial calcification, such as in patients with a history of prior radiation, or when suspecting malignant pericardial involvement, cardiac CT provides excellent anatomic detail for treatment planning. This review highlights the strengths and limitations of each imaging modality and discusses how their integration optimizes diagnostic yield, guiding both medical and procedural management. The authors provide a needed overview of established and emerging CMR techniques, including Dixon fat–water separation, 3D late gadolinium enhancement, and native T1 mapping for effusion characterization, as well as a practical clinical overview on the diagnostic imaging sequence specific to evaluating different clinical scenarios.

title: From exposure to imprint: CEO formative experiences and the architecture of accounting and financial decisions
abstractText: Purpose This review explains how chief executive officers' formative experiences become organizationally consequential and why apparently similar exposures are associated with different accounting, financing, risk and stakeholder decisions. Design/methodology/approach Following the Search-Appraisal-Analysis-Synthesis (SAAS) workflow, the study maps 105 Scopus-indexed journal articles published between 2011 and 2026 using Biblioshiny and VOSviewer and conducts a structured content synthesis of 102 studies whose focal construct is an executive formative experience. Findings The literature converges around upper-echelons and imprinting perspectives but does not support a uniform “adversity produces conservatism” account. The synthesis distinguishes four adversity-related imprint families – threat vigilance and loss avoidance; uncertainty habituation, resilience or self-efficacy; scarcity orientation; and prosocial reorientation – while treating institutional socialization as conceptually distinct. Persistent imprints become observable only when later situations activate them and when executive discretion permits expression. Accounting and financing architecture provides particularly discriminating tests of these mechanisms. Originality/value The review moves beyond exposure–outcome associations by separating exposure formation, imprint content, activation, expression and observed decision bundles. It recentres accounting and corporate finance in the chief executive officer formative-experience literature and develops an auditable mechanism-based research agenda.

title: Reverse logistics in electronics industry: a bibliometric analysis, challenges and future research prospects
abstractText: Purpose The proliferation of electronic goods has increased challenges for global e-waste; thus, reverse logistics (RL) and closed-loop supply chains (CLSC) in the electronics sector have become very challenging research areas. This study aims to provide a substantial bibliometric and systematic overview of the RL and CLSC research in electronics, with a particular emphasis on identifying potential barriers to implementation and synthesising findings into a conceptual framework for future empirical investigation. Design/methodology/approach Data analysis was performed using the PRISMA 2020 protocol, extracted from the Scopus database through searching the terms reverse logistics, closed-loop supply chain and electronics. The search occurred from 2010 to 2024 and after applying structured inclusion and exclusion criteria resulted in a final corpus of 94 peer-reviewed journal articles. Bibliometric methods, such as trends in publication, keyword co-occurrence, co-citation analysis and thematic mapping, were then used. Findings The volume of publications has grown sharply since 2019, with a combination of the regulators’ attention, the global e-waste crisis and COVID-19 supply chain disruption. Keyword analysis shows a new paradigm shift from operational efficiency to strategic sustainability. There are four dimensions where barriers to RL and CLSC introduction cluster: technical infrastructure gaps, policy and regulatory weaknesses, strategic and organisational resistance and market and consumer behaviour factors. Research limitations/implications Policymakers need to enhance extended producer responsibility (EPR) enforcement and implement market-based incentives. Electronics manufacturers should invest in a phased digital transformation, from RFID-based tracking to AI-enabled return forecasting and put design-for-disassembly principles front and centre in development. Originality/value In addition, introducing an original multi-dimensional Conceptual Framework of RL/CLSC Implementation in this paper synthesising drivers, barriers, enabling technologies and sustainability outcomes at technical, economic, environmental and social/political dimensions would lay a structure for future empirical studies.
