title: Synergistic Weakly Solvating and Nitrate Chemistry Enables In Situ Polymerized Quasi-Solid Electrolytes for High-PerformanceSilicon Anodes
abstractText: The practical application of silicon anodes in quasi-solid polymer electrolytes is severely hindered by sluggish Li+ transport kinetics and poor interfacial stability. Herein, we report a synergistic design strategy that integrates weakly solvating solvents (ethyl acetate and fluoroethylene carbonate) with a LiNO3 additive into an in situ polymerized poly(methylenebisacrylamide) (MBA)-based quasi-solid electrolyte (EF/N-MBA). This synergy not only constructs an anion-rich Li+ solvation shell that appreciably enhances ionic conductivity and lowers the desolvation barrier but also facilitates the formation of a robust solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) enriched in LiF and Li3N, markedly improving interfacial stability and electrochemical kinetics toward the silicon anode. As a result, the optimized EF/N-MBA quasi-solid electrolyte achieves a high ionic conductivity of 3.68 mS cm–1, a superior Li+ transference number of 0.73, and a wide electrochemical stability window of 4.48 V. The in situ polymerized matrix, combined with the flame-retardant weakly solvating solvent system, renders the electrolyte flame-retardant, substantially mitigating the safety risks of conventional liquid electrolytes. Remarkably, the pure silicon anode employing this electrolyte delivers a reversible specific capacity of 1385.0 mAh g–1 after 300 cycles at 1 A g–1, and maintains a capacity of 1352.3 mAh g–1 at a high rate of 5 A g–1. Furthermore, Si||LiFePO4 full cells demonstrate excellent cycling stability and rate capability. This work shows that solvation chemistry and SEI nanostructure in in situ polymerized quasi-solid electrolytes can be synergistically tailored via weakly solvating solvents and nitrate additives, offering a viable route to overcome sluggish kinetics and interfacial degradation of silicon anodes in quasi-solid batteries.

title: Diachronic changes in epicene pronoun use in academic writing by Chinese novice researchers in applied linguistics
abstractText: The use of epicene pronouns in academic writing has been highly advocated in recent years. While most studies focus on L1 English epicene pronouns, less attention has been paid to the use of epicene pronouns in L2 academic writing. To address this gap, this study analyzes diachronic changes of epicene pronouns in the academic writing of Chinese novice researchers in applied linguistics, focusing on the uses of generic he , the coordinated form he or she , and singular they . Drawing on a dataset of postgraduate master’s theses sampled across three sampling periods, the study revealsconstituent of sociopragmatic a clear shift: a significant decline in generic he and a marked increase in both the coordinated form he or she and singular they . This trend suggests a growing preference for gender-fair forms in L2 academic writing over time. Notably, singular they has been increasingly adopted with quantificational noun phrases and has gradually extended to other indefinite and definite contexts, though its overall usage remains limited. To promote L2 writers’ gender-fair language awareness, this study recommends three pedagogical interventions: training teachers in gender-fair language principles, integrating gender-fair language teaching materials, and implementing concept-based instruction for epicene pronouns.

title: Porphyrin-Phenothiazine-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks for Enhanced Photocatalytic Nitrogen Fixation
abstractText: Solar-driven photocatalytic nitrogen reduction represents a promising and environmentally benign approach for ammonia synthesis. However, developing efficient photocatalysts capable of converting nitrogen to ammonia under ambient conditions remains a significant challenge. Porphyrin compounds exhibit excellent photosensitive properties with strong absorption across both the ultraviolet and visible regions of the solar spectrum, while phenothiazine offers unique optoelectronic activity. In this study, we integrated these two motifs and synthesized a series of novel metal-free covalent organic frameworks (COFs) by structural modification of the phenothiazine linker with a methyl group and with oxygen-containing functional groups. All three frameworks are active for N2 photoreduction under visible light, and the activity depends systematically on the linker: the sulfone-functionalized COF-3 reaches 109.6 ± 3.6 μmol g-1 h-1 (1866.2 ± 60.7 μg h-1 gcat-1), outperforming both the unmodified (COF-1) and the methyl-modified (COF-2) frameworks. Mechanistic analysis and theoretical calculations revealed that the introduced oxygen atoms facilitate the separation and transport of photogenerated electrons within the framework. This work shows that rational molecular-level pre-design and fine-tuning of the linker can profoundly influence the structural and optoelectronic properties of COF-based photocatalysts, enabling superior activity without the need for metallic elements or co-catalysts.

title: Metallurgical characterization and creep-fatigue behavior of a Cu–Cr–Zr alloy assessed by disc pressure testing
abstractText: This manuscript presents an investigation of the high-temperature fatigue and creep behavior of a precipitation-hardened Cu–Cr–Zr alloy using disc pressure testing under thermo-mechanical conditions representative of fusion reactor components. Unlike conventional uniaxial testing, the disc pressure method generates a biaxial stress state and realistic strain gradients, providing a more accurate assessment of service conditions in thin-walled plasma-facing structures. Fatigue experiments were performed under cyclic pressure loading until crack penetration, while creep tests were conducted under constant pressure with continuous deflection monitoring at elevated temperatures. The results revealed characteristic low-cycle fatigue, with crack initiation predominantly near the disc center and anchorage regions due to strain localization and microstructural heterogeneities. Finite element analysis supported the observed damage evolution. Creep performance exhibited a strong dependence on both temperature and applied pressure, with failure occurring during the secondary creep stage. Furthermore, helium leakage monitoring demonstrated high sensitivity to early microcrack formation, enabling reliable leak-before-break assessment. Metallurgical characterization revealed heterogeneous grain structures, precipitate coarsening, and thermal over-aging effects, resulting in material softening and moderate embrittlement above 400 °C. The findings provide valuable insights into the durability, structural integrity, and long-term reliability of Cu–Cr–Zr alloys for high-temperature nuclear and fusion energy applications.

title: Ru-Promoted Activation of Ni/CaTiO3/CaO Multifunctional Materials for Integrated CO2 Capture and Dry Reforming
abstractText: Ni-doped CaTiO3/CaO multifunctional materials couple CO2 capture with dry reforming of methane (DRM), but strong metal–lattice interactions can delay Ni activation during reactive regeneration. Here, Ru was incorporated into Ni/CaTiO3/CaO to determine how promotion affects reduction, exsolution, and cyclic integrated CO2 capture and DRM (ICCDRM). XRD and STEM-EDS show exsolution of Ni and Ru from CaTiO3 and preferential spatial association of finely dispersed Ru with exsolved Ni. H2-TPR and CH4-TPR indicate that Ru facilitates reduction and activation of Ni-containing phases relative to the corresponding integrated monometallic materials. At 700 °C, the time to peak CH4 conversion decreased from 6.6 min for both monometallic materials to 3.5 min for NiRu, while first-cycle apparent CO2 uptake remained comparable (5.92, 5.19, and 5.43 mmol CO2 g–1 for NiRu, Ni, and Ru, respectively). NiRu also enabled syngas formation at 650 °C, where the monometallic materials produced negligible syngas. Over 30 cycles, apparent CO2 uptake remained relatively consistent and CO production was sustained. Carbon closures of 99.5% and 98.8% were obtained for cycles 1 and 5, and TPO indicated only ∼0.06–0.07 mmol C per cycle. These results show that Ru principally promotes reduction and cyclic reactivation of Ni, helping coordinate catalytic activation with carbonate-derived CO2 release.

title: Greening, gentrification, and wellbeing: how socio-economic factors may interact with the benefits of nearby nature
abstractText: Purpose Connection and proximity to nature are associated with improved wellbeing outcomes. Yet links between gentrification and urban greening mean socio-economic factors may override the predictive capacity of nearby nature on wellbeing. This study aims to explore relationships between connection with nature, socio-economic factors and attributes of nearby nature. Design/methodology/approach A state-wide survey of residents in Victoria, Australia, (n = 1427) documented participants’ connection with nature, demographic and socio-economic variables and subjective wellbeing during the coronavirus pandemic. We used spatial datasets to develop scores for variables describing nearby nature (i.e. within 1-km) and asked about the accessibility and safety of local parks. We tested relationships between these variables using bivariate correlations and their associations with wellbeing using linear and generalized additive models (GAM). Findings The best model indicated that stronger connection with nature, being older, having a higher household income and some nearby nature dimensions (particularly proximity to the coast or other waterways, higher area of non-native vegetation, perceived (in)accessibility of nearby parks) were associated with higher wellbeing scores. There were confounding effects between some variables. Social implications Our study reveals insights into nature-related and socio-economic factors associated with wellbeing, while highlighting the complexity of relationships between nature access, proximity, connection and other variables. This is useful in informing nuanced urban planning and social programs to support community wellbeing. Originality/value Our paper is unique in integrating socio-economic disadvantage, nature connection and nearby nature variables into one model. The GAM approach identified novel non-linear relationships with wellbeing including age and perceived park (in)accessibility, which may be unique to the pandemic.

FLUKA-based assessment of induced radioactivity in iron target and surrounding coolants under 400 MeV carbon-ion irradiation
abstractText: Simulations were performed to investigate neutron-induced radioactivity in the iron (Fe) target and surrounding coolants (sodium-potassium alloy (NaK), lead (Pb), water (H 2 O), liquid sodium (Na), and carbon dioxide (CO 2 )) by bombarding the target with 400 MeV carbon ions. Radionuclides produced within the target material and each coolant were evaluated over time using the FLUKA Monte Carlo code. The temporal evolution of all induced radionuclides was analyzed and visualized through time-dependent activity curves. Neutron yield was quantified at an incident energy of 400 MeV. It was observed that low-energy neutrons were the main cause of activation. During the shutdown of the accelerator, 56 Mn was observed with a high ratio inside the iron target, while 41 Ar, 200 Pb, 11 C, and 24 Na were identified as the primary contributors in the respective coolants: NaK, Lead, water, and liquid sodium. Specifically, 11 C was dominant in both water and CO 2 . From the start of irradiation to saturation, and with elapsed cooling time, growth and decay curves for each major induced element were summarized. A large amount of short-lived beta-decay radionuclides appeared while the accelerator was shut down; induced radionuclides with low activity were ignored due to low hazard. Considering the protection of radiation workers during maintenance or handling the equipment, research results show that lead (Pb) will produce the highest radiation effects when used as a coolant in a nuclear reactor, and it will require extra care as compared to water, gas, and other coolants included in this study.

title: When Mnemonics Outlive the Evidence: Lessons From Acute Coronary Syndrome Across the Nursing Education Continuum
abstractText: BACKGROUND: Clinical mnemonics are widely used in nursing education to simplify complex concepts and support knowledge acquisition, retention, and clinical recall. However, they may persist after the evidence that originally informed them has evolved. METHOD: This discussion article draws on current literature, historical reflection, and more than three decades of cardiovascular teaching observations to examine the evolution and continued recognition of the acute coronary syndrome (ACS) mnemonics MONA, AMONTH, and NOAH. RESULTS: The discussion illustrates how these mnemonics reflected different stages in ACS management and how memorable educational tools may remain embedded in nursing education and practice despite changes in clinical evidence. CONCLUSION: Clinical mnemonics should be periodically reviewed and revised to maintain alignment with contemporary evidence. The evolution of ACS mnemonics highlights broader implications for knowledge translation, curriculum renewal, and continuing professional development across the nursing education continuum.

title: A robust and efficient numerical scheme for the shallow-water equations with surface tension: application to the Jurin's law
abstractText: In this paper, we study shallow-water equations with surface tension over variable bottom topography. The capillary force is incorporated through a generalized potential combining the hydrostatic and surface-tension contributions. Based on this formulation, we first construct a first-order implicit-explicit scheme using a centered-potential regularization strategy. The water height and capillary potential are computed implicitly, while the momentum equation is updated through an upwind discretization associated with the numerical mass flux. We prove that the resulting method satisfies a discrete entropy inequality for the mechanical energy. A second-order extension is then obtained by using a Crank-Nicolson discretization of the implicit terms. The resulting formulation uses a single nonlinear implicit stage per time step, thereby avoiding the multiple implicit stages associated with multistage Runge-Kutta time discretizations. Finally, we introduce a congestion constraint to model a roof above the flow. A contact-angle treatment is imposed at the transition between free-surface and congested regions. Several numerical experiments are presented to assess the accuracy of the schemes, their ability to capture a traveling wave solution, and the behavior of the proposed congested model in a dynamic-waterline configuration.

title: Low-density parity-check coding for indoor LiFi: impairment-driven code design, current evidence, and open problems
abstractText: Light fidelity (LiFi) operates over an intensity-modulated direct-detection channel whose impairments differ structurally from those of radio links: signals must be real and non-negative, noise is partly signal-dependent, the transmitter doubles as a luminaire and is, therefore, constrained in the run-length statistics of its output, and channel gain depends strongly on receiver position and orientation. Forward error correction for LiFi has, nonetheless, largely been inherited from radio standards rather than designed against these impairments. This review organizes the field around an impairment-to-code-property mapping: for each distinct optical impairment we identify the LDPC design lever, we find that protograph constructions have been optimized directly against optical channel statistics in several works, whereas quasi-cyclic constructions – the family with the most mature hardware support and the most direct girth control at short block length – remain almost wholly unevaluated over optical wireless channels, with a single recent exception in free-space optics. We further find that carrierless amplitude and phase modulation, despite being motivated by severe bandwidth limitation, has no published LDPC-coded evaluation. We close with open problems ordered by the same impairment map, of which quasi-cyclic construction under LiFi short-block frame constraints and coded CAP transmission are the most immediately actionable.

title: Uncovering themes in user reviews of a smart urban mobility application with BERTopic: a data-driven framework for service improvement
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to identify the thematic structure of long-form user feedback on a smart urban mobility application in Istanbul by analyzing user reviews and to translate these themes into actionable insights for service improvement. Design/methodology/approach A total of 10,000 user reviews of the Istanbulkart – Dijital Hesabim application, posted on the Google Play Store between June 2019 and April 2025, were analyzed using BERTopic, which combines transformer-based contextual embeddings with density-based clustering and a class-based TF-IDF representation. The topics were then consolidated into themes and interpreted qualitatively. Findings The model extracted 40 topics, consolidated into six themes: transportation card integration issues, technical performance and application stability, payment systems and financial transactions, authentication and security, identity verification and account recovery, and general satisfaction and criticism. Transportation card integration problems formed the largest topic (13.21% of the 5,406 classified reviews), indicating that the transition between physical and digital systems remains the most salient difficulty in these reviews. Research limitations/implications The corpus, in which dissatisfied users are over-represented, comprises long-form Android reviews of a single application, so the findings describe what these users report and have limited generalizability. Irony and emojis remain difficult to interpret. Practical implications Findings from long-form reviews give local authorities and developers a starting point for prioritizing improvements in application stability, authentication and card integration. Originality/value The study shows that topic share alone is a misleading basis for prioritization, since the most frequent theme is the least severely rated and the problem profile shifts markedly across application versions.

title: Heparin-Decorated Hydrogel Microspheres Enable Bioactive Islet Encapsulation and Sustained Glycemic Control in Diabetic Mice
abstractText: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is characterized by immune-mediated β-cell destruction and chronic insulin deficiency. Pancreatic islet transplantation offers a promising approach to restore endogenous insulin production; however, the early post-transplantation period remains a critical barrier to successful graft function, as rapid protein adsorption, coagulation activation, and inflammatory cell recruitment at the material interface can compromise encapsulated islet viability. Here, we develop heparin-decorated hydrogel microcapsules to regulate early material-host interactions and improve the performance of islet encapsulation. Heparin was incorporated into a poly-l-lysine-modified gelatin (PLL-GEL) network through electrostatic complexation, where PLL was covalently anchored onto gelatin via transglutaminase-mediated cross-linking, and subsequently integrated with sodium alginate microcapsules fabricated by electrospraying and calcium-mediated ionic gelation. The resulting microcapsules exhibited uniform morphology, structural stability, and favorable physicochemical properties. Heparin incorporation reduced fibrinogen adsorption, prolonged coagulation times, and decreased macrophage adhesion, indicating improved early hemocompatibility and reduced material-induced cellular interactions. Furthermore, macrophages exposed to heparin-containing microcapsules showed altered immune-related transcriptional responses, suggesting regulation of early host responses. Encapsulated islets maintained high viability and glucose-responsive insulin secretion in vitro. Following intraperitoneal transplantation into diabetic mice, heparin-decorated microcapsules improved graft retention and sustained glycemic control over 30 days. Collectively, this study presents a functional material strategy for optimizing the early-stage compatibility of hydrogel microcapsules in islet transplantation.

title: Long-run linkages and parameter instability in the gold–silver relationship, 2010–2025
abstractText: Purpose The study aims to obtain evidence on the long-run linkages and possible instabilities in the gold–silver price relationship using daily futures prices over the period from January 4, 2010 to November 28, 2025. Design/methodology/approach This paper examines the gold–silver price relationship using various methods including unit root and standard cointegration tests, endogenous structural break test (the pruned exact linear time algorithm and the Bai–Perron endogenous break test), fractional integration and cointegration. Findings A break is detected in late 2017. Standard cointegration tests fail to find a stable long-run equilibrium over the full sample and the prebreak subsample, while one is found in the postbreak subsample. Furthermore, the Local Whittle fractional integration method provides evidence of a high degree of persistence consistent with long-memory dynamics. The fractionally cointegrated vector autoregressive results are broadly consistent with the previous findings: full-sample evidence for cointegration remains limited, while the postbreak period shows stronger, though still inconclusive, evidence of error correction and long-run co-movement between gold and silver. The results are shown to be robust across frequencies. Originality/value This study makes an original contribution by using a range of state-of-the-art econometric methods to shed new light on the gold-silver relationship, the focus being on the most recent decades characterized by various exogenous shocks and possible instabilities.

title: Nurses' Attitudes Toward ANCC NCPD Accreditation and the Association With Perceived Value, Satisfaction, Confidence, and Educational Quality
abstractText: BACKGROUND: American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC) Nursing Continuing Professional Development (NCPD) accreditation provides a framework for continuing education (CE) grounded in evidence-based standards. Despite widespread use of ANCC NCPD accreditation, little research has examined how nurses' attitudes toward accreditation relate to key CE outcomes. Guided by Donabedian's model, Kirkpatrick's evaluation framework, and expectancy-value theory, this study examined nurses' attitudes toward accredited CE and the association with perceived value, satisfaction, confidence, and educational quality. METHOD: This quantitative correlational design explored relationships between attitudes toward ANCC-accredited CE and perceived value, satisfaction with CE, professional confidence, and educational quality. Licensed nurses completed a structured survey. Data analysis included descriptive statistics and Spearman correlations. RESULTS: Nurses reported positive attitudes toward accreditation. Significant positive correlations indicated that more positive attitudes were associated with higher perceived value, greater satisfaction, increased confidence, and enhanced perceptions of educational quality. CONCLUSION: Nurses' attitudes toward accreditation influence key CE outcomes, aligning with theoretical expectations regarding structure, learner reaction, and motivation. Accreditation has a role in supporting high-quality CE and advancing professional development.

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of a Peer Growth Group Intervention to Enhance Psychological Resilience in Early Career Nurses: A Randomized Controlled Trial
abstractText: Background: Early career nurses face significant occupational pressures and risks, making psychological resilience critical for effective management of workplace stress. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a theory-driven resilience-building intervention for early career nurses. Method: This study adopted a two-arm, 1:1 pilot randomized controlled trial design to evaluate the effectiveness of a bi-weekly, eight-session resilience intervention for early career nurses. Outcome was measured by the Nurse Resilience Scale, Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale, and general self-efficacy scale. Results: Twenty-seven nurses were randomly assigned to an intervention group ( n = 13) or a wait-list control group ( n = 14). The intervention significantly improved overall nurse resilience ( p = .016), and no significant between-group differences were found in self-efficacy (overall p = .98). Conclusion: The findings demonstrate that a structured, theory-driven intervention can effectively enhance resilience among early career nurses, which highlights the intervention's practical utility in fostering adaptive coping mechanisms.

title: An individualised approach to autism and criminal intent
abstractText: Purpose This paper aims to examine how autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is treated in forensic evaluations of criminal intent and proposes an individualised, functional standard for weighing ASD-related evidence. Design/methodology/approach The paper synthesises recent empirical literature on ASD and social cognition, emotional regulation, adaptive functioning, suggestibility and threat perception and examines Virginia’s evidentiary statute on ASD and specific intent as an illustration of an individualised functional legal framework. Findings Diagnosis alone provides insufficient information about criminal intent. Autism-related differences in social cognition, emotional regulation and adaptive functioning are heterogeneous and only loosely tied to diagnostic status, so forensic relevance depends on documented, individualised impairment rather than the presence of an ASD diagnosis. Originality/value The paper integrates findings on theory of mind and criminal-intent recognition and on adaptive functioning in forensic ASD samples, with Virginia’s statutory framework to propose an individualised functional approach evaluators can apply directly to casework.

title: Normalizing sustainable fashion innovations: environmental messages and dynamic norms in circular fashion adoption
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to investigate whether informational messages promote interest in fashion products made from agri-food waste and whether dynamic norm cues strengthen persuasion in a trend-sensitive, ambiguous market. Design/methodology/approach Overall, 183 Italian adults were randomly assigned to control, environmental message or environmental plus dynamic norm message conditions. Participants reported purchasing intention and willingness to pay a premium price. Pro-environmental self-identity and identification with sustainable fashion consumers were tested as moderators. Findings Only the combined environmental and dynamic norm message increased purchasing intention, whereas neither message affected willingness to pay, suggesting a distinction between motivational interest and financial commitment. Exploratory analyses suggested that the environmental message was more effective among participants with low identification with sustainable fashion consumers. Pro-environmental self-identity did not moderate message effects. Research limitations/implications Self-reported intentions and a highly educated Italian sample limit generalisability. Future studies should use behavioural measures, field experiments, longitudinal designs and diverse samples to test whether initial openness persists and translates into purchasing and price acceptance. Practical implications Environmental messages combined with dynamic norm cues can increase initial interest in agri-food waste fashion, but the promotional strategy did not increase willingness to pay, highlighting the importance of product, price and audience segmentation. Originality/value The study shows that integrating dynamic norm cues into environmental appeals can increase initial openness toward novel sustainable fashion products, while purchasing intention and willingness to pay represent distinct outcomes for intervention design.

title: Disentangling the Etiology of Agitation and Hallucinations: A Case of Seronegative Autoimmune Encephalitis, Epilepsy, and Neurodevelopmental Comorbidity in an Adolescent
Gender in entrepreneurship education: a bibliometric analysis and research agenda
abstractText: Purpose This study maps the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of research on gender in entrepreneurship education (EE) and examines how existing studies report and explain gender differences in EE effectiveness, identifying implications for programme design and future research. Design/methodology/approach A bibliometric analysis of 590 Scopus-indexed documents (2005–2026) was conducted using VOSviewer and Biblioshiny to examine keyword co-occurrence, citation networks and thematic evolution. Additionally, 20 highly cited studies reporting gender differences in EE effects were coded according to the direction of these differences and the explanations provided. A broader dataset of 6,030 EE publications served as a comparative baseline. Findings The literature predominantly focuses on entrepreneurial intention and self-efficacy, while structural and contextual perspectives remain less developed. Among the 20 studies, EE effects were larger for women in seven, larger for men in six, no significant gender differences were found in two and mixed results were reported in five. Nine studies provided no explanation, while five offered individual-level explanations, five contextual explanations and only one integrated both perspectives. Digital and AI-related research also remains limited, representing approximately half the relative share of the broader EE literature. Originality/value This study reveals a disconnect between established individual and structural perspectives and their limited integration in explaining gender differences in EE effectiveness. It highlights the need for gender-disaggregated evaluations and theoretically grounded explanations of how and for whom EE works.

title: How boards judge CEO readiness: the HR leadership paradox
abstractText: Purpose Written for The Practice of Making Decisions section of Management Decision, this article examines how boards judge chief executive officer (CEO) readiness when the available evidence differs across candidates. The HR leadership paradox illustrates this problem. Design/methodology/approach The framework combines published empirical research on succession and executive evaluation with signaling and leadership-recognition theory. A fictional composite case illustrates the six-step routine. No primary empirical data are collected, and the routine has not been empirically validated. Findings A board should first agree on what the future role requires before comparing candidates. It should then ask whether the evidence is relevant, how clearly it shows each candidate's contribution and whether similar contributions are judged consistently. When important questions remain unresolved and a candidate has not met a requirement that must be satisfied before the vote, the board must not appoint the candidate on the available evidence. Practical implications A record documents candidates' decisions, alternative explanations, evidence that challenges initial judgments and the board's confidence in its conclusions. Once all essential requirements are met, the board must explain why remaining risks are acceptable and how it will monitor and respond to them. Originality/value The article offers a six-step decision routine for assessing candidates with different career records. For each requirement, the board records demonstrated capability, adverse evidence, reducible uncertainty and residual uncertainty, then assesses whether the evidence meets the standards agreed upon before discussing candidates. Measures to manage remaining risks cannot replace evidence needed to meet an essential requirement.

title: The pre-activation ecotone: a conceptual framework for unscheduled care and the emerging role of mobile integrated healthcare
abstractText: Purpose To define the “pre-activation ecotone” as a conceptual framework for unscheduled care, representing the interval between recognition of a health need and formal health system entry, and to examine its implications for care delivery design, patient decision-making, and system integration. Design/methodology/approach A targeted narrative synthesis of literature spanning ecology, emergency medicine, health services research, and public health. Sources were identified through targeted database searches (PubMed, Scopus), gray literature review, and reference chaining, with emphasis on studies and models addressing unscheduled care access, system design, and cross-sector coordination. Because the manuscript is intended as a conceptual framework rather than a formal review of all available evidence, studies were not systematically appraised or graded. Findings In the United States, current approaches to unscheduled care prioritize expansion of episodic access points, with limited attention to the pre-engagement setting where patient-driven decisions under uncertainty often lead to emergency system activation. Evidence from emergency medical services and health services research identifies this interval as functionally distinct yet structurally underdeveloped. Mobile integrated healthcare is emerging within this space, demonstrating feasibility in addressing unmet care needs and reducing avoidable utilization of traditional episodic-care venues in selected populations. The pre-activation ecotone provides a unifying construct to interpret opportunities to minimize avoidable care escalation and to guide healthcare system-level alignment. Practical implications Supports development of interventions targeting early assessment, navigation, and cross-sector coordination prior to emergency system entry. Originality/value Introduces a novel systems-level framework that reconceptualizes unscheduled care as a design problem centered on the interface between longitudinal and episodic care, offering a foundation for innovation in care coordination, access, and integration.

title: Modelling fusing and detailing agent effects on temperature and crystallinity in multi-jet fusion of polypropylene: a numerical and analytical sensitivity study
abstractText: Purpose Multi Jet Fusion (MJF) is an effective additive manufacturing method for the high-throughput production of thermoplastic components; however, the coupled thermal effects of preheating and liquid agents remain incompletely understood, particularly for polypropylene. This study aims to develop a numerical simulation that explicitly incorporates fusing and detailing agents to predict process temperature evolution and the resulting crystallinity in MJF-fabricated polypropylene. Design/methodology/approach A physics-based analytical–numerical framework was established by integrating an enthalpy-based crystallinity model with temperature-dependent thermophysical properties into an MJF thermal simulation that accounts for agent-induced absorption effects. Model predictions were validated against differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) measurements obtained from printed specimens. Preheat temperature and agent absorptivity were systematically varied, and multivariate statistical analysis was used to quantify the significance and interaction of these parameters on thermal and crystallinity outcomes. Findings The simulation captures the localised thermal modulation introduced by liquid agents: increasing the fusing agent absorption ratio substantially elevates local peak temperatures, reproducing behaviour consistent with commercial agent functionality. Multivariate analysis confirms that both preheat temperature and absorptivity are statistically significant drivers of maximum agent-region temperatures and crystallinity-related responses, with predictive performance reaching up to 98% accuracy across the tested design space. Originality/value This work reports the first MJF simulation that jointly models the combined effects of fusing and detailing agents for polymer parts, validated by DSC-based crystallinity measurements. The proposed framework provides a mechanistic, transferable tool for process optimisation and microstructure control in MJF polypropylene, enabling parameter-driven tuning of thermal history and crystallinity for improved part performance.

title: Update in alternative donor strategies in heart and lung transplantation
abstractText: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Alternative donor strategies in cardiothoracic transplantation are becoming routine. This review covers recent developments and their implications for the anesthesiologist. RECENT FINDINGS: Donor scarcity is a principal constraint on heart and lung transplantation. Donation after circulatory death (DCD) and the adoption of machine preservation have reshaped the donor pool. This review covers literature comparing thoracoabdominal normothermic regional perfusion with direct procurement and preservation, warm ischemic thresholds and their relationship to primary graft dysfunction, normothermic and hypothermic ex-situ perfusion, 10 °C static cold storage, and ex-vivo lung perfusion, and discusses the ethics of DCD. Extended-criteria and hepatitis C virus-viremic donors are now used routinely, and cardiac xenotransplantation is entering clinical study. Each advance alters graft physiology at reperfusion and the timing of perioperative services. Research into cardiac xenotransplantation is ongoing. SUMMARY: These strategies enlarge the donor pool and introduce novel graft physiological concerns, as well as ethical concerns, for the anesthesiologist.

title: Beyond cognitive benefits: the emotional costs of task and process conflict for innovative work behavior
abstractText: Purpose Drawing on affective events theory and the contingency model of conflict, this study aims to examine how task and process conflicts relate to innovative work behavior, focusing on the mediating role of emotional exhaustion and the moderating role of time pressure. Design/methodology/approach This study used Mplus 8.11 with robust maximum likelihood estimation and bootstrap procedures to analyze data from a three-wave time-lagged survey of 226 employees in Pakistan’s service sector. Findings The findings revealed that both process and task conflicts were positively associated with emotional exhaustion, which was negatively associated with innovative work behavior. Additionally, emotional exhaustion partially mediated the relationships between both process and task conflicts and innovative work behavior. Furthermore, time pressure strengthened the positive relationship between process conflict and emotional exhaustion, as well as the indirect relationship between process conflict and innovative work behavior via emotional exhaustion. However, the corresponding moderating effects for task conflict were not supported. Originality/value This study advances understanding of the emotional consequences of task and process conflicts for innovative work behavior by identifying emotional exhaustion as an underlying mechanism and time pressure as a contextual factor that exacerbates the adverse effect of process conflict.
